News.title: Football fans honour two brave cops killed in A66 wrong-way crash with poignant tribute at Middlesbrough FC home game
News.content:
COP TRIBUTE Football fans honour two brave cops killed in A66 wrong-way crash with poignant tribute at Middlesbrough FC home game

FOOTBALL fans have paid their respects to the two police officers killed in a horror wrong-way crash on the A66 last Saturday.

Middlesbrough FC asked supporters to pay tribute to Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough before their 12.30pm home game against West Bromwich Albion today.



The match kicked off at 12.30pm with a “show of support” for the two officers seen at 12.29pm.

The King has also written to the two officers’ families to express his condolences, the Mirror reported.



Middlesbrough FC said in a statement: “Immediately before kick-off, we’re asking supporters to join us in paying respects to Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough, the two Cleveland police officers who tragically lost their lives in the line of duty last weekend.

“We are also showing our appreciation for the dedication and hard work of both men, and to Cleveland police force in protecting and supporting our local community.

“The commitment shown by officers and staff, often in challenging and demanding circumstances, plays a vital role in keeping residents safe and helping people feel secure in their homes, neighbourhoods and local areas.”

A stadium announcement ahead of the tribute said: “Middlesbrough Football Club and its supporters wish to pay their respects to PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, the two brave Cleveland Police officers who gave their lives in the line of duty.”



Five young men, who were riding in the stolen VW Passat, also sadly lost their lives in the fatal collision.

Cole Worthy, 17; Theo Rae, 17; Makai Saddington, 18; and 23-year-olds Michael Cahill and Jakub Matusiak had all previously been convicted of various crimes by police.

Following the tragic collision Cleveland Police said its officers had been tackling alleged organised crime in Middlesbrough.

Last night, the force confirmed some 24 people had been arrested in the crackdown as chaos unfolded in the area in the wake of the fatal collision.

Hundreds of police officers from across Britain have been deployed to Middlesbrough in a bid to crackdown on the violence and prevent further retaliation – making a total of 24 arrests.



The chaos kicked off when a home belonging to Gye Worthy, was rammed twice by a Volvo SUV in the early hours of Saturday morning last week.

Minutes later, Gye’s 17-year-old son Cole and four of his friends raced through the streets in a Volkswagen Passat, allegedly pursuing the Volvo.

There is no indication that Gye was involved in any criminal activity.



As the Passat joined the A66 – on the wrong side of the road – cops called off the chase.

But just 10 seconds later, at 3.39am, the car ploughed into another marked armed-response vehicle carrying two officers.

All five occupants of the Passat and both of the officers were pronounced dead at the scene.

Chaos followed and some 17 people were arrested by Tuesday in connection with the fatal smash – 14 men and three women, aged between 16 and 61.

And within hours five more people were arrested, with help from the National Crime Agency and North East Regional Organised Crime Unit.



The force said they were a boy aged 16, an 18-year-old and a man of 21, all on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group, a 55-year-old on suspicion of assisting an offender and a 23-year-old on suspicion of making threats to kill.

In the days that followed, officers said four more men, aged 35, 25, 40 and 21, were being held on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life.

The arrests relate to a vehicle crashing into a house in Steele Crescent, Middlesbrough, on Thursday morning.

They were also being questioned over alleged arson after a caravan was set alight in Atlee Road on Wednesday morning, and a drugs offence.

And, on Friday, detectives confirmed they were not linking a house fire which killed a seven-year-old girl and her aunt to the A66 crash.



Natalie McDonald, 34, and her niece, Valentina Foster, died while four other people were injured in the blaze on Wednesday morning.

Two men, aged 23 and 31, remain in custody on suspicion of murder after the tragic inferno.

A 39-year-old man was also knifed amid the turmoil as Cleveland cops brought in reinforcements to get a lid on the chaos, all within a few miles.



Amid the crackdown and flurry of arrests, three men have subsequently been charged with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, possession with intent to supply class A and class B drugs and possession of criminal property.

Gang’s VW Passat, with cloned plates, is seen pursued by police. 3.39am: It joins the A66 in the wrong direction. Cops abort chase. Ten ­seconds later it collides head-on with a police armed response vehicle. PC Matthew Blades, PC Tom Clough and the five Passat occupants are killed.

The Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) for Cleveland Matt Storey said: “My thoughts remain with the family, friends and colleagues of Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough.

“They will be remembered as selfless, professional and courageous police officers, dedicated to serving their communities.

“I also offer my sincere condolences to everyone affected by the horrific fire in Grangetown, which sadly resulted in the deaths of two people.

“I have reiterated my request for a better, long-term, funding deal to enhance Cleveland’s response to serious and organised crime.

“People in Cleveland have the right to live without the fear of crime and I understand the concern, anger and grief recent events have caused.

“I want to assure them that I will continue to fight for the funding needed to improve Cleveland Police’s ability to prevent crime, bring offenders to justice and keep our communities safe.”

News.title: I was grieving my gentle giant husband’s suicide… then I saw his hanged body in police email, apology only made it worse
News.content:
LEAH Clarke opened the police email – there was a link and a warning that the contents could be “distressing”.

Confused, she clicked into it and was horrified to find footage of officers trudging through the woods. She knew what was coming but was unable to look away.





Leah’s partner of three years Ollie Roberts was found hanged in the woods having taken his own life, and the horror bodycam footage showed the moment officers discovered his body.

The mum-of-two, 25, from Derby, has been left traumatised and is now taking legal action against the under-fire force, which has also faced criticism for its failure to escalate its search for Ollie in the hours before he died.

The young dad’s body was found in the Middle Chine area of Bournemouth on January 28 2024 – hours after FaceTiming Leah threatening to take his own life.

A legal adviser for Dorset Police accidentally sent Leah an email on March 10 2026, which appears to have been sent to multiple recipients ahead of Ollie’s inquest. It included a link to sensitive footage of his body being discovered.

Leah told The Sun she couldn’t believe her eyes when she opened the link.

“I thought at the time it’s just weird but I must be entitled to it because I’m his wife,” she said. “I just thought, what a weird video.”





She continued: “When the video starts, they’re in the woods, and I kind of knew what we were coming to.

“It might sound a bit sick, but I couldn’t look away… they just found him, he was just there.”

Seen by The Sun, the email states: “The contents may be distressing to some.”

However, the following day, the same adviser sent a frantic follow up email saying the footage had been “sent to you in error”, advising Leah to “immediately and permanently” delete it “without viewing the attachment”.

They asked Leah to respond ASAP, adding: “Apologies for the oversight.”

In a separate email, they went on to say: “The error was completely mine.

“I misunderstood the instructions that I was given in terms of who to disclose the footage to.

“It should not have happened. I make no excuse for it.”



Leah told The Sun: “I was like, hang on, that’s really traumatising what you’ve sent me. It’s not okay.

“You’d triple check who you’re sending it to – before you press send you’d be making sure you knew who exactly was going to see it.”

She said the apologies were “too little too late” and, knowing she may need the footage and emails for a future complaint, refused to delete anything.

A legal claim letter sent to Dorset Police on Leah’s behalf, and seen by The Sun, states: “Seeing this footage has caused our client to suffer significant levels of distress and has caused her to suffer psychiatric injury.”

It goes on to allege a failure in duty of care, carelessness and negligence, adding: “Sent to her was footage of her late husband’s body being discovered, which would be incredibly distressing for any widow to see.”

Leah and Ollie had been together for more than three years when he died and share a son, Reuben, now three.

You're Not Alone EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

Leah said Ollie had video called her as he threatened to take his own life.

“Things were messy,” she said, with the pair having temporarily separated at the time of Ollie’s death.



At the age of 20, Leah had moved from Derby to Bournemouth and began working at a mental health facility, where she met Ollie.

They began dating and married two years later, before welcoming their son and eventually moving to Derby, allowing Leah to return to her hometown.

However, Ollie’s mental health deteriorated and he went missing on a number of occasions in the lead up to his death.

Leah said: “We tried to get him help.”

Police were alerted after the FaceTime call, as well as a worrying photo Ollie sent to Leah.

But he was not immediately graded as “high risk” despite a recommendation from the 999 call handler, his inquest heard in May this year.

It meant his mobile phone data couldn’t be used to trace him, and he was found dead the following day, January 28 2024, at around 2.40pm.

A jury at Bournemouth Coroner’s Court returned a narrative verdict, saying there were missed opportunities, and a failure to assess the risk contributed to Ollie’s death.

They also ruled there had been “insufficient and delayed responses” by the force.

Leah said: “Ollie was just this silly loveable gentle giant who lost his way.



“We love him and miss him every single day. He took a lot of tears with him the night he passed away.

“This was not the ending anybody wanted and I’m sorry he thought Heaven needed him more than we did.”

In relation to Leah’s legal claim, Dorset Police said: “We are aware of a legal claim against the Force, but as that is currently following due process, it would be inappropriate to comment on it at this time.”

In response to the inquest, Chief Superintendent Heather Dixey, of Dorset Police, said: “Foremost, I would like to express my condolences to the family of Oliver Roberts. Our thoughts remain with them.

“Dorset Police has fully engaged and cooperated with the coronial process and recognised the HM Coroner’s findings.

“As an organisation, we are focused on continually learning to improve our service to the public across all policing areas and we always look to strengthen our processes to ensure we serve the public as they would expect us to.”

News.title: Lindsay Clancy neighbors say meds turned mom into a ‘ZOMBIE’ in ‘self-imposed prison’ & hope for not-guilty verdict
News.content:
LINDSAY Clancy’s neighbors and residents close to where she strangled her three young children to death believe meds turned the depressed mom into a ‘zombie’ and feel she should be sent to a psychiatric hospital.

Clancy, 36, has pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility to the 2023 murders which shook the town of Duxbury, Massachusetts.



The jury has been deliberating since Thursday afternoon following a five-week blockbuster trial in which her mental state at the time of the killings has been at the heart of the case.

The U.S. Sun has been reporting from the trial at Plymouth Superior Court, where jurors heard weeks of emotional testimony about Clancy’s deteriorating mental health and the extensive list of medications she had been prescribed.





She strangled her children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan, with exercise bands and left them in the basement before throwing herself out of a bedroom window.

Prosecutors have that argued Clancy, who is now paralyzed, knew what she was doing when she carried out the murders on January 24, 2023.

Her defense, led by attorney Kevin Reddington, has argued she was suffering from severe mental illness and was hearing voices.

The closely watched trial has divided opinion, but residents who spoke to The U.S. Sun near the family’s home said they believe Clancy needs psychiatric treatment and not be sent to prison.



Local resident Eric McDonald spoke to The U.S. Sun outside the Kingsbury Club & Spa, minutes from the Clancy home, where Lindsay and ex-husband Patrick regularly took their children.

The kids were last at the club on January 17, 2023 – just one week before they were killed.

Eric said, “I think she should be institutionalized at a mental health facility and where she could get help she needs.

“She’s not going to get that in prison. She’s just going to get worse.

“It’s heartbreaking for the family. I can’t even imagine. And for her. I mean, she seems genuinely touched and upset.



“I’m sure the reality of it has had a chance to sink in by now. And I think that she’s a sad figure.

“I hope she goes to a mental institution because I think she has some serious issues, but allegedly she’s had them for a while and they were not being treated properly.

“I won’t say mistreated but not being treated properly. They just threw meds at her and hoped it would help and, you know, turn her into a zombie.”



Ruth Hearson, 81, lives opposite the Clancy family’s former Duxbury home, a large, traditional New England-style property set back from the road and surrounded by trees.

She was home when the murders happened between 5pm and 6pm and saw police arrive but only found out the heartbreaking circumstances days later.

Ruth told The U.S. Sun, “She obviously wasn’t in her right mind. That’s what I think.

“No one in their right mind kills their babies and jumps out a window on the second floor, thinks they’re gonna kill themselves.”

Asked how she feels about Clancy now facing life behind bars for murder, she said, “I feel bad. When you’re like that, you’re not guilty. Because it wasn’t you doing it.



“If you’re in a psychotic state, that’s what’s in control of you. Not your regular mind. Sorry, it isn’t.

“And she had all those drugs in her, that’s what was controlling her. I really believe that.”

Ruth believes Clancy should be treated in a hospital rather than sent to prison.

Clancy could receive psychiatric treatment even if convicted, but would remain under a criminal sentence.

If found not guilty due to lack of criminal responsibility, she could be committed to a hospital without receiving a prison sentence.



“She would get the care she needed,” Ruth said. “In the prison, you don’t really, especially in a wheelchair.

“She’s in her own living hell. I’m sorry. So putting her in prison… she’s already in her own prison.”

Ruth added, “I’m heartbroken for her because she doesn’t have her babies.”

Mark Shortt lives two doors down from Clancy’s old home, which sold in 2024, and believes she was let down by medical professionals.

Separate civil lawsuits over Clancy’s medical care are also ongoing, with both Lindsay and Patrick are suing medical providers who treated her before the killings.



The suits allege failures in her psychiatric diagnosis, treatment and medication management contributed to the deaths of Cora, Dawson and Callan.

The providers have denied wrongdoing.

The defense argued Clancy was psychotic and believed a voice had commanded her to kill the children, while prosecutors pointed to evidence they say showed planning and awareness, including sending Patrick out to pick up medication and takeout before the killings.

Neighbor Mark, 62, told The U.S. Sun, “People get prescribed a lot of medication in the United States.

“I can’t say that medically what happened as far as how they treated or mistreated or maltreated her. But I will say that whatever they did, it didn’t work.



“So was she let down? I’d have to say, yeah, well, certainly her three kids were.

“There’s nothing good that’s going to come out of it for her. She’s in [a] prison anyway.”

The mom-of-three was prescribed 13 different psychiatric drugs in the four months before the killings, including antidepressants Prozac and Zoloft, anti-anxiety drugs Valium, Klonopin and Ativan, antipsychotics Seroquel and Thorazine, and sleep aid Ambien.

Jurors heard Clancy herself had repeatedly complained about the impact of the medications, telling providers she felt “completely numb” and reporting intrusive thoughts she had never experienced before.

She also told a friend she felt “like a zombie,” while a note on her phone last modified the day before the killings said medication had “stole[n] me from my own body.”



Valerie Franks, who lives in Duxbury part time, told The U.S. Sun she was stunned by the number of medications prescribed to Clancy.

Valerie said, “Why aren’t these doctors talking to each other? Why aren’t they looking at the records? Why are they just dishing out all of these [anti] psychotics? I listened a little bit to the doctors [in the trial].

“How can one person be sane with all that going into their body?”

Asked if she thinks she should be sent to prison, Valerie said, “Personally, I think she’ll be better off in a hospital.”

But she believes no matter where she ends up, she is in her own self-imposed prison.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She’s going to be a mental wreck anywhere she goes, whether she’s in a hospital or whether she’s in a prison, she’ll never be the same. Look at her. Look at her body. Look at her mind. She’ll never be the same.

“I wish the best for her. How can you be a sane woman when you’ve killed your three children and hurt yourself to the point where you’re crippled?”

News.title: Man fighting for life after falling from balcony at block of flats – as man in 20s arrested
News.content:
PLUNGE HORROR Man fighting for life after falling from balcony at block of flats – as man in 20s arrested



A MAN is fighting for his life after falling from a balcony, as a man in his 20s is arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

Cops were scrambled to Salford, Greater Manchester, just after midnight yesterday, after receiving reports that a man had plunged to the ground from a block of flats.



He was rushed to hospital with life threatening injuries, where he remains in a critical condition.

Police have since arrested a man in his 20s on suspicion of attempted murder, he remains in police custody for questioning.



Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it had referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

Officers had earlier contact with the parties involved in the horror, the force said.

A probe into the incident remains ongoing, with GMP asking anyone with any information that may assist their investigation to come forward.

The force said the harrowing incident is believed to be an isolated event with no further risk posed to the public.

Chief Inspector Lee Gridley from GMP’s Salford district, said: “A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, and he is currently being questioned in custody.

“Our officers are working at pace to establish the full circumstances, and a scene will remain in place whilst the investigation continues.



“We understand that incidents of this nature may cause concern within the community; however, we believe this is an isolated incident and that there is no wider risk to the public.

“We would like to hear from anyone who may have information that can assist us.

“Anyone that was in the Liverpool Street area of Salford around the time of this incident, or who has mobile phone, CCTV, Ring doorbell, and dashcam footage, can contact police on 101 and quote log 8 of 29/08/2026.

“Alternatively contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Is this cornered Putin’s last roll of the dice? Chilling threat to UK, 300,000-troop ‘hammer blow’ & shadow Nato attacks
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin is plotting a terrifying final gambit to crush Ukraine as the tyrant ramps up his blistering threats towards the UK.

As tensions between Moscow and Europe reach boiling point, the dictator is preparing to unleash a 300,000-troop “hammer blow” and crank up sabotage attacks on Nato.



Putin’s last roll of the dice could be an aggressive expansion of electronic warfare on a scale the West has never seen before.

Sabotage attacks on European GPS signals “would cause instant massive disruption and chaos”, Russian military expert Keir Giles told The Sun.



The threat of intensified asymmetric warfare on Nato comes as Putin is pushed closer to his wit’s end.

Ukraine‘s stunning strikes on key Russian targets have wreaked havoc for ordinary people – crippling fuel supplies and sparking energy blackouts over the summer.

Putin’s shadow warfare campaign could be coupled with a massive conscription of Russian troops to help punch through Ukraine‘s sturdy frontline.

Volodymyr Zelensky has said Putin is planning to draft over 300,000 new recruits to help pummel Ukraine’s defences and take the rest of Donetsk.

Fully capturing the rest of Donetsk has become a key target for Russia due to the Fortress Belt – a 50km-wide defensive line of cities which is vital to pushing enemies back.

A new conscription would be a “hammer blow of extra forces” to rejuvenate Moscow’s barbaric invasion efforts, Russia expert Mark Galeotti told The Sun.



But as Putin looks to up the ante on Nato nations, he will likely rely on one of his tried and tested methods of sparking chaos in Europe – drones.

A string of drone plots have already paralysed major airports – including a terrifying ordeal in Leipzig earlier this month which sparked panic as an explosive-laden UAV was discovered next to a fleet of planes.

It came after several packages burst into flames at warehouses in Birmingham and across Europe in 2024 having been delivered by jets.



The chilling operations are “a really cost effective way of disrupting our lives”, Galeotti said.

Europe’s increasing iron-clad commitment to Kyiv could sink Russia to new lows if it deems the strengthening partnership as a real threat.

On Monday, Andy Burnham handed Kyiv the blueprints to long-range Storm-hadow missiles to help continue Ukraine‘s campaign of strikes on key Russian targets.

Russia hit back with a furious response and issued a chilling threat to strike British military targets.

Kremlin cronies accused the UK, France and Germany of “playing with fire” and said Britain was actively “participating” in the war.



Putin mouthpiece Dmitry Peskov blasted Britain for “adding fuel to the fire”.

But Burnham hit back and said: “Who started the fire? That’s the question, isn’t it?”

This war of words from Russia is designed to sound “scary but ambiguous”, Galeotti said.



International security expert Elisabeth Braw said Europe’s growing united front against Russia could force Putin’s hand and cause a never-before-seen surge in shadow warfare attacks.

She told The Sun: “We’re likely to see more attacks on logistics hubs… but also other airports and railways.”

Putin is plotting riskier gambles to push the boundaries of their shadow warfare campaign to the limit, Giles said.



Some of these have already been “indistinguishable from warlike acts”, he said.

The brazen dictator wants to see how far he can stretch Europe without getting a significant blowback.

And there is one method that Moscow has surprisingly not tested yet – a massive GPS jamming surge.

It could cripple Europe if orchestrated effectively and leave Nato members frozen during periods of crisis.

“We should be watching for the expansion of Russia’s electronic warfare, what’s usually referred to as GPS jamming,” Giles said.



The disruption would be “enormous”, he warned.

He added: “That would cause instant massive disruption and chaos, and it’s a bit of a surprise we haven’t seen Russia testing that yet,” he said.

Putin’s shadow warfare could turn deadly on a dime – and it’s only down to pure luck that civilian casualties in Europe have been limited.

During the Leipzig drone sighting early in August, a second UAV is believed to have struck an incoming jet, forcing it to divert.

Just days later, another bomb-laden device was found just west of the airport, along with what appeared to be some sort of antenna strapped to a tree.



Putin has “no reservations about targeting civilian installations”, Braw said.

Flying a drone rigged with explosives into an airport demonstrates how Putin is comfortable killing innocent civilians.

She added: “Russia is willing to take such casualty risks.”

Russia’s increasing shadow attacks on Europe are just another test for Nato allies on how they can respond to Putin’s growing aggression.

Moscow will also want to make sure Kyiv’s landmark technological win from the Storm Shadow plans is stamped out.



Russia expert Anna Matveeva told The Sun Russia will be looking to “degrade Ukrainian industrial and energy capacity”.

The Kremlin will be looking to put their foot on Ukraine’s neck this winter to stop the production of key weapons.

“I think the plan is to try to destroy Ukraine’s industrial and energy capabilities,” Matveeva said.

It comes amid fears Putin is gearing up for a terrifying test of his perilous nuclear-powered “Flying Chernobyl” super weapon.

An influx of aircraft converging in the Arctic has sparked concerns the tyrant could fire the cruise missile which is fuelled by its own atomic reactor.



The Kremlin has long hailed the “invincible” Burevestnik missile which carries a nuclear warhead and reportedly boasts an “unlimited range”.

This means it could strike the UK should Putin ever decide to blitz the West, according to analysts.

News.title: Car rammings, fatal house fire & balaclava yobs… How aftermath of A66 crash has left tinderbox town fearing ‘gang war’
News.content:
A TINDERBOX town is caught up in a “gang turf war” – with a horror crash, multiple fires, house rammings and a stabbing leaving nine people dead across five days of carnage.

Hundreds of police officers from across Britain have been deployed to Middlesbrough this week in a bid to crackdown on the violence and prevent further retaliation – making a total of 24 arrests.



Five “joyrider” youths and two police officers died in a wrong-way smash on the A66, before schoolgirl Valentina Foster, seven, and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34, died in a house fire following a suspected arson attack.

A caravan and multiple vehicles were also torched and a 39-year-old man knifed as Cleveland cops brought in reinforcements to get a lid on the chaos, all within a few miles.



In the early hours of last Saturday morning, a stolen car rammed through the window of a terraced red-brick home in the Acklam area of Middlesbrough, triggering a police chase.

The house, belonging to Gye Worthy, was rammed twice by the Volvo SUV, which reversed into the front window at around 3am, causing extensive damage.



Minutes later, Gye’s 17-year-old son Cole and four of his friends raced through the streets in a Volkswagen Passat, allegedly pursuing the Volvo.

There is no indication that Gye was involved in any criminal activity.

A police patrol spotted the Passat after the plates activated an ANPR camera and initiated a high speed chase lasting nearly seven minutes.



Ring doorbell footage captured it being driven at speed at around 3.36am, with locals recalling the noise of the two cars.

As the Passat joined the A66 – on the wrong side of the road – cops called off the chase.

But just 10 seconds later, at 3.39am, the car ploughed into another marked armed-response vehicle carrying two officers.

The cop car was travelling on the correct side of the carriageway and had not been part of the high-speed chase, but was in the area to assist.

The five young men in the Passat and two officers – PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38 – died in the head-on smash at 3.39am.



A fundraiser, launched by Cleveland Police, said the two police officers “paid the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty“ and has already bypassed £1million.



Cops named the “joyriders” as Cole Worthy, 17, Michael Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.

The Volvo and Passat both had cloned number plates.

By Tuesday cops had arrested 17 people in connection with the fatal smash – 14 men and three women, aged between 16 and 61.

And within hours had also arrested five more people, with help from the National Crime Agency and North East Regional Organised Crime Unit.

The force said they were a boy aged 16, an 18-year-old and a man of 21, all on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group, a 55-year-old on suspicion of assisting an offender and a 23-year-old on suspicion of making threats to kill.



Investigators uncovered extensive social media and TikTok photos and videos, including of Saddington and Matusiak posing in cars and on motorcycles wearing black balaclavas, alongside anti-police rap lyrics.

Amid the crackdown and flurry of arrests, three men have subsequently been charged with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, possession with intent to supply class A and class B drugs and possession of criminal property.



Local council officials and residents have noted rival gangs in the town, allegedly involved in the rammings and chases, routinely use balaclavas to conceal their identities, reports The Daily Telegraph.

In the early hours of Wednesday, a house fire broke out on Birchington Avenue, around a mile away from the A66 crash in the Grangetown area.

Emergency services scrambled to the home at 5.23am, with firefighters tackling flames billowing from upstairs windows.

Seven-year-old Valentina Foster and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34, tragically died in the devastating blaze.



Natalie’s 15-year-old daughter and a friend had managed to escape through an upstairs window after kicking it out.

Cops said a woman, aged 48, was pulled from the fire and taken to hospital in Newcastle upon Tyne in a critical condition.

Three others were hurt, including one who jumped from an upstairs window.

Armed cops guarded the fire-hit property – though investigators say this is not believed to be connected to the A66 crash or wider turf war.



Two men, aged 23 and 31, were quickly arrested on suspicion of murder over the fire and remain in custody.

Minutes apart on the same morning, a caravan was set alight on nearby Atlee Road, also in Grangetown.

In the early hours of Thursday, just before 1am, another house wall was rammed by a car in Steele Crescent, South Bank.

Cleveland Police said the property was empty, adding: “It has not yet been confirmed whether this incident is linked to wider organised crime”.



Tactical officers subsequently intercepting a Mercedes on nearby Kingsley Road around 10.30pm that night.

Four men inside the vehicle were arrested on suspicion of arson for the caravan fire, criminal damage with intent to endanger life for the Steele Crescent ramming, and possession with intent to supply Class A drugs after a large quantity of drugs and £15,000 in cash were seized from the Mercedes.

Also at around midday on Thursday, a 39-year-old man was stabbed at an address in Eston, five miles from Middlesbrough – with no arrests yet made but police not ruling out a link with the ongoing turf war.

Middlesbrough MP Andy McDonald has slammed the unrest, calling the unsavoury events a “whole series of utterly appalling acts of wanton criminality”.

Previous convictions of four occupants Cole Worthy Use threatening abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress on 27 October 2024 and pleaded guilty Failing to surrender to custody on 14 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Common assault of a police officer on 27 April 2025 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Using a vehicle without insurance on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without reasonable consideration on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving using a mobile phone on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Jakub Matusiak Using a vehicle without insurance on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Makai Saddington Possession of a controlled class C drug on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Possession of a knife in a public place on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty 11 October 2025 three offences for assaulting a police officer and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Racially aggravated intentional harassment, alarm and distress on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Theo Rae 12 shoplifting offences between 21 October 2023 and 4 May 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences Three thefts from motor vehicle offences between 31 January 2024 and 25 September 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences One theft of vehicle on 13 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Possession of cannabis on 22 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking on 16 May 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking 2 January 2025 and pleaded guilty Conviction of an offence while a youth rehabilitation order is in force on 26 February 2025 and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 30 April 2026 and pleaded guilty Michael Robert Cahill No convictions

He added there was an “underlying cause” attracting young men into such behaviour.



Mr McDonald said: “They’re getting pulled into this appalling set of behaviours and engaging in this performative criminality without any regard for the consequences.”

Distraught friends and family paid tribute to Valentina and her auntie, with one relative saying: “Why you? You’re just a baby.”

Natalie’s mum Lisa Kirton told the BBC that Valentina, known as Tina, had been staying with the family over the school holidays.

Masked youths sparked outrage after setting off flares in the memory of Matusiak – one of the joyriders killed in the horror A66 crash.

The gathering took place on South Bank field on Monday, only a few hundred yards away from the site of the crash which claimed seven lives.



Several of Valentina’s relatives also posted tributes to Matusiak.

One lad, who we are not naming, shared a photo with Matusiak, 23, and wrote: “Till we meet again Tuz.” He also posted details of Matusiak’s September 4 funeral.

Meanwhile, an unauthorised memorial vigil in Haswell for Michael Cahill resulted in five vehicles being torched.

Four of the “joyriders” had previously appeared in court charged with a series of offences, Cleveland Police said.

The uncle of one of the A66 crash gang was jailed for previously driving on the wrong side of the same road during a similar 100mph police chase.



Aaron Saddington, 23, was locked up for 20 months in June after trying to shake off cops by speeding at oncoming traffic on the dual carriageway.

He was caged after pleading guilty to dangerous driving, driving while disqualified and without insurance, according to court documents obtained by The Sun.

The terrifying incident was almost identical to the head-on crash last Saturday.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander, Superintendent Emily Harrison, said: “We continue to work to establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened, but we are keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time.”

Of the 24 people arrested following the A66 crash and subsequent organised crime crack down, three people have been charged.



Kai Beattie, 19, has appeared at Teesside Magistrates’ Court charged with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cameron George, 26, faces charges of possessing Class A drugs with intent to supply and criminal property, and has been remanded in custody for Teesside Crown Court.

Kai Inico, 21, is charged with possession with intent to supply a Class B drug and has been released on conditional bail.

News.title: Cruel mum shoots dead 11-month-old son as ‘she didn’t want to give up custody’ & chillingly tells cops ‘it was worth it’
News.content:
'KILLER' MUM Cruel mum shoots dead 11-month-old son as ‘she didn’t want to give up custody’ & chillingly tells cops ‘it was worth it’

A MUM shot her 11-month old son dead, then told cops it was “worth it” if it meant the child’s dad could never see him.

Madeline Daly, 36, was convicted of killing Basil Stoner in a camper van as police closed in on her for kidnap.



She had snatched her baby and taken him across state lines to New Mexico, violating a court order, prosecutors said.

After shooting her son, Daly tried to turn the gun on herself but was subdued by officers.



Daly had taken the child to New Mexico.

When she was arrested, she told police she had been keeping her son “safe” from his dad and parental relatives.



Daly made unsubstantiated claims that Basil “would have been in danger and molested” with his father.

She claimed the child’s dad “never wanted anything to do with Basil, financially, physically, emotionally ever”.

Daly had taken Basil from Wyoming against a court order that had given the child’s dad emergency custody.

Dad Jake Stoner reported the child missing on November 28, telling investigators he had last seen his son two months earlier.



If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 or chat at thehotline.org.

Daly had disappeared, but when her warrant was flagged on a background check for a job she applied for, a business owner called the cops.

Police tracked her down to a bunkhouse and she ran into a nearby RV.

Cops were waiting for a warrant to search the vehicle when they heard a single gunshot.



They rushed in to find Basil had been shot dead.

Paramedics tried to save the child, but nothing could be done.

Daly told police she had kidnapped her son because “she was not going to allow her son to go back and forth from Nebraska to Wyoming twice a month”.

Detective Lt. Jason Jordan wrote in an affidavit: “Even if the rest of life is worthless she would do it again just so to make sure that the (family) didn’t touch him.”

It said: “When asked what went through her mind when she saw law enforcement walking up, she replied, ‘Jake can’t get Basil.”



The child’s dad was devastated, with his lawyer saying he had sat by the phone for hours waiting for news of Basil.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Madeline pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and is facing life in prison.

News.title: Festivalgoers brave heavy rain as strong winds & thunderstorms kick off bank holiday weekend with yellow warning issued
News.content:
FESTIVALGOERS across the UK are bracing for an onslaught of heavy rain as a new yellow thunderstorm warning has been declared by the Met Office.

It’s the third yellow thunderstorm warning of the week and threatens fans at events across the country.



This weekend is a bumper occasion for festival fans with Reading, Leeds, Victorious and Creamfields all on the same bank holiday.

But the forecast is looking grim with thundery showers and light winds sweeping across England.





Now the Met Office has put in place a yellow weather warning for thunderstorms with some flooding to property, transport disruption and power cuts expected.

Some areas may see 5-25mm of rain in just an hour along with hail and lightning.



The warning stretches from south-west England and parts of Wales across the Midlands to the east of England, and is in force from midday until 9pm on Saturday.

Heavy rain has already hammered Reading Festival with tents and fields covered in mud.

Artists have turned to performing in wellies and fans have fallen victim to the mud with several seen slipping over.



Parts of southern England and Wales will face gusty winds across the weekend which could challenge camping and travel plans on Saturday and Sunday.

Zones of wet weather are expected across the country which could be torrential and thundery, especially across southern England.

For northern parts of England, including Leeds Festival, it’s likely the showers might merge into longer spells of rain during the afternoon.

Sunday will start bright and dry except for some light showers in northern areas.

But a zone of heavy and thundery showers will sweep across the country from the west.



After downpours earlier this week, parts of the Midlands and northern England may face flash flooding.

South eastern areas of England look set to get lucky on Monday with less intense scattered showers compared to some heavy and thundery showers across the north.

News.title: Prisoners 'found with banned fat jabs and glow-up shots' behind bars
News.content:
Prisoners 'found with banned fat jabs and glow-up shots' behind bars

EXCLUSIVE: The Independent Monitoring Board said unregulated weight-loss injections and skin improvers were found inside HMP Thorn Cross near Warrington, Cheshire

View 2 Images Inspectors found the weight-loss injections and "glow-up" jabs at HMP Thorn Cross (Image: Alamy Stock Photo)

Prisoners are taking illicit fat-busting jabs and glow-up shots that improve skin radiance behind bars, a report reveals.

‌



Watchdogs have said weight loss jabs and skin improvers had been detected for the first time in one of the UK's jails. Steroids were also discovered HMP Thorn Cross near Warrington, Cheshire, according to the prison’s Independent Monitoring Board.

‌



The IMB revealed: “Finds this year have changed and have started to include unregulated 12 weight loss injections and injections of ‘alluvi glow’, a research drug that purports to regenerate skin and muscle tissue.” Earlier this year Chief Inspector of Prisons, Charlie Taylor, said inmates in UK prisons were getting fat jabs and hair loss drugs shipped behind bars by drone gangs.

‌



View 2 Images Inspectors also found "alluvi glow", a research drug that purports to regenerate skin and muscle tissue

Katie Price reveals son Harvey will be starting weight loss drug after Ibiza trip READ MORE :

He said it made it possible for prisoners to pick from a “menu” of illicit substances banned in prisons. The banned substances are allegedly flown into prisons by gangs operating drones, some packages can weigh up to 4kg.

In an annual report Mr Taylor said: “This just shows the scale of the problem the Prison Service is facing. Along with weight-loss drugs and others for hair loss, prisoners can buy anabolic steroids along with illegal drugs like cannabis and ketamine.

‌



“Prisoners in some jails are able to pick off a menu, choosing from a range of different drugs.” At HMP Thorn Cross inspectors also revealed the range of other drugs discovered after prisoners were subjected to mandatory drug tests – MDTs.

The report revealed: “Cocaine, ketamine and cannabis were the most widely detected illicit drugs on MDTs. Both cocaine and ketamine are more rapidly metabolised than other illicit drugs and so it is thought the men choose these, as there is a lower risk of a positive drug test.

“Intelligence reports, along with drug finds, suggest that steroid misuse is highly prevalent; in the month of April 2026 the only illicit drugs found on the estate were steroids.

‌



“Illicit items continue to be found on a very regular basis from a combination of ad hoc finds, targeted searches from intelligence reports and random searches, which includes the use of sniffer dogs. Mobile phones and drugs are regularly found on site.”

The report also revealed the jail had set-up its own football league. IMB inspectors added: “In terms of team sports, the sports field is an underused resource.

"Encouragingly an inter-unit football match was held this spring and was a great success.

Article continues below

“Matches are to continue weekly, creating a prison unit football league. Gym instructor courses have finally started this reporting year, delivered by the prison gym staff and with around 10 men on the course. These courses will equip the men with qualifications to help them gain employment on release.”

A Prison Service spokesperson said: “This report recognises clear positives at HMP Thorn Cross, including low levels of violence and strong support for those with drug and alcohol addiction.

“But we know more must be done, which is why we have invested over £40 million in physical security measures to clamp down on illicit items. Any prisoner caught with contraband can face disciplinary action, including loss of privileges and extra time in custody.”

News.title: Big Church Festival live: Hero helped lift sign off victims after it came 'crashing down' killing man
News.content:
Ambulance crews and police were called to Big Church Festival on Friday afternoon

One person has died after a sign fell on people at Big Church Festival in Steyning in West Sussex, with ambulance crews treating six people at the scene

Big Church Festival live: Hero helped lift sign off victims after it came 'crashing down' killing man

A 41-year-old man has died after a huge sign came “crashing down” onto people at Big Church Festival in Steyning.

Author Andrew Ollerton has since revealed he and his wife were walking just a few paces behind when the sign fell. He said they rushed to help lift it off those underneath and gave first aid alongside others until paramedics arrived.

Police and ambulance crews rushed to the Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday afternoon after reports of several people having been injured.

Six people were treated for injuries at the scene following the incident at around 3.38pm. Sussex Police later confirmed a man from Eastbourne had died.

The festival, which had been due to continue until Sunday, has now been cancelled by organisers.

South East Coast Ambulance Service was called to reports of multiple people in need of medical attention, while an air ambulance was pictured leaving the scene.

This is a live news event. Please check for the latest updates below.

News.title: Body found in search for missing Brit who disappeared on Greek island
News.content:
Body found in search for missing Brit who disappeared on Greek island

A search operation was launched with emergency workers and volunteers combing part of the Greek island of Kefalonia after the 55-year-old Brit went missing on Tuesday

View Image The man was reported missing from the holiday hotspot of Kefalonia (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A body has been found during the search for a missing British tourist on the Greek island of Kefalonia.

‌



The 55-year-old had been holidaying with his wife in Katelios before setting off on foot towards the wider Pastra area, Greek media reports.

‌



A major search operation involving police officers, firefighters, emergency workers and volunteers was launched, with drones also deployed as teams scoured difficult terrain.

‌



Searchers faced temperatures of up to 36C as they looked for the missing man across the island.

A trained rescue dog was reportedly given some of the tourist’s belongings to smell before leading searchers to a difficult mountainous area near Pastra, where a body was found.

Article continues below

Local authorities have not yet formally confirmed whether the body is that of the missing 55-year-old. Searches in the area were reportedly called off following the discovery.

The man’s relatives were in Kefalonia and remained in regular contact with search teams, according to local reports.

The Mirror has contacted the Foreign Office for comment.

News.title: Donald Trump boasts as US makes oil move after deposing Venezuela's Maduro
News.content:
Donald Trump boasts as US makes oil move after deposing Venezuela's Maduro

The US president boasted in a block capital post on Truth Social that the country would see its oil reserves 'more than double' as his administration plunders Venezuela

View 5 Images Trump has announced a major new oil venture for the US in Venezuela (Image: AP Photo/Manuel Balce Ceneta)

Donald Trump has made a bare-faced boast cementing his true aims in Venezuela after deposing the country's former leader and shipping him to the US.

‌



The US President declared this weekend that a deal made with the nation, led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, "more than doubles American oil reserves". Revealing the details in a Truth Social post, he said controlling a fifth of the South American nation's oil reserves in a deal with private business would yield his country more than 65 million barrels, describing it as "THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!"

‌



The announcement comes after Trump was accused by Venezuela's former leader Nicolas Maduro, who is awaiting trial in a New York prison on federal drug trafficking charges, of trying to seize control of the country's reserves.

‌



View 5 Images The Trump administration claimed the deal would give the US 65 million barrels of oil (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

He revealed in his social media post that the deal was forged with the help of Marco Rubio, his Secretary of State, and claimed there was "no cost" to US taxpayers.

He wrote: "At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 ‌BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer."

‌



He boasted, again in capital letters, that the transaction "MORE THAN DOUBLES American Oil Reserves". Rubio said in his own statement that the deal was "a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people".

View 5 Images Nicolas Maduro was plucked from Caracas earlier this year (Image: US President Donald Trump's TRUT)

He added in a post on social media: "For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion (£73.8 million) in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy."

‌



Rodriguez, who is now running the country under tight US control, has also claimed that the new deal with the Trump administration will be a huge boon for the nation.

She said the deal calls for the development of 17 strategic oil fields and potential of 65 billion barrels, while confirming the private investment. She said: "These investments will contribute not only to the recovery and modernization of our industry, but also to our country's economic growth, the energy security of our hemisphere, and greater balance in international markets."

View 5 Images Delcy Rodriguez revealed the plans would see the creation of additional oil fields (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The Trump administration has revealed scant additional details, but it is a continuance of its long-running US pursuit of oil in the nation, in which an audacious military operation was conducted this year to depose and extract Maduro.

He was plucked from the nation's capital, Caracas, during 'Operation Absolute Resolve', after an unsealed indictment accused him and his associates of conspiring with Colombian guerrilla groups to traffic drugs to the US. After pledging to run the country until a "safe, proper and judicious transition", Trump has made no secret that he covets Venezuela's oil reserves.

He teased American plans to retrieve the country's oil in immediate official comments on the operation, saying private companies would "go in" and "start making money".

‌



View 5 Images Trump said following the operation that the US would retrieve Venezuela's oil (Image: Satellite image Â©2026 Vantor/AFP)

He said at a press conference: “We’re going to have our very large US oil companies, the biggest anywhere in the world, go in, spend billions of dollars, fix the badly broken infrastructure, the oil infrastructure, and start making money for the country and we are ready to stage a second and much larger attack if we need to do so.”

Since then, Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores - who was also indicted - have been awaiting trial at the Metropolitan Detention Center (MDC) in Brooklyn, New York.

Article continues below

They will face trial in June next year, with a pre-trial hearing set for November 17 this year set to hear motions from both parties.

News.title: Smartphone owners warned over 'harmless' apps in hacking surge
News.content:
Smartphone owners warned over 'harmless' apps in hacking surge

Experts at Which? say the vast majority of cases involving hacked phones dealt with by its technical support team can be traced back to a dodgy app

View 3 Images In the worst cases, the apps can even take over the appearance of the phone (Image: Organic Media via Getty Images)

Smartphone owners have been warned that a seemingly harmless app could leave their device at the mercy of hackers.

‌



Experts at Which? say that the vast majority of cases involving hacked phones dealt with by its technical support team can be traced back to a dodgy app. The rogue software can masquerade as something useful - such as a PDF reader or QR-code scanner - before bombarding the victims with adverts, demanding suspicious permissions or encouraging them to download yet more software.

‌



In the worst cases, the apps can even take over the appearance of the phone, making it harder for users to find their way into settings and remove them. Which? Technical Support Adviser Conor Houlihan said rogue apps and unwanted pop-ups were a common problem encountered by the organisation's experts.

‌



He said it could be particularly alarming when adverts suddenly appear across the entire screen or familiar menus on a phone are changed. One Which? member reported their Samsung phone had become virtually unusable because of constant pop-ups and adverts.

The messages encouraged the victim to call a telephone number or install another app – but restarting the phone did nothing to stop them. Which? said its experts had encountered rogue apps capable of replacing the phone's launcher, the software responsible for controlling the appearance and behaviour of the home screen and app drawer.

Some had even imitated the Android Settings screen, potentially making it harder for owners to work out what was wrong and remove the offending app. The consumer group highlighted a fake PDF reader as an example of how an innocent-looking app could become a menace.

‌



View 3 Images The rogue software can masquerade as something useful (Image: Ekaterina Goncharova via Getty Images)

The app displayed an alarming warning that the device needed 'cleaning' and offered a supposed solution. But it also requested permission to send and view SMS messages – something Which? says should immediately raise suspicions for a basic PDF reader.

The danger signs

Which? experts advise smartphone owners to be particularly wary if their phone suddenly starts behaving strangely.

‌



Warning signs include:

Pop-ups appearing constantly, including when other apps are being used.

Apps appearing that you do not remember installing.

Unexpected changes to the home screen or app drawer.

Alarming messages claiming the phone needs cleaning or urgent attention.

An app demanding permissions that appear unrelated to its purpose.

Prompts telling you to telephone a number or download another app.

The crucial advice is simple: do not do what the pop-up tells you to do. Do not call a number displayed in a suspicious warning and do not install another app because you have been instructed to do so. Instead, Which? recommends checking the apps recently installed on the phone.

‌



On Android devices, owners can go to Settings > Apps and look for anything they do not recognise, particularly software installed around the time the problems started.

If an unwanted app refuses to be removed, Which? recommends trying Safe Mode, which temporarily disables apps installed by the user. On many Android phones, users can open the power menu and press and hold Power off until the Safe Mode option appears.

Once the phone restarts, the suspicious app can be removed through Settings > Apps before the device is restarted normally.

‌



It may not even be a hacked phone

Which? also warns that some apparently frightening pop-ups can actually be browser notifications from a website. On Chrome, users can check these by going to the three-dot menu, then Settings > Site settings > Notifications.

Notifications from websites they do not recognise or trust should be blocked. But anyone who has entered bank, payment or other sensitive details into a suspicious app or website should act quickly.

Which? advises contacting the bank using a trusted telephone number or its official app and changing passwords for accounts that may have been put at risk.

‌



View 3 Images Which? said its experts had encountered rogue apps capable of replacing the phone's launcher (Image: SimpleImages via Getty Images)

Android users face particular risk

The Which? experts say most of the cases they see involve Android phones. One reason is that Android allows apps to be installed from outside the Google Play Store.

That does not mean Google Play is completely safe, however, as harmful apps have occasionally slipped through its checks. iPhones sold in Britain have tighter restrictions on installing software from outside Apple's App Store.

‌



But Which? warns that iPhone users can still encounter scam apps and nuisance browser notifications.

How to avoid downloading a rogue app

Which? recommends sticking to official app stores where possible and checking an app carefully before installing it. Look at the developer's name and recent reviews, paying particular attention to complaints about intrusive adverts, unexpected subscriptions or persistent pop-ups.

And think twice before downloading an app simply because a website tells you that you need one.

‌



Your phone may already have the feature you are looking for. For example, both Android phones and iPhones can scan QR codes using their built-in cameras, so there is usually no need for a separate QR scanner.

Permissions are another major warning sign. If an app asks for access that appears to have nothing to do with its function, users should stop and think before granting it. A QR-code scanner asking for access to contacts, for example, should set alarm bells ringing.

Android owners should also make sure Google Play Protect is switched on. This can be checked through the Google Play Store by going to the profile picture, Play Protect and Settings, and ensuring 'Scan apps with Play Protect' is enabled.

Article continues below

Keeping the phone and its apps updated is also important because security updates can protect against newly discovered threats. And users should be especially suspicious of unexpected links arriving by text, email or social media – particularly if they are being urged to install software or change their phone's settings.

The Which? warning comes with a reassuring message too. Its experts say many rogue-app problems can be fixed once the offending software has been identified and removed, or unwanted browser notifications have been blocked.

But the first step is recognising that the frightening warning flashing up on your screen may itself be the trap. More information here.

News.title: Dolly Parton's heartbreaking final resting place as family gather for funeral
News.content:
Dolly Parton's heartbreaking final resting place as family gather for funeral

Dolly's death touched the hearts of millions around the world, and now the iconic singer and person has been laid to rest surrounded by her closest family

View 6 Images Only Dolly's closest family attended her funeral (Image: AP)

Dolly Parton's loved ones have gathered at the country music legend's final resting place, days after her death at the age of 80. Around a dozen of the singer's relatives were at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in Nashville on Friday morning.

‌



The star is to be laid to rest beside her beloved husband Carl Dean as the first images of their heartbreaking tomb have emerged online.

‌



The Jolene singer died on Tuesday, August 25, following what her representatives described as a "brief battle" with cancer. She was surrounded by loved ones at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville.

‌



Dolly had made her wishes for after her death clear, opting against the kind of huge public send-off that could easily have accompanied the passing of one of America's most celebrated performers. Instead, her family previously announced that the star wanted an intimate farewell attended only by those closest to her.

"At Dolly’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family," they said.

6 View 6 Images Dolly's nephew said she wanted to be laid to rest in a soft cotton dress, after years of wearing uncomfortable rhinestones (Image: Getty Images for Focus Features) 6 View 6 Images Dolly is now with her beloved husband, Carl, who died last year

‌



It has not been confirmed whether Friday's gathering was the funeral itself. However, Page Six reports that relatives arrived carrying flowers while police and security were present around the cemetery.

Dolly's nephew Bryan Seaver, who also served as her head of security, was among those seen arriving and was reportedly helping to coordinate proceedings. Her final resting place will reunite Dolly with Carl, her husband of 58 years, who died aged 82 in March 2025.

In photos obtained by Page Six, the couple's tomb features a bronze front depicting a peaceful mountain landscape inspired by their native Tennessee. Dolly's name had already been added alongside her husband's following her death.

‌



The plaque also pictured what appears to be Dolly's humble childhood home next to an engraving of Carl's.

Details of Dolly's burial are expected to reflect the flamboyant star's personality.

View 6 Images Dolly and Carl are buried side by side (Image: Dolly Parton)

‌



She will reportedly be laid to rest wearing a comfortable cotton dress and her trademark high heels. When breaking the news of her death, her nephew Bryan revealed she had spoken to him about wanting comfort. He said in the video, "Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because, after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest."

Dolly's family have asked well-wishers not to send flowers and instead encouraged anyone wanting to honour her memory to donate to her Imagination Library.

The literacy programme, founded by Dolly in 1995, provides free books to young children and became one of the most celebrated parts of her extensive philanthropic work. Fans around the world have also been invited to leave messages in Dolly's memory online.

‌



View 6 Images An image of Dolly Parton's childhood home, in the mountains of Tennessee is immortalised on her final resting place

Her death brought an outpouring of tributes from across the entertainment industry following a career spanning more than six decades.

In an obituary published by Woodlawn Memorial Park, Dolly was remembered as a "global icon and humanitarian" whose legacy extended far beyond her music.

‌



It said: "A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family."

Woodlawn is also the resting place of several figures with close connections to country music, including Dolly's longtime collaborator Porter Wagoner and her friend Tammy Wynette. Carl's parents are also buried there.

Dolly and Carl's extraordinary relationship began before she became one of the most famous women in the world.

‌



View 6 Images Dolly and Carl met when she was just 18 years old (Image: Dolly Parton)

They met outside the Wishy Washy Laundromat in Nashville in 1964, on the very day an 18-year-old Dolly arrived in the city to pursue her dreams of becoming a singer. Carl was 21.

They married two years later in a small ceremony in Georgia and remained together for almost six decades, with Carl famously choosing to stay almost entirely outside the spotlight as his wife's career soared.

‌



Following his death last year, Dolly described them as the "perfect partners" and wrote: "He is in God’s arms now and I am okay with that."

She signed off the tribute with the words "I will always love you", a reference to one of her most famous songs.

Dolly had also revealed years before her death that there was another song she hoped would form part of her own farewell.

Article continues below

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly in 2014, she chose the country-gospel song If We Never Meet Again, which had also been played at her father's funeral.

Explaining its significance, Dolly said: "That was my daddy’s favourite. We did sing it at his funeral, and I would like it to be sung at mine."
