Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes reveals 'awkward' Man Utd situation after replacing Harry Maguire as captain
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes reveals 'awkward' Man Utd situation after replacing Harry Maguire as captain

Bruno Fernandes took over the Manchester United captaincy from Harry Maguire but admitted to feeling awkward about it at first

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes took over from Harry Maguire as the Manchester United captain (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has admitted to feeling "awkward" after being asked to replace Harry Maguire as club captain. However, the reigning Premier League Player of the Year credited his predecessor with making the change-over as seamless as possible.

‌



Maguire, who signed a new one-year contract extension on Friday, was relieved of the armband under Erik ten Hag in 2023 after a decline in performances. Fernandes, 31, was named his natural heir even though the two would remain team-mates at Old Trafford.

‌



And Fernandes has described the moment he and Maguire first spoke after that decision was made. However, Maguire's mature manner over the situation immediately made the incumbent skipper "more relaxed about the situation."

‌



"To be honest, [when] I got asked if I wanted to be captain of the club, it was a bit awkward for me because obviously I hadn't spoken to Harry about it," he told LIFEJACKET. "But he already knew it before me, so I think the manager spoke with him before speaking with me.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"So he was very good, he came and talked to me about it and he said that if he had to lose the armband, it would go to someone like me. So that made me a little bit more relaxed about the situation, also because me and him had a very close relationship before because he was already captain, I was captain when he wasn't there.

‌



Man Utd made history vs Ipswich - now their decline means any win will do on Sunday READ MORE :

"So we knew this would keep the communication [about] things we needed to sort out in the dressing room, or whatever. And that hasn't changed since then, because obviously I've got the armband but I've always made Harry aware [he's] part of the captain's armband, too, because I think he deserves that respect in terms of everything he's done for the club and everything he's done also for me since I came to the club."

Fernandes went on to say it was nonetheless difficult for him to disguise his pride at being selected as skipper. He acknowledged the long line of iconic United captains and how big a moment it was for him to join that exclusive group.

View 2 Images Fernandes and Maguire remain close in the United dressing room despite the captaincy swap (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



In an ideal scenario, a change of captaincy would occur when one skipper leaves a club on a high note having performed his duties to a tee. But in Maguire's case, it was perceived almost as a demotion within the United squad during a period of underperformance.

When asked how things have changed for him as captain, Fernandes went on to say the only real difference is the amount of media commitments. The Portugal playmaker was already accustomed to performing a lot of media duties but took on an even greater responsibility as captain.

‌



On a more micro scale, however, he's endeavoured to keep things largely the same. More specifically Fernandes concluded by saying he has always tried to treat others the same as he gave a modest summary of his duties.

"I haven't changed the way I behave around people or the way I treat people," he added. "Because I think the main thing always has to be respect between the people you work with, towards you and you towards them.

"And it doesn't change by you being the captain. It doesn't make you any bigger than anyone else, so it's just an armband that gives you responsibility in certain moments that you have to make decisions on behalf of others. But that's the only thing and you can't step on top of anyone just because you've got the armband."

Sports.title: PSG star knocked out in worrying scenes during warm up as medics rush on pitch
Sports.content:
PSG star knocked out in worrying scenes during warm up as medics rush on pitch

A Paris Saint-Germain player was knocked out in a harrowing collision ahead of the club's clash with Lille on Friday, as medics rushed over to provide treatment

View Image Matyev Safonov suffered a ruthless collision before the match (Image: Ligue 1)

Matyev Safonov was wiped out in a brutal collision during Paris Saint-Germain's warm-up ahead of their Ligue 1 fixture with Lille on Friday. The goalkeeper was spotted lunging to punch a ball away during drills prior to kick-off, when his head collided with a member of Les Parisiens' first-team coaching staff.

‌



The 27-year-old lay on his back on the pitch, as medical staff rushed over to provide treatment, as players and staff surrounded Safonov anxiously. While Lucas Chevalier began preparing for a last-minute change between the sticks, the PSG No. 2 was ultimately told to stand down, with Safonov allowed to start after brief treatment.

‌



Safonov managed the full 90 minutes as PSG were held to a 2-2 draw at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, in a highly-dramatic encounter. Hakon Haraldsson opened the scoring for the hosts just 21 minutes in, with Lille putting on a defensive masterclass to hold onto their lead for the majority of the duration.

‌



Andoni Iraola breaks silence on Bradley Barcola transfer after Liverpool agree £120m move READ MORE :

Dilane Bakwa put another sword in PSG's back with less than 10 minutes remaining, with Les Parisiens left with a mountain to climb to take anything from the match at 2-0 down.

Thankfully, Luis Enrique didn't have to make the trip back to the French capital too red-faced, with Vitinha clawing a goal back early into stoppage time, before Marquinhos levelled matters at the death.

It came as a troubling showing for the defending Ligue 1 champions, who have now managed just two points from their first two matches of the season.

‌



The club were also held to a 2-2 draw by Rennes last weekend in their opening match of 2026/27, and sit sixth in the league standings as a result.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star claims he 'never wants Bruno Fernandes to win award again' as demand made
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star claims he 'never wants Bruno Fernandes to win award again' as demand made

Manchester United talisman Bruno Fernandes has recently been named the PFA Player of the Year but Patrice Evra claims he wants to see the playmaker change his approach

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes and Man Utd were beaten in their opening game of the season

Former Manchester United star Patrice Evra has sensational claimed he "never wants to see Bruno Fernandes win Player of the Year again" as he called on the talisman to have more of an influence on his team-mates.

‌



Fernandes has long been the leading light at Old Trafford and last year enjoyed arguably his best year to date. He broke the record for the number of assists in a season en route to being named the PFA Player of the Year.

‌



His efforts helped haul United up to third, owing to a stunning run of form in the second part of the season. Fernandes has often taken on responsibility for the team with his individual quality winning games singlehandedly, but Evra wants to see an evolution.

‌



The Frenchman has hailed his match-winning ability, but believes he now needs to have a greater impact on his team-mates, which would likely mean sacrificing individual awards.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Stake ambassador Patrice Evra said on his Kick Stream: "Bruno will keep winning all the personal awards, but I want him to make his teammates play better. So yes, Bruno will provide assists, score goals, all of that, but let’s stop being hypocritical. I’m asking all of Man United, does Bruno make the team play better? Does he control the game? No. But does he win you games? Yes.

‌



"That’s more important, but now that he’s won the Player of the Year award, I don’t want to see him win it again. I want Bruno play a part of the team, to be the maestro, to control the game, to dictate the game. I know what I’m talking about."

Fernandes was unable to inspire United in their opening game as Michael Carrick's side were shocked at Hull. The Championship play-off winners stunned those from Manchester by securing a 2-0 win, which served as a reality check for the former champions.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes was recently named PFA Players' Player of the Year (Image: Professional Footballer's Association)

‌



Evra believes Fernandes needs greater help from those behind him, especially if he's playing further forward as a playmaker, and has suggested that Kobbie Mainoo should play instead of new signing Youri Tielemans. At Hull it was the former Aston Villa man who got the nod ahead of Mainoo.

“If you want Bruno to play as the number 10, then fair enough, but you need a midfielder behind him to control the tempo," said Evra. "Someone like Kobbie Mainoo. But that’s not the way we’re playing right now. Bruno, Mainoo and Baleba are our best midfield. Tielemans is too soft, I prefer Mainoo.”

Sports.title: Liverpool's Bradley Barcola fee explained as Reds save £22m after transfer breakthrough
Sports.content:
Liverpool's Bradley Barcola fee explained as Reds save £22m after transfer breakthrough

Liverpool have reached an agreement to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain just days before the summer window slams shut, with the Reds saving £22m on the move

View Image Liverpool look set to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: PSG via Getty Images)

Liverpool have managed to save £22million in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola, having struck a deal with Paris Saint-Germain to the tune of £123m. The Reds have pursued the 23-year-old winger for the entirety of the summer, with Les Parisiens initially slapping a transfer fee of around £145m on him to deter any suitors.

‌



However, with the Frenchman falling out of favour under Luis Enrique, coupled with the acquisitions of Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche behind Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, PSG's valuation of Barcola has dropped. Now a deal has been agreed to move on Barcola for £123m.

‌



As per the Athletic, that fee is made up of an initial guaranteed £106m, as well as £17m in add-ons. A medical for Barcola is now expected in the next 24 hours.

‌



Steven Gerrard names the one signing Liverpool must make before deadline day READ MORE :

Liverpool handed third Harvey Elliott transfer bid as player faces major choice READ MORE :

It comes as Liverpool lacked creativity in the final third last Sunday, as they kicked of their Premier League season with a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St James' Park. Barcola should recify that issue, given the Lyon-born talent managed 11 goals and two assists in Ligue 1 alone last term, before shining with France at the World Cup this summer.

However, Barcola isn't the only player that the Reds are looking to snap up as the summer transfer window ticks down. Andoni Iraola could also have Ismaila Sarr at his disposal for the rest of the season, with Liverpool agreeing a five-year contract with the Crystal Palace attacking-midfielder.

Negotiations with the Eagles now await, given the club rejected an opening bid of around £51m for the 28-year-old. Elsewhere, Liverpool are also reportedly considering a move for Monaco's Lamine Camara.

‌



Monaco are thought to be willing to sell the 22-year-old midfielder ahead of Tuesday's transfer deadline, but only for the right price. Further departures could also come on Liverpool's part ahead of the window closing.

Sports.title: F1 contracts: How long is each driver signed up for?
Sports.content:
A look at how long each Formula 1 driver's contract is believed to be, as it stands in 2026, amid the potential for some key moves heading into the 2027 season.

McLaren

Lando Norris - 2030

Lando Norris agreed a contract extension in August 2026 to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030, with options to extend beyond that season.

Norris has been with McLaren since his F1 debut in 2019 and became world champion in 2025.

Oscar Piastri - 2028

Oscar Piastri signed a new multi-year contract extension ahead of the 2025 F1 season that will keep him at McLaren until the end of 2028.

Mercedes

George Russell - 2027

Officially, Mercedes announced George Russell only for 2026 after speculation throughout last summer.

But, Sky Sports News understands Russell signed a multi-year contract so will be with Mercedes until at least the end of 2027.

Kimi Antonelli - 2027

Mercedes confirmed Kimi Antonelli will remain for 2026 at the same time as their October announcement regarding Russell's future.

Sky Sports News understands, like Russell, Antonelli signed a long-term deal that will keep him at Mercedes for at least a third campaign in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli superbly won the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix

Red Bull

Max Verstappen - 2030

Max Verstappen ended speculation about his future by signing a new Red Bull contract in August 2026 that will see him stay with the team until the end of 2030.

Verstappen citied the possibility of V8 engines returning, confidence in Red Bull and racing in other motorsport categories as some of the reasons behind his new deal.

Isack Hadjar - 2026

Isack Hadjar will be the seventh driver in the last eight years to try their hand at being Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull following his impressive rookie campaign at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar's future will be largely dictated around how close he is to Verstappen, regardless of how strong the RB22 is.

Ferrari

Charles Leclerc - 2028

Charles Leclerc penned his latest Ferrari deal in June 2026. As with his previous agreement, announced in January 2024, the team did not publicly comment on the length of his contract, simply saying that it secured Leclerc's future at Maranello "for the coming seasons".

That would take Leclerc up to at least the end of 2028, while there may also be options beyond that to extend further too.

Lewis Hamilton - 2027

Lewis Hamilton's shock announcement in February 2024 to join Ferrari in 2025 was one of the biggest F1 transfer deals in the sport's history.

Ferrari announced the move as a multi-year deal. Hamilton provided more clarity on the precise length of that term when he confirmed at the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix that he also had a contract in place for at least 2027, which would be his third year at the team. Sky Sports F1 understands Hamilton also holds a unilateral option for 2028 too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the 2026 Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

Williams

Alex Albon - 2027

Williams announced during the 2026 summer break a one-year contract extension for Alex Albon that will keep him with the team until the end of 2027.

The short-term nature of the deal perhaps reflects concern in Albon's camp over the team's lack of progress, but also a lack of realistic alternatives being available to him.

Carlos Sainz - 2028

A day after Albon's extension was announced, Williams revealed that Sainz had agreed a multi-year extension that appears to tie the Spaniard to the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

The "multi-year" nature of the deal came as a something of a surprise given Sainz had publicly expressed doubts over remaining with Williams given their poor start to the 2026 season.

Racing Bulls

Liam Lawson - 2026

Liam Lawson will look to establish himself as the lead driver at Racing Bulls against rookie Arvid Lindblad and should he really impress Red Bull, it should not be ruled out about the possibility of him being in contention to return to the main team.

If that's not possible, Lawson may talk to other teams to secure a spot on the 2027 grid, but he must first deliver some strong results.

Arvid Lindblad - 2026

British teenager Lindblad is the only rookie on the 2026 grid after impressing Red Bull in his three practice outings last year, finishing sixth in first practice in Mexico City.

The 18-year-old just needs to ensure he does not make any big mistakes and if can match, or beat, team-mate Lawson, at the very least he will have a second season at Racing Bulls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch as F1 drivers reunite to take their class of 2026 season photo

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso - 2026

Fernando Alonso agreed a contract extension in April 2024 to remain with Aston Martin until at least the end of the 2026 F1 season.

Alonso is the oldest driver on the grid and will turn 45 later this year, which would make him the first driver to compete in Formula 1 at that age since Graham Hill in 1975.

Aston Martin appear to be on the backfoot, so there will naturally be questions about whether Alonso will retire at the end of this season.

Lance Stroll - 2026

Lance Stroll is the only driver in the field whose contract details are largely unknown, partly because he is the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, and appears to have a seat for as long as his father remains in that position.

Stroll has been outperformed by Alonso during their three seasons together but Aston Martin formally announced in June 2024 that the Canadian has a deal for "2025 and beyond".

Haas

Oliver Bearman - 2026

Oliver Bearman's first full F1 campaign in 2025 saw a mixture of high-profile mistakes and lightning speed - with the latter aspect leading to speculation over whether he could replace Hamilton at Ferrari in the future.

Haas are unlikely to be front-runners in F1 any time soon, so at 20 years old, Bearman could be a key name in the driver market this season, should he impress on the track.

Esteban Ocon - 2026

Esteban Ocon's stock has fallen slightly over the last two years after a disappointing end to his time at Alpine in 2024 and being outperformed by Bearman at Haas in 2025.

Ocon will aim to get on top of Bearman in the inter-team battle, which could be important given both drivers have not been confirmed for 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oliver Bearman discusses his ambition to one day be in a Ferrari seat, but admits he's 'just getting started' with Haas

Audi

Nico Hulkenberg - 2026

Nico Hulkenberg signed a multi-year contract when he joined Sauber, which is now Audi, in 2025 which means he does not necessarily have a seat beyond this season.

Hulkenberg still seems to enjoy F1 and has not shown any signs of retiring despite being a father and 38 years old.

Gabriel Bortoleto - 2026

Gabriel Bortoleto perhaps did not hit the heights many expected after winning the F3 and F2 titles in his rookie seasons on his way to F1.

Bortoleto improved as 2025 went on and is still one of the best young talents on the grid, so it will be in Audi's best interests to keep the 21-year-old.

Alpine

Pierre Gasly - 2028

Pierre Gasly announced a new contract last September to stay at Alpine until at least the end of 2028, having joined the team in 2023.

Gasly has established himself as the lead driver at Alpine and a more competitive car this year could see him cause some surprise results when the top teams trip up.

Franco Colapinto - 2027

Franco Colapinto replaced Jack Doohan just six rounds into the 2025 season and recovered from a shaky start to his Alpine career to earn a seat for this season.

The Argentine has impressed Alpine enough to retain his seat for a second full campaign in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Craig Slater sits down with Franco Colapinto to discuss his new contract at Alpine

Cadillac

Sergio Perez - 2027

Sergio Perez returns to F1 this year with newcomers Cadillac after a season out of the sport and will be with the American outfit for at least two seasons.

Although Perez was only confirmed for 2026, Sky Sports News understands he signed a multi-year deal.

Valtteri Bottas - 2027

Valtteri Bottas is also understood to have agreed a multi-year contract that will see him be with Cadillac until at least the end of 2027.

Just like Perez, he spent 2025 on the sidelines but will be hoping to add a few more highlights to his F1 career.

Sports.title: 'Nowhere else I want to be' - Norris extends McLaren contract until 2030
Sports.content:
Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris has extended his contract with McLaren until at least 2030.

The 26-year-old Brit's previous extension, which was announced ahead of the start of the 2024 season, was understood to tie him to the team until at least the end of 2027.

He will now stay at McLaren for at least another four seasons with the extended deal to the end of 2030 including "a multi-year option to commit beyond that date".

Norris claimed the 2025 title to become Britain's 11th world champion, and the first McLaren driver to triumph since Lewis Hamilton in 2008.

Saturday's announcement of the new deal follows Norris winning last weekend in the Netherlands to claim the 13th Grand Prix victory of his F1 career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Lando Norris' roller-coaster season so far, which has seen several DNFs and race wins, putting him in the mix to challenge for the title.

Norris said: "McLaren is my home, and I'm very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030.

"When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships.

"We've achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we're capable of achieving it."

Norris at McLaren: The story so far Race debut: 2019 Australian Grand Prix

Starts: 163

Wins: 13

Podiums: 48

Pole positions: 18

Best season finish: World champion, 2025

Team principal Andrea Stella described Norris as "an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren".

"But above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team," added Stella.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1."

After McLaren, the reigning constructors' champions, failed to claim a Grand Prix win across the opening 10 rounds of the season, Norris has won back-to-back races to reignite hope that he could yet defend his title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The moment Lando Norris became F1 2025 World Champion!

Norris is fourth in the drivers' standings, 83 points back from leader Kimi Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining. Norris must also leapfrog Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who both trail the Italian by 59 points.

Norris is driving his eighth season for McLaren, having been given his F1 debut by the team as a 19-year-old in 2019. His 163 Grand Prix starts are a team record, with Norris having surpassed fellow Brit David Coulthard's mark of 150 at last year's Qatar Grand Prix.

McLaren's other driver, Oscar Piastri, last year signed a contract extension that ties him to the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

McLaren were briefly linked with a move for Max Verstappen earlier this summer, but the four-time world champion recently ended speculation over his future by signing a contract extension - also until 2030 - with Red Bull.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix.

On Norris' contract, Stella added: "This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together.

"With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

Chief executive Zak Brown said: "[Norris'] journey with the team is a fantastic example of our commitment to identifying, developing and supporting world-class talent, and his achievements speak for themselves.

"Together with Andrea, Oscar and the wider team, Lando has helped drive McLaren into a new papaya era of success... We are extremely excited about what lies ahead and remain fully focused on continuing to compete for wins and championships."

'Four more years fighting for championships'

Norris has played a key role in helping McLaren transition from being a midfield team when he joined to returning to the front of the grid.

He and Piastri led the team to a first constructors' title for 26 years in 2024, before adding his maiden drivers' title the following season after coming out on top of an intense battle with his team-mate and Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Lando Norris looks back at his career up until his World title win in Abu Dhabi.

Asked during an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News whether it was an easy decision to sign an extension, Norris replied: "I would say so.

"After what we've achieved the last two years, over just the fun that we've had together since 2019, nowhere else I want to be, to be honest with you.

"I know we can achieve a lot more together here, exactly where I am, and I'm very excited about our future together."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris celebrates becoming World Champion with tears, doughnuts and hugs!

Norris is open to the idea of spending his whole career at McLaren, and says he would be "so proud" to leave F1 having only driven for the Woking squad.

"I don't know what the future holds," Norris said. "I still, of course, believe that we can win more as a team and win more constructors' and more drivers' championships, and that's why I want to stay here.

"But they are also the only team I've ever been with and the team that I love, and I call this place my home. So, if I do end up just doing my whole career in McLaren, that's something I'll be so proud to say and to carry with me through the rest of my life.

"But I don't know what point I want to go to as a driver. Whether I want to be 30 or 40, 50. I don't know that state yet.

"So, I'm just very, very pleased to, of course, announce I'll be here for four more years and four more years fighting for wins and championships, hopefully."

Sports.content:
We have an action-packed day’s racing on Saturday with flat action from Chepstow, Windsor and Saratoga, live on Sky Sports Racing...

6.30 Windsor - Ghostwriter, Tenability and Silawi headline

The feature event on a splendid card at Windsor sees Ghostwriter and Tenability headline nine runners for this Listed August Stakes.

Ghostwriter has attracted a lot of attention since Amo bought him for £2 million back in June 2025 and he has yet to reward his connections. A classy operator at his peak, he showed he might be building towards a big performance when fourth at Goodwood and this looks a good fit.

Silawi, winner of the Grade One Canadian International at Woodbine last year, ran a cracker when runner-up in the Jebel Hatta in January but has not hit those highs since. Well beaten in Germany last month, he will hope to bounce back at a track that suits.

Tenability shoulders a three-pound penalty for his Tapster Stakes success at Goodwood but usually runs his race, while Warrant Holder is another for each-way players to ponder.

Debut winner Crown And Two bids to remain unbeaten in the opening Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Novice Stakes at Windsor.

The Tom Clover-trained colt created a fine impression when landing a Newmarket novice 23 days ago and he rates the one to beat if handling these slower conditions.

George Boughey's Arthur Carrot broke slowly when second to Mithaaly at this track earlier this month and he should be sharper on this occasion.

Others to note include William Haggas' twice-race Bulletsnap while Blue Victory remains capable of better after his debut fifth.

Last-time winners Minster Man and Roxa Love clash in a cracking Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes at Chepstow.

Minster Man chased home the useful Evenfall on debut before landing a Musselburgh novice with plenty to spare. A fine big type, he will be expected to improve again and could defy an opening mark of 85.

Roxa Love built on her debut when outpointing Henley On Thames at Brighton and with that rival winning at York last week, she must be of interest under Pat Cosgrave.

Sports.title: Fight of the year? Mayer and Cameron seek to cement greatness
Sports.content:
It was cordial, until it wasn't. Courteous, until it wasn't. Captivating, already.

Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron need not marinate Saturday night's main event with any further spice, but few will grumble over a new dimension to the rivalry.

Each had been complimentary of the other's accolades, willingly acknowledging the elite talents of one another and mutually admiring the ease at which a rare pound-for-pound collision has come to fruition as they teased a fight-of-the-year contender.

But a subdued build-up exploded into life on Friday as the pair needed to be split by security after butting heads and trading insults at a surprise clash during their weigh-in.

This was not in the script, for either.

"I've had some heated build-ups before, but that's only because it was just very genuine and authentic," WBA and WBC champion Mayer had told Sky Sports, speaking ahead of the weigh-in. "I didn't go looking for it. And Chantelle seems to be a pretty chill, down-to-earth person, so I don't think she would even go there if she felt some type of way."

WBO belt-holder Cameron, also in reference to their relaxed build-up, had added: "I think it shows we're two great fighters. You don't need all the trash talk and the bad blood. Just putting on a circus is not needed. We're just two good fighters that are going to beat each other up."

How it all changed.

Mayer vs Cameron - fighter records

Mikaela Mayer Wins 22 Losses 2

Chantelle Cameron Wins 22 Losses 1

Intentional or not, things would turn up a notch on the eve of their super-welterweight world title showdown in Birmingham. By the end Cameron had vowed to "smash her head in".

Before now it loomed as a fight capable of selling itself based on resume, based on skillset and based on the magnitude of two greatness-bound fighters sharing the ring; Mayer arrives as a three-weight world champion, while Cameron has reigned in two weight classes and as the only woman to defeat the great Katie Taylor as a professional.

The closely-matched pair had prompted familiar fence-sitting among peers and pundits understandably struggling to forecast Saturday's headline act.

"I know I believe in myself, she believes in herself and the exciting part about this is we genuinely both think that we're better fighters," said Mayer. "Now we get to go in there and prove it.

"I think it's split in the public. Half the people think that Chantelle's a better fighter, and half the people think that I'm the better fighter. So that's what's going to sell this fight.

"I know I'm going to win, but the public doesn't. That's what makes this exciting and intriguing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikaela Mayer says if she reproduces her form from training camp she may shock the pundits who are calling this a close contest and win by knockout

Among the themes to emerge this week has been Mayer's insistence that it would be "impossible" for Cameron to train for this version of her, such has been the American's self-proclaimed evolution alongside coach Kofi Jantuah over the last two years.

"As I'm shadowboxing I don't even do the same combos anymore," said Mayer. "It takes time for a coach to instil what he's trying to show a fighter, especially an older fighter like me - I have to change habits.

"He's really made me a better fighter. It's been a 10-month lay-off, but not a lay-off, because I've been in the gym every day perfecting all that stuff that he's trying to drill into me..

"I just seriously don't think you can train for me because I'm not throwing the same stuff. I'm not moving the same way."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron says Mikaela Mayer's pre-fight talk is a sign of lacking confidence and she's certain of winning a close contest in Birmingham

Cameron, fighting at super-welterweight for the second time after April's win over Michaela Kotaskova, has meanwhile cast doubt on how much growth there is left for Mayer at this stage in her career.

"I think that's just insecurity speaking," Cameron said. "She's not going to change that much. That's just doubting yourself and having to be insecure and speaking up for good hype. I don't get too much into that."

As far as storylines surrounding Cameron go, her victory over Taylor has been unsurprisingly heralded as a defining moment in her career.

The Northampton fighter defeated Taylor by majority decision in May 2023 to retain her undisputed super-lightweight champion status, before losing the rematch via the same outcome later in the year.

"Styles make fights and that's yesterday's news," she said. "I've done it, I'm proud of it, but it's yesterday's news.

"I've moved on from that and now I've got another good opponent and I want to take the win on Saturday to say I beat another legend in boxing. I think that's going to really cement my resume.

"I think this will be one of my best performances. I think the way my career's been, it's just perfect timing for me and I think it's going to be the best performance of my career."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois once again tried to rattle Amelia Moore at their head to head but the American gave as good as she got.

Cameron has since won four fights on the bounce during her route to super-welterweight, where Mayer has greeted her with question marks over whether a Katie Taylor-level performance is still within her.

"It was an amazing fight. Even the second one where she didn't get the decision, it's still debatable, so for her to be the only person to beat Katie Taylor, that says something, that's an accomplishment she should feel proud of," said Mayer.

"But the way boxing, the way the sport is, you can't stay over one win for too long. You've got someone else to handle.

"I think that was the best of her, though. I think that was probably the best weight. I don't know if she has that same speed and aggression at this higher weight. I don't see her moving the way she did against Katie Taylor in the first fight, and that's what she needs to do to beat me, for sure."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alycia Baumgardner took everyone by surprise including Mikaela Mayer as she grabbed the mic and asked her former rival a question at the press conference

Ellie Scotney, who recently vacated her undisputed female super-bantamweight championship, suggested this week the winner of Saturday's fight would enter the top four greatest female fighters of all time. MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian also echoed the notion that this weekend's victor would enter GWOAT territory.

It beckons as a legacy bout between two fighters who have shrugged off turbulent moments to remain at the very top of the sport. Mayer endured defeats to both Alycia Baumgardner and Natasha Jonas that she maintains she should have won, while Cameron was denied the opportunity to settle the score with a trilogy fight against Taylor.

"Me and Cameron, there's parts of our career that you can kind of compare and call similar," said Mayer. "For us to be at such a high, to take a loss and then to feel that sort of backlash from the boxing community where it's kind of like we did so much, and then we slipped a little bit, and it's like we were unforgiven.

"It's so hard in boxing to come back from things like that, so it takes time, and some people never do, but we've sort of navigated our way back, and now we're meeting each other back at that height.

"It's really scary because one of us is going to have to take that fall again."

But who?

Sports.title: Barcola set to sign Liverpool contract to 2031
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola is set to sign a Liverpool contract to 2031 after the Premier League club reached an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over the structure of the transfer.

Sky Sports reported on Friday that an agreement in principle had been reached for Barcola to move to Anfield in a package worth £120m.

The final discussions had centred over the structure of deal, with Liverpool now set to pay £106m up front and up to £17m in add-ons.

Documents must still be exchanged between the clubs and Barcola must complete a medical, which is expected to take place this weekend.

There had been a gap in valuation between the two clubs earlier in the summer, with PSG previously asking for around £145m for the France international, but the 23-year-old is now set to sign a five-year deal with Andoni Iraola's side.

Barcola would become Liverpool's second most expensive signing of all time, following the club-record deal to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle for £125m last summer.

Barcola's arrival would potentially allow Cody Gakpo to leave Anfield, with Tottenham and Manchester City both interested in the Dutchman.

Liverpool are also trying to sign a second new winger, with their target currently Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr following difficult negotiations with Brighton for Yankuba Minteh.

Is Barcola really the right winger to replace Salah?

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Callum Bishop:

Liverpool appear to have made their decision that Bradley Barcola is their Mohamed Salah replacement. Even if they don't naturally play on the same flank, Barcola will surely be looked at as the man to bring Salah's level of productivity from the wide areas.

Image: Bradley Barcola's minutes by position for PSG in the Champions League

When you think of Salah in his pomp, you think of the goals he brought to the team by cutting in from the right flank. Perhaps there's an expectation for the Frenchman to provide similar returns. But is that really what Liverpool need from their wingers?

Salah had his least productive season at Anfield last campaign. There are a number of factors for why that is, but one of those was a change in his role thanks to the introduction of two number nines.

When the middle man in the Liverpool attack was Roberto Firmino, it allowed Salah to be the person chances were created for as the Brazilian was far from a stereotypical goalscorer. However, when Hugo Ekitike and Alexander Isak arrived on Merseyside, Salah's modus operandi shifted. More of a provider, less of a finisher.

His record of 10 assists wasn't terrible, but what's interesting is that he only provided one for Ekitike and none for Isak.

Barcola is an incredibly talented player with major upside, but Ekitike and Isak may see his arrival as more of a hindrance in their desire to shine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher is full of praise for French winger Bradley Barcola but says he does not play in the position where Liverpool need to strengthen

One thing is for sure. Jamie Carragher isn't convinced that the French international is the answer Liverpool need.

"He's a left winger for me," Carragher said. "They don't have anyone who looks comfortable playing on the right but they have four players in the squad before Barcola joins who can play off the left.

"In terms of balance of the squad, it's not the position Liverpool need."

Liverpool interested in Palace's Sarr

Image: Ismaila Sarr is another target for Liverpool

Liverpool have also approached Crystal Palace over potentially signing winger Sarr.

Andoni Iraola's side are considering their options after talks stalled with Brighton over Minteh.

Palace have no intention of letting Sarr go at this stage and consider the 28-year-old to be not for sale. He has three years left on his contract.

Sarr missed Palace's opening weekend defeat at Everton. Reports claimed he was refusing to train but it is understood that the winger is currently injured.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage provides a transfer update on Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr and says he expects both of them to stay at the club.

Asked about Sarr's future during his press conference on Wednesday, Palace boss Pierre Sage said: "I understand for everybody that to have this kind of contact is difficult because you hesitate a lot, but for the moment he is with us.

"He is under contract, he is injured, and maybe you can link his injury and the situation.

"But for me, he is honest, and I have no problem with that. I spoke with him this morning about that. Yesterday about that too, and we just want him on the pitch, and all the rest for the other people."

Mbaye set to follow Barcola to PL with Villa move

Image: Ibrahim Mbaye is set to make a move to Aston Villa

Aston Villa have reached a verbal agreement with Paris Saint-Germain to sign winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

A contract is being finalised and a medical is due to take place this weekend. The deal for the 18-year-old is worth £47m. PSG are making up to £170m from the deals for Bradley Barcola and Mbaye.

Mbaye predominantly plays on the right wing and made 24 Ligue 1 appearances for PSG last season, scoring three goals and adding two assists.

Sports.title: Wimbledon star Fery through to first career ATP final in Winston-Salem
Sports.content:
Wimbledon star Arthur Fery continued his dream summer by reaching the final of the Winston-Salem Open on Friday.

Fery has paved his way through the ATP 250 event with a couple of routine wins over Cruz Hewitt and qualifier Mees Rottgering, and then a three-set victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic in the quarterfinals

And the 24-year-old advanced to the final after Australian James Duckworth - a player he also defeated in Cincinnati just two weeks ago - retired through injury with Fery leading 6-4 1-2.

"I'm really happy to be in the final," said Fery. "Obviously, not the way I wanted it to end at all. I hope James is going to rest up and get ready for next week but very happy to be through.

"I played well in the first set. He was serving very well and tricky but managed to get the break and from then on I thought I was playing good.

"He was hindered at the start of the second set and I saw it. It's never easy playing someone who you know is physically challenged, but overall it felt good apart from that last forehand."

The Briton went on a fairy-tale Wimbledon semi-final run earlier this summer and he is set for a new career high Monday. Eight weeks ago, Fery was ranked outside the top 100.

Image: Ignacio Buse of Peru will play Fery in the Winston-Salem Open final on Saturday

Fery will take on Peruvian Ignacio Buse in the final on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 9pm BST, the world No 36, who held off Frenchman Benjamin Bonzi 6-2 4-6 6-1 to reach his second ATP Tour final.

"It's going to be another tough match," admitted Fery. "Ignacio is playing really well. He's a young guy who is breaking out so it's going to be a great match. Definitely a good week for both of us and I'm going to sit down with my coach and see what I can do to beat him."

The highest seed remaining in North Carolina, 22-year-old Buse's career highlight came in May when he claimed his first tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 in Hamburg.

A year ago Buse was ranked No 135 but he will be seeded at the US Open where he is slated to face American Marcos Giron in the first round.

Fery, who is set to make his main draw debut at the US Open starting on Sunday, faces a tough task against Italy's world No 14 Lorenzo Musetti in the opening round.

Sports.title: Cherki and Haaland double up in Manchester City cruise at Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
All who attend the Rayan Cherki show know the ticket comes with a guarantee of entertainment. Enzo Maresca, a manager famed for his obsessive positional control, does not need to put limits on the Manchester City wizard. Cherki has to feel free and he was at his creative best against Crystal Palace, who were in this game before City’s creative heartbeat took it away from them in the second half.

It has been a fine start to the former Lyon player’s second year in England. Cherki was inspired against Bournemouth last week, coming off the bench to spark City’s fightback from 1-0 down with two assists, and this was better. The Frenchman scored twice and the first, a little prod with the outside of his left foot after a mazy run, left you wondering if you have seen something like it before.

Palace, stuck on zero points despite fleeting signs of encouragement in Pierre Sage’s first two outings, had no answer to Cherki’s magic. He is an irrepressible talent and a deep thinker. Listening to the post-match plaudits, Cherki smiled, shrugged and said his performance in the first half was “so shit”. Maresca, though, had a different view.

“His performance for me was very good, not because of the two goals, but the way he worked off the ball,” City’s manager said. “He has to press. His game was complete. He loves football. We know how good he is. We know the quality he has.”

Cherki was not alone in starring for City. Phil Foden impressed and Erling Haaland, who is up and running for the season, grabbed an emphatic double in a performance strong enough to make Maresca think his post-Pep team have moved on from their Community Shield debacle. “We struggled the first five, 10 minutes, because we were pressing in the wrong way,” the Italian said. “After that we were in control.”

A challenge for Maresca is working with an incomplete midfield after the exits of Rodri and Bernardo Silva. Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived from Lille, £86m an eye-catching fee for an 18-year-old after his exploits for Morocco at the World Cup, but there is room for one more. Enzo Fernández, desperate to leave Chelsea, is the top target before Tuesday’s deadline.

Not that anyone is going to argue that City are short on midfield options. Maresca, ever the tinkerer, shuffled the pack again. The experiment with Marc Guéhi in the engine room was discontinued, allowing him to slot into central defence against his old side. The £116m Elliot Anderson was the sole pivot, Nico O’Reilly pushed high in a 4-1-4-1 system and Josko Gvardiol inverted from left-back, much like Marc Cucurella in Maresca’s Chelsea side.

There are subtle tweaks to the Guardiola template, though some things never change. City led through a familiar source in the 17th minute, Antoine Semenyo crossing from the left and Haaland finding space to loop a clever header over Dean Henderson.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland wraps up victory with the fourth goal. Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images

The defending was poor from Palace, who have had an uncertain summer. They were arranged in familiar fashion, Sage sticking with Oliver Glasner’s 3-4-2-1, but some key faces have gone and others were missing.

Jørgen Strand Larsen led the line in the absence of the unsettled Jean-Philippe Mateta, who may be out for four weeks. Ismaïla Sarr, keen to join Galatasaray, was unavailable and Daniel Muñoz was on the bench amid suggestions of interest from Nottingham Forest. Frailties were inevitable. The defence has lost Maxence Lacroix, sold to Chelsea. Anderson, Semenyo and Foden had chances before half-time. “You saw how we want to play until the 65th minute,” Sage said. “We trust in our process.”

Sage likes to play on the front foot. Adam Wharton, subject of a failed enquiry from City recently, swept a ball through for Eddie Nketiah to test Gianluigi Donnarumma in the second minute. Daichi Kamada went close and Tyrick Mitchell fluffed a header after more enterprising play from Wharton.

Palace lacked incision, Nketiah missing again early in the second half. City pressed, O’Reilly and Foden hustling Kamada. Foden advanced and Cherki took over. The Frenchman danced in from the left, danger rising as he wriggled into the area. A host of Palace defenders were thrown off balance, unable to live with Cherki’s footwork and close control. Expect the unexpected. Cherki floated past Jaydee Canvot and held off Chris Richards. For a moment the ball seemed stuck under his feet but he used Takehiro Tomiyasu as a shield and unveiled a finish that was less poke and more dab, Henderson rooted to the spot as the ball rolled tantalisingly over the line.

Palace quickly grabbed a lifeline, Yéremy Pino’s free-kick hitting the woodwork and bouncing in off Donarumma for an own goal, but Cherki was in his element. He scored again in the 59th minute, a fierce shot from 20 yards deceiving Henderson after flicking off Richards.

City sent Bouaddi on for his debut, Anderson withdrawn. They wanted more. Foden, catching the eye in front of Thomas Tuchel, released Haaland. The Norwegian, who has scored in all six of his league games against Palace, was never going to miss.

Sports.title: European football: PSG scramble another draw while Bayern make flying start
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain defender Marquinhos scored deep into stoppage ⁠time to snatch a scarcely deserved 2-2 draw at Lille on Friday as the Ligue 1 champions ⁠continued to struggle ⁠after ​being held by Rennes on the opening weekend.

After the poor 2-2 draw ‌against Rennes, things went from bad to worse for PSG when Lille took the lead in the 21st minute as Icelandic playmaker Hákon Haraldsson latched on to a brilliant reverse pass from Olivier Giroud and curled an unstoppable shot past ‌Matvei Safonov.

Despite all their attacking riches, the Parisians struggled to get shots on target as Lille packed their ​defence and forced the champions to attack from wide areas, and Lille appeared to have secured the three points when Dilane Bakwa scored in the 84th minute.

PSG midfielder Vitinha threw his side ⁠a lifeline in the first minute of stoppage time with ​a superb ​strike curled into the top-left ​corner, and the Portuguese international then crossed for ​Marquinhos to head ‌home the ​equaliser four ​minutes later to complete an improbable comeback.

View image in fullscreen Bayern Munich take the lead as Dayot Upamecano’s effort finds the net against Stuttgart. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

In the Bundesliga Bayern Munich kickstarted their title defence with a resounding 5-1 victory over Stuttgart thanks ⁠to a sparkling second-half display at the Allianz Arena that showed they have lost none of their ⁠potency from last ⁠season.

Goals from ​Dayot Upamecano, Michael Olise, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Luis Díaz capped a superb performance from the hosts during which they also ⁠missed several other opportunities.

It was a mixed night for Stuttgart’s Josha Vagnoman, who scored at both ends having briefly equalised early ⁠in the second half, as Bayern extended their unbeaten run to 15 ‌matches with victory in their first match of the new campaign.

Bayern won the Bundesliga ‌title by 16 points last season, scoring a record 122 goals in the process, ‌and there are signs they could be as dominant again as they created chance after chance against the side who finished fourth last term.

View image in fullscreen Milan supporters display a huge Baresi banner at San Siro before kick-off in the game against Venezia. Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/Reuters

In Serie A Gonçalo Ramos scored with a flashing drive from a tight angle for his first Serie A goal as Milan beat Venezia 2-0 at San Siro. Milan spent €74m to acquire Ramos from PSG and the Portugal forward delivered a goal to treasure on 69 minutes before a late own goal from Redouane Halhal settled the game.

“The most important thing isn’t my goal, it’s the win,” Ramos said. “I should have scored more than one goal tonight.” Milan opened the season with a 2-1 win at Torino making Friday’s encounter their first home game since the death of Franco Baresi and they paid tribute to their former captain before kick-off.

In La Liga, Racing Santander beat Elche 3-2 for their first win since returning to the Spanish top flight, while Alavés beat Villarreal 1-0.

Sports.title: ‘Now is a good time for players to speak up’: Lucy Bronze on Fifa and helping refugees
Sports.content:
Lucy Bronze does not stop. Her brain runs a hundred miles a minute. She does not need traditional entertainment. “I’m not good at watching TV – I can’t sit still,” Bronze says, sitting sort-of still, on a bench shielded from the wind, overlooking Chelsea’s training pitch at Cobham. “Someone recently asked me what I listen to in the car and someone else jumped in and was like: ‘Lucy has her own podcast going on in her own head.’ I don’t listen to music, I don’t listen to podcasts, I just have a million thoughts going on.”

Bronze’s late ADHD and autism diagnosis help it make sense, but her mum had always suspected she might have one of the conditions, so it wasn’t a surprise. “Naomi Girma said to me: ‘I’ve never met someone who trains so hard in the gym with zero music on; it does not make sense.’ I was like: ‘It’s literally in my head, I don’t need anything else.’”

Walking her dog, Nala, is the main thing Bronze does to relax, but otherwise she is “just involved in so many things, different businesses, PFA boards, stuff for Fifpro and Uefa at the minute. There’s obviously a lot going on behind the scenes and I’m just keeping up to date with things like that.”

“Things like that” are hugely rewarding and Bronze gets pleasure out of elements that could seem tedious but contribute to the wider game and its growth. “I love growing-the-game stuff, but it’s emotionally draining as well,” she says. “Myself and Kim Little are on the PFA players’ board and we speak to each other a lot. We’re in quite similar positions as older players who’ve lived so much of the game and want to give so much back and we feel like we’ve got so many great ideas to help so many people and that there’s so much to be done but you just want to do it all tomorrow.

“Sometimes you’ve just got to keep pushing and pushing but I do enjoy it and I feel like I’ve got endless energy so it does help that I’ve got like all these different avenues to push myself.”

Recently, that has involved being vocal about Gianni Infantino’s rogue and scuppered plan to sell off the World Cup, and his tenure as Fifa president. At the start of the month the defender backed the threat of a European boycott of Fifa competitions, regardless of what it meant for her football ambitions, telling the New Zealand Herald: “It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow.”

In a press conference on Tuesday before Chelsea’s 5-2 victory over Real Sociedad in the first leg of their Champions League qualifier, Bronze explained why she had shared the social media post of the former France defender Mikaël Silvestre, who is on Fifa’s players’ voice panel, which said “change is necessary” at the top of the game. “The football comes first no matter what, no matter who’s in charge, who’s playing … and it feels like now is a good time for players to speak up.”

View image in fullscreen Lucy Bronze, seen here during a pre-season match in Sydney, believes moving WSL matches to Stamford Bridge is a statement of intent from Chelsea. Photograph: Ayush Kumar/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images

A summer with no major international women’s tournament has given Bronze time to focus on some of the issues she is most passionate about. “I’ve been trying to go to Colombia for four years to do stuff with refugees,” says Bronze, who was asked to help with fundraising for the UNHCR (UN Refugee Agency) during Covid and has been involved since. She says, with a wry smile: “Sarina [the England head coach, Sarina Wiegman] is the one who’s always blocked it because she said that she didn’t want me travelling there before a tournament and getting jet-lagged, especially before the World Cup in Australia. She blocked it then and she blocked it before the Euros because we didn’t have a lot of time. She was like: ‘Lucy, it’s not a good idea for your body.’ So, that’s been planned for a long time.”

The trip to Colombia, which according to the UNHCR is facing a humanitarian crisis and has about 2.8 million Venezuelan refugees and migrants and seven million people who are internally displaced, was worth the Wiegman-enforced wait.

“It was crazy,” she says. “I had had a bit of the background explained to me beforehand. A lot of people don’t necessarily know so much. I guess now that there’s been the earthquake in Venezuela people know a bit more, but it’s generally not spoken about as much because it’s Venezuela to Colombia compared to like, Ukrainians to wealthier countries like England or Germany.

“Being on the ground and especially around kids was special. They don’t know why they’re in that position and it’s not their fault, it’s just the life that’s been put in front of them and they just make the most of the smallest of things. It was a tiring time, emotionally and physically, but it was powerful seeing so much good work being done too.”

Experiencing the resilience and joy of children in the worst of circumstances is “really moving” says Bronze. “At the same time, when we went to leave, there were kids saying: ‘Take me with you,’ which is really devastating.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Lucy Bronze has had the time to focus on some of the issues she is most passionate about this summer. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Bronze went with shirts, including some from Girma. “There was a refugee girl there who was the captain of this football team which was all boys,” says Bronze. “Nay’s [Girma’s] parents were refugees too. So I told this girl Nay’s story, and this kid’s face just lit up. I showed her pictures of Nay playing for America and I gave her her shirt. This girl was so excited because while it’s not someone in the exact same situation, it’s someone whose family had to rebuild their lives and she could see her own life in it and how amazing she’s doing now.”

Helping people on and off the pitch gives Bronze energy. There is excitement for the new season with Chelsea’s changed and young team under Sonia Bompastor after a high-energy pre-season.

“I feel like it’s taken Sonia till now to do everything she’s wanted to do behind the scenes, in terms of her staff and putting the trust into her staff to do the things that are part of her vision,” Bronze says. “There’s been a hard transition and balance to find what makes Chelsea so good and so dominant and so ‘Chelsea’, while also evolving and adapting, because that’s what you have to do.”

That hampered them last season, Bronze thinks: “The first year everything kind of went smoothly. As things started to change, we were so desperate to win because we are Chelsea – we need to win – but at the same time, it was about [how] we do that while evolving and I think that’s maybe what we struggled with in the second half of last season.”

There have been big changes off the pitch too, with all Women’s Super League games to be played at Stamford Bridge, starting with Aston Villa next Saturday, and cup games at Kingsmeadow in Norbiton, south-west London.

“It’s a statement of intent on the future of Chelsea’s women’s team,” says Bronze.

“Chelsea have been this dominant team on the pitch but now we need to dominate in every aspect. Not just in winning the league six times in a row – that is fantastic – but we need to win the Champions League, we need to grow as a team, we need to grow in the way that we play and the people that we bring in and we need to have a stadium that represents that ambition. Everything contributes.”

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola due for medical as Liverpool finalise £123m deal for winger
Sports.content:
Liverpool have finalised a deal worth up to £123m for Bradley Barcola, with the Paris Saint-Germain winger to undergo a medical this weekend for his move to Anfield.

Liverpool agreed the outline of a deal with the Champions League holders on Wednesday night, after lengthy talks over their main summer transfer target.

The structure of the package has now been accepted and the Anfield club will pay £106m up front for the 23-year-old, plus £17m in add-ons based on individual and team achievements.

Personal terms with Barcola have already been agreed, with the France international’s representatives giving the green light to his transfer to Merseyside last month.

The winger is set to have a medical over the weekend before completing a transfer that will make him the second-most expensive signing in Liverpool’s history, behind Alexander Isak.

Liverpool’s other incoming senior players so far this summer are the centre-back Ronald Araújo, on loan from Barcelona, the Osasuna winger Víctor Muñoz and the defender Jérémy Jacquet, whose £55m move from Rennes was agreed in January.

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants one more signing for Tottenham before transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi is keen to add one more signing to his Tottenham squad and has said outgoing deals are also possible before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline.

De Zerbi had dinner on Thursday night with Spurs’ owners and key executives and they discussed a final push to a window that has already exceeded his expectations. The manager welcomed Omar Marmoush to the club on Thursday from Manchester City and is preparing to involve him in Saturday’s home game against Newcastle. Spurs have also been linked with a move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

“I didn’t expect a market like we have done,” De Zerbi said. “I think we can do one player more and in one specific position. Yesterday we went for dinner with the owner, with Vinai [Venkatesham, the chief executive], with Johan [Lange, the sporting director] and with Enrico [Venturelli, De Zerbi’s assistant]. We spoke about this.

“It can be possible out or in. The transfer market is crazy and we have to be able to find the new players. If some players go out, leave, or to make another player [come] in … I don’t know. We are very happy with the market we have done until now. It has been more than my expectation at the beginning.”

De Zerbi is open to trimming his squad and mentioned midfielder Pape Sarr as one possible departure. “We have to see in the last day of the market what can happen with him,” he said. “I’ve been very clear with every player. If you speak clearly at the beginning you can’t expect a surprise. The players who want to leave, they left. Maybe we have some players who want to leave and they are waiting for the offer. We are waiting for the offer. To stay here, they have to feel proud and happy.

“If you want to leave and you have not found the offer, it’s your problem, not my problem. I give respect, I kiss you, I hug you, but at the end [they] have to stay calm inside the dressing room. And not to speak too much because the rules have been clear.”

De Zerbi said Mohammed Kudus, who has been out since January with a thigh injury, could return to the bench against Newcastle. He added that Micky van de Ven was “right to play” – in other words to start. He will make a decision on whether to start Pedro Porro and Sávio or use them as substitutes. “Marmoush is available to play, maybe also [at] the beginning of the game,” he said.

De Zerbi considered his established, senior options for the front line, excluding No 10s – Kudus, Sávio, Marmoush, Dominic Solanke, Richarlison, Mathys Tel and Wilson Odobert.

“Odobert is injured for a long time [after ACL surgery],” he said. “Before February, March, he is not available. And then maybe one of these players can leave before the end of the window. I think we are not too many players [in this department.]”

De Zerbi made clear he wanted to include Dejan Kulusevski in the squad he submits to the Premier League after the closure of the transfer window. The attacking midfielder last played on 11 May 2025. Spurs are putting no timeframe on his return from a knee problem.
