“I hope and I will be very, very happy to see Kulusevski inside of the list and I want to put Kulusevski inside because he is working very well and he’s a different player,” De Zerbi said. “Also Xavi Simons … before March, April, he’s not ready [after ACL surgery]. Kulusevski feels good, he’s improving day by day. He deserves it because he suffered too much for his age. I’m not speaking of him as a player but as a human.”

De Zerbi said he had paid for the meal with the club’s top brass at an Italian restaurant and he was effusive in his praise of how they have driven an expensive reboot of the squad. Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer – a figure that does include the £50m purchase obligation on Marmoush, which is due next summer. He has joined on an initial loan.

“Really, it’s the first time [in my career] that I didn’t push to complete the squad,” De Zerbi said. “They pushed to build [with] the top players. Johan Lange was brilliant in terms of ideas to make solutions. Also, Vinai. I remember when we closed the Sandro Tonali deal, Vinai made a video call to me when I was on holiday and he had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Cole Palmer is a unicorn in this world inventing moments of pure pleasure | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
This week Central Cee launched his new Premier League song, called The Team. It owes its existence to a youth-centred, fist-bumping corporate tie-in with Coca-Cola, the press release for which appears to have involved a man in golf-casual clothing frowning at his computer screen for half an hour before typing “cool urban street words, what are?” into the AI search box, then nipping off for a quick brain-bowl strategy lunch with Roger from the Bluesky Synergy hub.

The song is really good, because Central Cee is really good. He’s super-smart with words, funny and snappy, but also surprisingly tender and raw.

And yes, this is an oh-no-dad’s-talking-about-rap moment. You can just scroll down if you like. The whole thing moves on to Cole Palmer very quickly, why he’s both the best English footballer and very easy to love currently, for various reasons.

Central Cee is a significant figure, perhaps the biggest British recording artist right now. He’s also oddly raw and fearless in the things he says, in a way that feels distinct from the standard, mannered modern person, and which has got him into trouble at least once.

A few years back there was a furore when Central Cee decided to speak out against sexual prejudice. This sounds as if it should just be fine. Except, Central Cee’s call for tolerance was expressed via a lyric in the song Doja. And that lyric was: “How can I be homophobic? My bitch is gay.”

Hmm. Problems there. What Central Cee is saying here, what Central Cee has done while appearing to express a progressive sensibility, is to introduce an entirely new tier of … Basically what he’s saying is: how can I be homophobic? I’m far too busy being sexist.

This caused understandable offence. The b-word is demeaning and cheap, whatever your intentions. Don’t say it. Find better words. To his credit, Central Cee was very good at explaining and apologising, open to other views, while also seeming genuinely non-judgmental of other people regardless of difference or identity, with the exception, of course, of wastemen, mugs and snitches.

He seems to have been forgiven now. More than that, he’s startlingly successful, the most streamed British rap artist of all time. Young people respond to him hungrily. He seems adaptive, fitted to the modern world. In the Coke video he looks blankly into the lens, gives you everything and nothing, risky but also weirdly fearless.

What does this have to do with Cole Palmer, and the surge of heartfelt Palmer-love across all platforms this week after his brilliant performance against Fulham on Monday?

First, Palmer is good friends with Central Cee. He even turned up at the launch of the Coke song just before Chelsea’s Premier League opener. And Palmer really was sensational at Craven Cottage, twirling about between the defensive lines, all perfect touch and interesting angles.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer was sensational for Chelsea against Fulham at Craven Cottage. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The reaction was significant too. Everyone went wild for this. In particular passionate football men of a certain age went wild. This boy is gold, this boy gets people off their seats, the man in the TalkSport video chair growled, speaking from the gut and the spleen, coming off less like a piece of football analysis, more like a man offering a brave, husky funeral elegy for a very loyal family dog.

This passion does have an edge to it. It is a mark of how hungry we are for something different, a counterpoint to the dominance of systems football, that despite being entirely academy-coded Palmer still seems to be a unicorn in this world.

For the middle-aged proper football man he can look like a flicker of the pre-digital memory, football in the time of maverick authenticity, an age of mud, of landlines, of not wearing a seat belt, of smoking in pubs, of the casually discarded woodland porn mag, of Barry Davies shouting: “Oh, it’s magnificent and can’t they just taste it” while mods throw darts at each other in the background, because old fun is the best fun.

This is, of course, both deluded and incorrect, because football encourages such feelings and because many middle-aged men are already both of these things. But Palmer is genuinely unusual in the modern game. He turns up in strange spaces, finds gullies and currents in between those static pegs.

Right now he is perhaps the only truly creative English player out there, in the sense of inventing the game in front of him, dishing up in those moments the pure pleasure of a story being told in real time.

He even looks a little unusual in an era of hyper‑athletes. Palmer is light and mobile. He can turn with balletic grace. But he also has that gangly, mischievous physicality, like a very clever cartoon alpaca has worked out how to put on a royal blue football kit and run around occasionally doing amusing celebrations.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

From here Palmer will benefit from having a very good club manager who gets his position. At Bayer Leverkusen Xabi Alonso designed an entire team around getting the best out of Florian Wirtz, the “free electron” in the structure.

Beyond this, Palmer is clearly the player the national team should have been configured around after Euro 2024. It made some logical sense not to pick him for the World Cup, because merit and fitness are also important. But Thomas Tuchel simply has to play Palmer, Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane together now, even if you have to pack the team with cement sacks and tins of beans to make it work, because this is just incredibly hot, and there is literally no other point in playing these games.

But it isn’t just the football. Palmer is also just weirdly likable. There is a temptation to cast him as a Lego-haired blank, some kind of urban idiot savant, a human being made entirely from white bread, energy drinks and discarded phone cases. But he’s clearly very smart, and also very modern in his own way.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer’s persona is unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

This is another element of the Palmer persona. He looks unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. But the blankness is a thing, a way of being in the middle of all that glare. Palmer gives you nothing to bite on, no gaps in the armour. He even seems weirdly post-race, or just non-race, some kind of bowl-headed omni-man.

It is both an attitude and a shield of sorts. There’s a thing young people do on the internet, known as Nonchalance. This is all about projecting indifference and impassive facial expressions, appearing comically unbothered while chaotic things happen around you. In the picture with Central Cee at the Coke thing they’re both doing it, staring blankly into the camera open but also closed.

Palmer seems to do this naturally. He will sit with his legs crossed while a group of angry men have an on-pitch brawl nearby. He will have the sense of raw dramatic irony to look genuinely amused on the live TV feed as the referee stands right in the middle of the Chelsea huddle, one of the most comically weird sub-moments of the modern age.

There is a theory nonchalance is a political attitude, a response by the post-Gen-Z demographic to the challenge of making the world you find less incoherent, less intrusive on your space, a blank against the constant wall of noise, dogma and ideological boilerplate hurled your way.

Even the way Palmer plays has a kind of shrug about it, an existential creativity, making up your own patterns, making the world small, you-sized, following the lines in front of you.

One of the best bits of Monday night’s game was his interview after. Sky’s reporter Emma Saunders asked Palmer: “How ready are you for this season?” His response was: “Did you not watch the game?” – which from some old‑school, spam-faced football man might have sounded a bit weird, a bit off on power dynamic, a bit man-woman.

But it really wasn’t that at all. Palmer was already laughing. Saunders laughed back. And it was just a nice moment, banter-stuff, mate-chat, playing the game in front of you. English football has such an interesting figure here, not just a brilliant footballer, but a distinct presence, a way of existing in the middle of all that heat. Let’s try not to break him this time.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 8: Everton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 10th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

With a new manager in charge, the new season brings some fresh optimism for Everton. But nobody associated with the club will be getting carried away. Last season concluded with a respectable eighth-place finish and anything similar again would be considered a solid campaign for a team operating on a relatively small budget. The latest set of financial accounts showed Everton’s wage bill to be five times smaller than Chelsea’s, illustrating the financial gulf between the Merseysiders and those challenging at the top of the Women’s Super League.

There have been positive elements to Everton’s transfer business this summer, not least the arrivals of Jutta Rantala, Noémie Mouchon and Hannah Cain from relegated Leicester City, as well as turning the Slovenia midfielder Zara Kramzar’s loan move from Roma into a permanent deal. Last season’s loan move for Hannah Blundell from Manchester United has also been converted into a permanent transfer, which was revealed in unusual circumstances, with the 32-year-old emerging from a make-shift ‘coffin’ during an amusing walkout at May’s World Sevens Football event in London.

Scott Phelan’s team have a fairly kind start to the season given they begin with back-to-back matches against newly-promoted sides in Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic. Their second home league fixture is against the other promoted side, Birmingham City. In between there are meetings with the sides that finished 10th and 11th last season, in West Ham and neighbours Liverpool. Everton do not face any of last season’s top three teams until November. They will, therefore, be keen to make a fast start and get plenty of points onboard before a tougher-looking run of games either side of the winter break.

Off-field picture

Everton’s women’s team was sold to the men’s parent company, Roundhouse Capital Holdings, last year in a move that was understood to be largely aimed at helping ensure the men’s team’s compliance with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules (PSR). The women’s team train at the Finch Farm complex in Halewood, which they share with the men. It is one of the better-equipped facilities enjoyed by a WSL side.

The manager

Phelan was formally appointed in June after a four-month spell in interim charge, taking over from the sacked Brian Sørensen. This is the 38-year-old former Everton youth midfielder’s first senior managerial job, after coaching within the club’s boys’ academy. Phelan deploys a calm, measured approach and has spoken of his “unbelievable pride” at being given this job.

Star signing

There is a lot of excitement at Everton about Australia forward Holly McNamara, signed from Melbourne City, where she won back-to-back Golden Boot awards in the A-League, on a free transfer. If the 23-year-old can replicate her goalscoring form in the northern hemisphere, Everton could well have a strong season and, with McNamara alongside Cain and Mouchon, the Merseyside club have a completely new-look attack. The England youth centre-back Hannah Silcock has also been snapped up from Liverpool, which looks like a very astute piece of business.

View image in fullscreen Holly McNamara won back-to-back Golden Boots during her time at Melbourne City and has been handed the No 9 shirt at Everton. Photograph: Patrick Snow Jr/Everton FC

Stat attack

Despite having the third fewest shots last season, Everton had the third most from Opta-defined fastbreaks (counterattacks). They also scored the joint-most goals from them (four), but that can only carry them so far. Their attack in regular play needs work.

Set for a breakthrough

The England youth defender Naomi Layzell has arrived on loan from Manchester City and Everton and the Lionesses will be hoping it can be a good year for the fit-again 22-year-old. Layzell came to prominence with a goal against Barcelona in the Women’s Champions League two years ago but has since suffered injury misfortune. There is hope at Everton that Layzell can kick on this season and show why she is potentially a future regular for England’s senior side. She has previously been called up to train with Sarina Wiegman’s side.

What they say

“It’s been a tough pre-season in terms of the physical load and things like that, but that’s great preparation for the season. It’s just so important to get everyone on the same page early on. We want to do as well as we can in terms of getting results and being where we want to be in the table” – Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan

Where are they playing their home games?

The women’s team moved to Goodison Park last summer and will continue to play all of their home games there. They made their debut at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season in a one-off appearance, losing to Manchester United, and while there is no confirmation of when they will next play at the men’s ground, it is understood that is not off the table for the coming campaign.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish told the reason emotional Aston Villa homecoming won’t happen
Sports.content:
Aston Villa won't take Jack Grealish back as he doesn't 'tick the right boxes' for Unai Emery.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino with Grealish's future still uncertain heading towards transfer deadline day.



2 Grealish made over 200 appearances for boyhood club Villa Credit: Getty

A man in demand

Grealish featured in Manchester City's first two games of the season but wasn't among the substitutes for Friday's 4-1 win at Crystal Palace.

And he has been linked with a move away from the Etihad Stadium to a number of other Premier League clubs, including Villa – who he joined aged six and went on to captain before his £100m switch to City in 2021.

New City boss Enzo Maresca hinted that he would give Grealish opportunities this term, but the winger may have to look elsewhere for the kind of playing time he'd like – which might help him revive his England career.



The 30-year-old looked on track to do that during an impressive loan spell at Everton last season, only for his campaign to be cut short by injury in January.

talkSPORT understands Grealish would prefer to join Everton in the event of an exit from the Etihad.



It's also understood that Villa would be interested in bringing him back to Villa Park on loan, while City denied reports of an approach by Sunderland.

Cascarino can't see him fitting the bill for Emery's Villa, however.

Cascarino's Grealish doubt

The former Villa, Chelsea and Republic of Ireland striker told Alan Brazil on talkSPORT Breakfast: "I think the manager [Emery] wouldn't take Jack back.



"I think Unai Emery wants certain players to do certain things and I'm not sure that Jack ticks those boxes."

Brazil didn't seem so sure, replying: "I hate when you have a player with Jack's ability running with the ball, strong on the ball, getting in the box. I hate when people say, 'He's a luxury player'. I hate that.

2 Grealish recorded eight goal contributions in 20 Premier League outings for Everton Credit: Getty

"It takes all to make a team; it takes all different types."

The Ipswich legend noted Grealish's disciplinary issues in the past but stressed how much he endeared himself to Everton supporters.



"I like Jack, I really do. And yeah, he's been a naughty boy in his time, but that was normal when we played. It's different now.

"But look at some of the games he's been absolutely brilliant in. Everton fans really like him."

Moyes reacts

Responding to talk of a return to Merseyside for Grealish, Everton boss David Moyes said ahead of his side's trip to Bournemouth on Saturday: "We are in the recruitment business and we are looking to see if we can bring some players in if possible.

"But there’s no guarantee and to name one person would be wrong. Jack’s not at our club. He was brilliant for us, a great boy, but not for us to talk about because he’s at another club."

Sports.title: Harry Kane offers big contract update as Ballon d’Or chase continues
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has confirmed that he has started talks to extend his deal at Bayern Munich beyond 2027.

The England captain has been a hit with the Bavarian behemoths, winning titles in two of his three seasons so far.

2 Kane hasn't been able to get a goal in his first two games of the season Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old has 98 Bundesliga goals in 95 appearances since his arrival.

Last term's 61 in 51, and his performances with England at the World Cup, have him among the favourites for the Ballon d'Or.

Kane's future with Bayern Munich has consistently been a hot topic with some pundits insisting he should return to the Premier League.

After his breakthrough at Tottenham, he eventually became their record goalscorer with 280 goals in 435 games for the club.

Meanwhile, in the Premier League alone he netted 213, leaving him 47 behind legendary centre-forward Alan Shearer.

But rather than return to England it appears likely he will now extend his time in Germany.

What did Harry Kane say?

"The first meeting started last week," Kane told reporters after Bayern's 5-1 home win over Stuttgart in their Bundesliga opener.

"I'm 33. It's probably going to be, not my last contract. But it's a big contract for me to sign.

"They need to make sure I'm happy. They obviously need to make sure they're happy… There's no panic from either side.

"I'm sure we'll get to a point where both sides are happy."

2 Kane helped England to finish third at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or hunt

Kane must now go on a real tear in the Bundesliga and Champions League if he wants to win the Ballon d'Or.

New Barcelona star Rodri is likely to be his main competition after Spain won the World Cup.

However, should Kane score a host of goals and star in Europe before the ceremony, he could wrestle it away from the ex-Man City man.

In two appearances so far, though, he's yet to score or assist.

In his first outing after the World Cup, he helped Bayern Munich win the German Super Cup.

Meanwhile, in his first league game he put in a brilliant performance as they beat Stuttgart 5-1.

Sports.title: NFL team axe 16 as brutal reality of training camp emerges following roster date rule change
Sports.content:
The Browns have fired the starting gun on the battle for roster spots with the NFL's deadline for 53-player squads fast approaching

In Cleveland it's been all about the quarterback battle, but the reality of the race for an NFL roster place is also hitting home.

Sunday's deadline for all 32 NFL franchises to name their 53-player rosters is fast approaching with the final preseason games taking place.



5 Jack Stoll's future will lie elsewhere after he was among the names cut by the Browns Credit: Getty

5 Todd Monken (C) is preparing for his first season as a head coach Credit: Getty

The Cleveland Browns completed their three-game slate with a win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night.

That game - like most of training camp - threw up another quarterback curveball, but it also gave Cleveland a jump on the rest of the league when it comes to naming their squad.



And on Friday night general manager Andrew Berry and head coach Todd Monken began the process of getting to the roster that will enter the next couple of weeks before the September 13 opener.

Tight End Jack Stoll is the most high-profile name on the list, with his contract terminated from Injured Reserve.



MORE FROM THE BROWNS Shedeur Sanders ruined Pro Bowl and forced embarrassed NFL to cancel 75 years of history

NFL Weekly Newsletter - SIGN UP! talkSPORT is your home for NFL in the UK as we launch our biggest year of coverage yet! 2026 promises to be an epic year for NFL on talkSPORT - and we want you to join us for the ride. MORE INFO & SIGN-UP HERE! This season will be our biggest ever with live commentary of 90+ games, including behind-the-scenes access to international games and all three London fixtures, plus bumper coverage of Super Bowl 61 at SoFi Stadium. Exclusive interviews, hard-hitting opinion, latest front-office drama and top breaking news - all delivered straight to your inbox each week.

The five-year veteran joined the Browns in Free Agency, becoming the fourth stop in his career having been undrafted in 2021 - only to make the Philadelphia Eagles roster.

After signing a deal worth just over $1million, the 28-year is free to join another team having agreed a settlement with the Browns.



Cornerbacks Tre Avery and Tyler Hall also had their contracts terminated, alongside Tackle Tyre Phillips.

In addition 12 further players were waived.

Drew Biber, Jeremiah Byers, Nik Constantinou, Christopher Edmonds, Nate Evans, Coziah Izzard, Patrick Jenkins, Jeremiah McClendon, Izavion Miller, Jamil Muhammad, Ben Patterson and Jermaine Terry II will now seek fresh options.

5 Stoll scored his first touchdown while on the New Orleans Saints last season Credit: Getty

5 Dillon Gabriel's future with the Browns may be decided in the coming days Credit: Getty



Cleveland will also have the option of adding the cut players to their practise squad, should they clear waivers, while they will also be monitoring waivers for the flood of available players.

Teams can name a practise squad of 17 players, although the 17th spot is reserved for international players as part of the International Player Programme.

Who do the Browns face in Week 1?

The Browns begin the regular season with two games on the road - they are in Florida to face Jacksonville in Week 1, before taking on Tampa Bay in Week 2.

5 Deshaun Watson has won the starting quarterback job in Cleveland Credit: Getty



Deshaun Watson has already been named as the starter for the season, but how long he lasts remains to be seen.

The controversial $230m quarterback angered fans with his response to being booed and critics are already suggesting that two games on the road gives the franchise a chance to ease him into the season.

Cleveland are not at home until Week 3, when the Carolina Panthers visit Huntington Bank Field, and the hope from ownership is that he will have played himself into form.

The alternative is Shedeur Sanders, who many feel should be given the start to see what he has learned after a rookie season in which he flashed enough in a handful of starts.



The Browns long-term future at the position is likely to lie in the 2027 NFL Draft, but both Watson and Sanders are certain to make the roster.

Sanders' fellow 2025 draft pick Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green are also in the competition and it remains to be seen what status they take.

Sports.title: Rayan Cherki told Enzo Maresca ‘give me five minutes’ before man-of-the-match display
Sports.content:
Manchester City's Rayan Cherki revealed manager Enzo Maresca wanted to substitute him before his game-changing impact against Crystal Palace.

Cherki continued his fine start to the season with two brilliant second-half goals in Man City's 4-1 win at Selhurst Park, doubling the visitors' lead then restoring their two-goal advantage minutes after Palace had halved the deficit.



2 Cherki has scored three goals in three appearances against Palace Credit: Getty

Cherki steals the show

Erling Haaland also bagged a brace, his first goals of the season, as City made it two Premier League wins from two under new boss Maresca.

But it was Cherki who stole the show under the lights in south London, following up his two assists in City's late comeback victory over Bournemouth on the opening weekend.

Yet he might not have even got the chance to take this game by the scruff of the neck as he did.



"I was playing so badly," the 23-year-old France international said afterwards. "When Enzo wanted to substitute me, I didn't like that."

And perhaps that was a masterstroke from Maresca – it certainly seemed to spur Cherki on.



"I said to the manager, 'Give me five minutes and you won't need to make any substitutions'," he continued. "Then I really had to show that I deserve to play. I had to score or provide an assist. And I managed that."

Cherki's first goal was pure individual brilliance as he waltzed through the Palace defence before slotting a deft, disguised finish past Dean Henderson to make it 2-0.



His second – after Yeremy Pino's wicked free-kick had hit the post and gone in off Gianluigi Donnarumma's back – to put City 3-1 up showcased his ability to find the net from range.

It was the kind of performance that saw talkSPORT's Adrian Durham once remark that the former Lyon man had been 'sent to save football'.

A naughty slip of the tongue

Before being presented with the Player of the Match award by Sky Sports, Cherki caused a bit of a stir with his own assessment of his display.

"My performance was so-so," he reflected. "In the first half, we didn't find the space. I played so s***.



2 Cherki holds himself to high standards Credit: AFP

"I need to show them I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more. I looked at Enzo and I knew I needed to change it for the second half."

Cherki is already halfway to reaching his goals tally from last term, his debut campaign in the Premier League.

He's also up to 14 assists in the competition – only record-breaking Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has provided more since the start of last season.



What's next for City?

City return to action next Saturday when they entertain newly promoted Coventry, before the first Manchester derby of 2026/27 at Old Trafford the following Sunday.

Maresca's men have also found out their opponents for the Champions League league phase.

They'll take on Paris Saint-Germain, Sporting Lisbon, Napoli and AEK Athens at home and face Barcelona, Porto, RB Leipzig and Lens away.

Sports.title: Tottenham reject bid from Premier League rivals for fan favourite one year after signing
Sports.content:
Tottenham reject bid from Premier League rivals for fan favourite one year after signing

Tottenham have reportedly rejected a bid for Kevin Danso from Sunderland.

The Black Cats wanted to land the centre-back on a season-long loan, according to the BBC.

2 Danso played for De Zerbi against Charlton and made an immediate impact with a goal Credit: Getty

News of the offer comes just days after he scored his first goal for Spurs in a 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton Athletic.

The Austrian, who played for his nation at the World Cup this summer, was, though, only a second-half substitute.

Tottenham have embarked on an enormous rebuild this summer and transfers have been coming thick and fast.

No stone has been left unturned by manager Roberto De Zerbi as he seeks to turn the club into European contenders after two Premier League campaigns of relegation battles.

Savio and Omar Marmoush are the two latest signings, with the former getting a goal and an assist on debut against Charlton.

However, the overhaul has also seen two new centre-backs join with Jan Paul van Hecke arriving in a £52million deal from Brighton, while Marcos Senesi comes in on a free transfer from Bournemouth.

And while Cristian Romero finally left the club in a £34.2m move to Atletico Madrid, Danso now finds himself down the pecking order.

He was vital as cover for most of the 2025/26 campaign and was one of Tottenham's steadiest performers when Romero and new captain Micky van de Ven were out through injury and suspension.

Danso first joined Spurs on loan from Lens in January 2025 and helped the club to their Europa League final win.

He came off the bench in the 1-0 triumph over Manchester United to shore up the backline and see the game out.

2 Danso was key for Tottenham in their Europa League win Credit: Getty

His transfer then became permanent that summer in a £20.9m move.

Fans have taken to the defender despite his rotational role with his passion and his determined performances impressing.

However, minutes are likely to be in short supply, as suggested by his cameo role against Charlton.

Realistically, it now appears he is fifth choice centre-back with Ben Davies starting on the left side in midweek, leaving him only ahead of Kota Takai.

Meanwhile, Archie Gray has previously been used there in a pinch, while the club have highly-rated 17-year-old Jun'ai Byfield on the books.

It's unknown if Sunderland will return with another bid for Danso.

Sports.title: $325m stadium court battle forces franchise to settle 40 miles away into temporary home for 2027 season
Sports.content:
NWSL fans will have to wait until 2028 to see Boston Legacy FC's new home at White Stadium.

$325m stadium court battle forces franchise to settle 40 miles away into temporary home for 2027 season

Boston Legacy FC's White Stadium move has been pushed back.

The NWSL expansion franchise hoped to be in the renovated 11,000-seat arena by 2027, but a lengthy court battle delayed construction.

2 White Stadium is having 500 seats added to meet NWSL requirements Credit: Instagram / bostonlegacyfc



A recent ruling has allowed the project to resume despite opposition from some residents and an environmental nonprofit.

It will not be ready until 2028, however, with an alternative venue lined up.

The Legacy will play at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., for the 2027 campaign.

"Throughout this journey, we have been guided by a simple belief: Boston deserves a world-class home for professional women's soccer and youth sports–a home that will shape the future of our club, expand opportunities for Boston Public Schools students, and serve families and communities for generations to come," owner Jennifer Epstein said in a statement.



"We are deeply grateful to our fans, partners, the City of Boston, and Boston Public Schools for believing in this vision and helping us move it forward.

"With certainty now in place, we are excited to continue building our club and our community together at Centreville Bank Stadium in 2027, while keeping our eyes on what has always been the destination: bringing Boston Legacy FC home to White Stadium."



The Legacy have been playing at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough and Centreville Park Stadium while a $325 million renovation to bring White Stadium up to minimum requirements is completed.

Epstein described the renovation as a “transformative project,” which will be “worth the wait” despite “taking longer than we all would have wanted."



NWSL pushes 2027 season to Super Bowl week

It is hoped that the stadium will be ready in fall 2027.

The 2027 season will begin in February -- the league's earliest ever start date and the same week as the Super Bowl.

2 It will also be given a major facelift Credit: Instagram / bostonlegacyfc

"Given the realities of the match calendar in 2027, we tried to think through if we're playing on Super Bowl weekend, how do we try to be a part of the conversation and not separate the sports world, but just aggregate it more around that area?" Carlin Hudson, the NWSL's vice president of strategy, told ESPN.

It will expand to 18 teams and could possibly reach a 34-game schedul3 in 2028.



"We will essentially have the ability to rewrite the entire competition structure," Hudson added.

"I don't expect us to have drastic changes coming into it, just given that we will figure out how we ingest the two new teams.

"But I think we have the ability to look ahead and rewrite it and work collaboratively with potential media partners and the players' association and all of our key stakeholders ahead of that."

Boston is currently 15th of 16th teams in its debut season with five wins from 21 matches.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola set for Liverpool medical in next 24 hours ahead of £123m move to Premier League club: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Malaga push for Everton's Aznou

Malaga are progressing in talks to sign Adam Aznou from Everton.

Sports.title: Lando Norris signs new £30MILLION-per-year deal at McLaren: Reigning world champion commits to Formula One team until 2030
Sports.content:
Lando Norris signs new £30MILLION-per-year deal at McLaren: Reigning world champion commits to Formula One team until 2030

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lando Norris has committed his future to McLaren until at least 2030 in a deal worth up to £30million a year.

The world champion made the news known to his team on Saturday at their factory in Woking and will continue at the organisation that has underpinned his career since he joined their junior programme in 2017 as test and simulator driver.

He has since driven in 163 grands prix – more than any other McLaren driver in history – and taken 13 wins, 18 pole positions and 48 podiums.

Norris, who is 26, will, therefore, continue in tandem with Oscar Piastri, the Australian who signed up to McLaren on a similarly long-term deal last year.

He believes the announcement could boost the team, saying: ‘It’s best for what will motivate them and make them more comfortable and give them a push.

‘So, it’s perfect timing from that perspective. I want them to know that there’s no other place I’d rather be than right here. And that’s a good thought for me to have, but it’s also a very good thought for every individual here in McLaren to have, I hope.’

Lando Norris has committed his future to McLaren, signing a £30million-per-year deal

Norris remains one of the grid’s best-paid drivers, alongside the likes of Charles Leclerc at Ferrari, and perhaps slightly ahead of George Russell at Mercedes.

Lewis Hamilton, at Ferrari, and Max Verstappen, at Red Bull, are Formula One’s chief earners in deals worth £80m a year, perhaps more with bonuses added.

‘I’m open to staying at McLaren for the rest of my career,’ added Norris. ‘I’d be very, very proud at the end of my career to say that has been the case.

‘I’ve not been someone who’s jumped from team to team, or jumped to a potential opportunity to the next potential opportunity.

‘I’ve stuck with McLaren through times when there was a chance in the past to go elsewhere. And I am very happy to just stay where I am.’

Sports.title: Liverpool's imminent £123m signing Bradley Barcola sharpens up before mega-money Anfield switch as barber confirms move is ON - as PSG star travels to Merseyside for medical
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola enjoyed a final trip to the barbers as the French star prepared to head to Merseyside to complete his £123million move to Liverpool. Barcola is set to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours ahead of signing from reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain. Liverpool have agreed an initial £106million fee with PSG, while the deal for the 23-year-old winger will also include up to £17m in add-ons. Barcola is expected to sign a five-year contract. Documents are still to be exchanged between the clubs and details are being arranged for Barcola to travel. The French star's barber signalled preparations were in full flow ahead of Barcola's move to Liverpool, which will be the most expensive signing of the summer transfer window. Barber Enzo Dias, whose studio is located in Paris, shared a video of him trimming Barcola's hair on Friday. Bradley Barcola's barber shared footage of him cutting the French star's hair prior to him travelling to Liverpool to complete a £123m move The arrival of Barcola will be a major boost for Liverpool's new head coach Andoni Iraola Barcola, 23, is set to become the most expensive transfer of the summer window 'Last ride for Bradley Barcola before he leaves,' Dias wrote on Instagram. The video was also captioned 'last cut for Barcola before Liverpool.' Liverpool made a breakthrough with PSG earlier this week after several weeks of negotiations to try to bring down the European champions’ stubborn valuation which started at £145m. Barcola, 23, has been the top target for several months as Liverpool look to replace Mohamed Salah after his move to Trabzonspor. They previously targeted – and had a bid rejected for – Yan Diomande, who ended up at Real Madrid. Negotiations have been led by sporting director Richard Hughes and Fenway Sports Group president Mike Gordon. Barcola came through Lyon's academy but spent the last three seasons at PSG, where he won two Champions Leagues and three Ligue 1 titles. The winger, who played for France at this summer's World Cup and scored against England in the third-place play-off, hit 39 goals in 152 games for PSG.

Sports.title: New Liverpool co-owner spotted at Anfield for first time since leading consortium in buying £1.65billion stake alongside Amazon's billionaire founder Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
New Liverpool co-owner spotted at Anfield for first time since leading consortium in buying £1.65billion stake alongside Amazon's billionaire founder Jeff Bezos

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool's new co-owner Amit Bhatia was spotted at Anfield for the first time since leading a consortium in buying a £1.65billion stake in the football club.

Bhatia's 1892 Holdings this month purchased the minority share in Liverpool, alongside billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos as well as Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

On Saturday, Bhatia - who became Vice Chairman of the club following the investment - was seen in the stands sporting a club tie ahead of Andoni Iraola's first competitive match at Anfield.

Iraola oversaw the Reds' dramatic 2-2 draw with Newcastle at St James' Park last weekend, and is aiming for his first win in the dugout as the Reds face Nottingham Forest.

Bhatia, who was previously director and co-owner of Championship side QPR, was unable to hide his delight at joining the iconic football club.

'It feels incredible,' Bhatia told club media on Friday. 'It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners.

Liverpool's new co-owner was spotted at Anfield for the first time on Saturday afternoon

Amit Bhatia has led a consortium involving Jeff Bezos in purchasing a £1.65billion stake

'We're talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we're talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.

'I'm just the biggest admirer of everything that is associated with this football club, whether it's the history and the culture, the supporters, the journey of this club, the owners in FSG, the management team at Liverpool. There's just so much to admire, so much to frankly be in awe of.

'And so to have the opportunity at this point in time, to hopefully potentially -- I want to just be very clear, subject to all kinds of regulatory approvals that we're going through the process [of] now -- but the simple fact that we've been potentially welcomed in by FSG to be part of such an incredible football club, a historic football club, an iconic football club like Liverpool, frankly it's the stuff of dreams. And it is the greatest honour I think that anybody can have.'

Bhatia is a British-Indian millionaire who worked as an investment banker. His father-in-law, Lakshmi Mittal, is an Indian steel magnate with an estimated net worth of more than £22billion.

"I think again it's very important to emphasise that we're going through a regulatory process. That regulatory process is under way and we have to be incredibly respectful of that process.

"So it's important to say that, number one. Number two, I think it's important to be very clear that this club remains under the ownership of FSG. FSG are the decision-makers and this is their ownership. They have invited us and we're very fortunate to be a partner as a minority alongside them.

"And so my involvement really, or our involvement really, would be in any capacity that FSG felt that we could be useful to them. So, subject to regulatory [approval], in any capacity that FSG wants us to be involved, in any way that they think that we can add value for the betterment of the football club, is how we will make ourselves available at all times.

"We come from different geographies, we come from different professions, and hopefully with that you bring different experiences and ideas, different thoughts. If we are called upon, if there's any area that we have this expertise in or that FSG would like to discuss with us, our thoughts or our involvement, we would absolutely be there.

"We believe that the potential for the football club is still vast ahead of us and we have had some discussions with FSG as to those thoughts.

"And hopefully if everything goes well, our association with the club will also be for a very, very long period of time. And so as and when we can see those opportunities and we feel that they're in the best interests of the football club, as an entire group we'll come together and try to support in the best way that we think we can.

"And so that's very exciting to think about, because as I said, the potential is enormous. And we're very excited to see what the future holds for us in that regard."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo bounces back from half-time hooking by Ange Postecoglou to score winner and extend Al Nassr's perfect start to the season in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo bounced back from being substituted in midweek by Ange Postecoglou by scoring the winner to preserve Al Nassr's perfect start to the new campaign.

Al Nassr had completed a remarkable comeback from two goals down to beat rivals Al Ettifaq 3-2 on Tuesday, with the fightback coming after Ronaldo had been hauled off at half-time.

Ronaldo, however, was in the starting line-up again on Friday night as Al Nassr faced Al Taawoun in the Saudi Pro League.

The reigning champions fell behind in the first half with Mohammed Bassam Al Hurayji putting the visitors ahead.

Samu Costa scored for Al Nassr in first half stoppage time to leave the teams level at 1-1 at the break.

Ronaldo this time remained on the pitch at the start of the second half and struck within five minutes of the restart.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored the winner as Al Nassr maintained their perfect start to the season

Ronaldo scored from close range, flicking in his team-mates' already goalbound effort

Ronaldo was brought off in the closing stages by Ange Postecoglou as Al Nassr won their fourth successive league match to top the early season table

The Al Nassr captain flicked home from close range, turning his team-mate Mohamed Simakan's goalbound shot into the roof of the net.

Simakan appeared shocked by Ronaldo's intervention with his effort already heading into the bottom corner.

Ronaldo's goal proved to be the winner on the night, with the veteran forward having watched the final ten minutes from the bench after being taken off again by Postecoglou as he builds his fitness at the start of the season.

The goal took Ronaldo's career tally to 978, with the 41-year-old hoping to reach four figures before retiring.

The goal also saw Ronaldo become Al Nassr's all-time top goalscorer in the Saudi Pro League having struck 104 times.

His overall total of 131 puts him joint second in the club's list of top scorers in all competitions, some way shy of Majed Abdullah's tally of 259.

'I'm very, very happy,' Ronaldo said post-match. 'It's a great achievement, but it's not just Cristiano's achievement.

'I have to say thank you to my teammates, because without them, this wouldn't have been possible.

'But I'm also very happy for the fans.'

The match was the perfect response to midweek, where Ronaldo had been seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel with his side 2-0 down to Al Ettifaq.

Ronaldo bounced back from being substituted at half-time in midweek, when his team recovered from 2-0 down to win 3-2 without him

Postecoglou had stressed after Al Nassr fought back to win without Ronaldo that the focus should be on his team's efforts to turn the match around.

'I think there’s a bigger story today, and that is that ten men of Al Nassr were unbelievable. That's all you should write about today, everything else doesn't matter,' he said on Tuesday.

'It doesn't matter what team because if you see ten men in those conditions for so long, 2-0 down to come back, that's the only story today.'

Al Nassr are currently top of the early Saudi Pro League table after beginning the season with four wins, while they were also victorious in their opening King's Cup match earlier this month.

Sports.title: Inside the US Open's notorious 'hash court' - which Alexander Zverev once labelled 'Snoop Dogg's living room' - as British stars contend with 'one of the worst' smells at Flushing Meadows
Sports.content:
Inside the US Open's notorious 'hash court' - which Alexander Zverev once labelled 'Snoop Dogg's living room' - as British stars contend with 'one of the worst' smells at Flushing Meadows

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Court 17, which lies close to the border of the Flushing Meadows Corona Park that surrounds the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, is sunken below ground level, and nicknamed ‘the pit’. A recent, cheekier, moniker, bestowed on the court by the Danish media for the floating smell of marijuana which drifts over from the park, is 'hash-banen', or ‘hash court’.

If the Honey Deuce is the US Open’s signature drink, an argument could be made that weed is the tournament’s unofficial signature scent. Long before New York’s legalisation of recreational reefer in 2021, tennis stars who complained about the stench included Martina Hingis, who wondered if someone was ‘smoking some heavy s***’ during her doubles match with partner Flavia Pennetta in 2014. But that was on Grandstand. Court 17, which Alexander Zverev described as ‘Snoop Dogg’s living room’ in 2023, is a different beast altogether.

For British stars stateside, the smell is a challenging wrinkle to grapple with as they fight for their lives on-court.

‘I have experienced it,’ Katie Boulter, who will play American Carol Lee on Sunday, shared. ‘You got down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot.

‘I’m not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on specific courts. I’ve played on (Court 17) before and I did smell it during my match. It’s something that I wouldn’t like to smell in the middle of my match.’

‘I thought today was really bad,’ said Francesca Jones, who qualified on Friday with a win against Joanna Garland on Court 15. ‘Today was one of the worst.

Katie Boulter is among the British stars to have spoken out about the smell of marijuana around Court 17 at the US Open

Smoking is prohibited within the grounds of the US Open, but with the site nestled in the centre of Corona Park, there is no jurisdiction to stop those over 21 having marijuana next to its courts

Francesca Jones described the smell as 'really bad' during her qualifying match on Friday

‘Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round (of qualifiers), and I said to the guy, "is this normal?”.

‘He's like, "Yeah." I was like, "Well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well." This year, I was like, "should I make the same joke?" But no, I was like, “look, lock in, lock in.”’

Smoking of any form is strictly prohibited within the grounds of the US Open, but with the site nestled in the centre of Corona Park, there is no jurisdiction over how private citizens over the age of 21 might enjoy marijuana next to its courts.

‘While we can’t control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this,’ a statement shared by the USTA read. ‘This includes enforcement by our security and guest services teams when they are made aware of any individual that may be smoking, making them aware that although it may be legal in New York, that smoking is not permitted on parks property, including the tennis center.

‘We constantly work with the NYPD and Parks Department, and we believe this has helped to decrease smoking near our fenceline.’

The already-atmospheric 2,500-seater bowl of Court 17 is particularly affected by its position close to the park, but practice courts, and many of the outdoor courts to the south of the complex like Court 15 are also subject to the drifting smell.

‘I’m trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don’t want to... You don’t need distractions,’ Boulter explained. ‘So yeah, I wasn’t a huge fan of it.”

But while Boulter joins fellow stars such as Maria Sakkari, Nick Kyrgios and Casper Ruud to publicly take issue with the aroma, Jones was quick to lean into the funny side.

'Sometimes you know, (it bothers me) - when I'm hallucinating,’ she deadpanned. ‘No, I had a wee giggle to myself, and then I was like, “okay, back to the point.”

The Briton is based in Barcelona, where 'it's legal in groups, and you can smell it everywhere.’

And Jones is not alone in leaning into the particular vibe of the Big Apple’s US Open.

‘It’s New York,’ Harriet Dart said after she defeated her compatriot Heather Watson in qualifying to book her match-up against Peyton Stearns. ‘I feel like everywhere you walk around, it’s everywhere, no?

‘It is what it is. Same for everyone.’

Sports.title: PRINCE NASEEM HAMED: New British boxing heavyweight star Moses Itauma could be as big as Michael Jordan or Tiger Woods... and even better than me!
Sports.content:
Naseem Hamed is late.

It is not, as you might expect, because the former world champion has travelled halfway across the country to meet. He lives 10 minutes down the road from the Fairmont Windsor Park, one of his favourite hotels.

'I'm only late because I live so close,' he jokes. 'What can I say, you know me, I like making an entrance.'

Hamed strolls into the library room in a black T-shirt and black shorts, grabs a cup of tea in a rather more elegant china mug than most people would settle for, and drops into his chair.

There is still a presence about him. A big energy. The kind that made him one of British boxing's biggest stars long before social media existed.

We are here to talk about Moses Itauma, who this weekend will attempt to become the youngest British heavyweight champion in history when he faces Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF title.

Daily Mail Sport sat down with Prince Naseem Hamed to speak about Moses Itauma

Hamed was full of praise for young British superstar Itauma, who is fighting Filip Hrgovic

The pair are facing off for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at London's O2 Arena this weekend

And Hamed has barely settled in before he delivers a verdict that would have been unthinkable for the man who once called himself The Prince.

'I'm going to say something I've never said before. I think Moses is better than me. I haven't said that about many fighters. Actually, I haven't said that about any fighters. But, I think Moses has a very bright future. He is going to be the best that's ever lived.

'Listen, I can't just put him right there in front of every greatest fighter that's ever lived right now. He has to face some challenges and everybody needs a dancing partner in boxing. You know, Muhammad Ali had Joe Frazier, and Thomas 'Hitman' Hearns had Roberto Duran and Sugar Ray Leonard. But, Moses has got the ability to go all the way and beyond.'

And Hamed is talking about more than just boxing. He sees the makings of a sporting star in the mould of the biggest names in the world.

'I've seen Moses has become the face of Nike. Let me tell you something about Nike: they don't really get it wrong too much. They pick the right guys. When they picked Michael Jordan, they chose right. When they chose Tiger Woods, they chose right. They've got Moses now and they've chosen right.'

Think about that for a moment. The Prince Naseem Hamed, a man whose entire persona was built around the certainty that he was the most talented fighter in history, has just volunteered another man for the throne.

He is not saying it because he has been pressed into a comparison or because he is trying to be generous to a young protege. He is saying it because, having watched Itauma, he genuinely believes it.

'I've always waited for somebody to come along that I could say is going to be better than me,' he says. 'And I can honestly look at Moses and just think, yeah, this guy's the one. There is no one else I could even think about saying that about.'

So why Itauma?

Hamed points to something beyond the knockouts.

'He's more of a correct and complete fighter compared to what I was. Mine was a natural force of ability. It was all ad-lib. You didn't know what was going to happen, it was one of a kind and although Moses has that too, I think he's more calculated. More correct. His speed is blinding for somebody who's six foot four. He's so light on his feet, can move and has got blistering speed. Then there is the power. That's why it's going to be really hard for anybody in the sport of boxing today to get anywhere near him.'

Now Itauma has the chance to show the world why Hamed is so convinced.

At 21 years and seven months, he is only fractionally older than Hamed was when he challenged Steve Robinson for the WBO featherweight title. Hamed went into that fight 19-0 with 17 knockouts, having boxed 68 professional rounds.

Itauma is 14-0 with 12 knockouts and has boxed just 31 rounds.

It is an extraordinary lack of experience for a man about to fight for a world heavyweight title, particularly against Hrgovic.

The Croatian is 34, has won 20 of his 21 fights and stopped 15 opponents. His only defeat came against Daniel Dubois. He is bigger, older and vastly more experienced than most of the men Itauma has faced.

And there is a question hanging over the unbeaten Brit: what happens when somebody finally makes him uncomfortable?

Hamed had to answer it himself against Kevin Kelley in New York.

It was Hamed's US debut, with HBO heavily promoting his arrival and plastering his face across Times Square. But instead of the quick finish he had expected, Kelley dropped him three times - only for the Brit to rise each time and win.

Itauma has never faced that kind of adversity. He has not boxed beyond the sixth round and, after stopping his last two opponents inside five rounds, has spent barely sixteen minutes in the ring over his last two outings.

Hamed knows there is no way of predicting how someone will react when they are finally forced into that territory but believes Itauma is equipped to handle it.

'I've always said you don't know how somebody is going to react until they get hit with a huge shot.

'Everybody talks about Moses not having enough rounds, but I didn't have loads of rounds either. We both didn't have that learning phase in the same way a lot of fighters do.

'With the Kelley fight, it was the first time I found myself in that sort of situation really and I dealt with it. I got knocked down, I got back up and I won the fight. That's experience in itself.

'Of course I'd love Moses to have more experience. I'd love him to go through those hard rounds and learn what fighters normally learn. But boxing is about levels.

'And when you're already on the level Moses is on, you don't necessarily need to go through everything everybody else has gone through to get where you're going.'

Hamed (pictured in 1999) finished his career with a record of 36 wins and one defeat

Hamed believes Itauma is better than he was and argued the young Brit could become as big a sporting star as the likes of Michael Jordan and Tiger Woods

Hamed points to Itauma's demolition of Dillian Whyte as evidence.

Whyte was 36 and well past his best when they met, but he was still a former world title challenger with years of heavyweight experience and a record that included fights with Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury.

Itauma took him apart in just a few minutes.

'Who would have thought that the fight with Dillian Whyte, with all his experience and with the trouble that he gave AJ and everything else, was going to be such a one-sided fight over in, I don't know, minutes?'

There is another part of Itauma that Hamed keeps returning to.

His humility.

'I love the fact of how humble he is,' Hamed says. 'His parents must have brought him up to be the man that he is today, because it shows. And he's a breath of fresh air in boxing.'

That matters because the attention around Itauma is already enormous.

Frank Warren, Hamed's old promoter, has called him the most talented boxer he has worked with at that age - even more talented than Hamed - and the nation are already crowning him the next face of British boxing.

Hamed knows what it is like to be placed under that kind of spotlight, so I ask him whether the expectations ever weighed on him. His answer is characteristically Hamed.

'I didn't know what pressure meant. I never felt pressure. I didn't understand pressure. I couldn't even spell it.

'So, I never felt that I was that type of guy to let things like that get under my skin, or be nervous, or feel pressure in any way.

'And we always say pressure makes diamonds, so I don't think that's going to happen with Moses.'

It was a different time in British boxing, but Hamed was not alone in carrying the weight of expectation. Ricky Hatton, who was on the undercard against Kelley that night in New York, would go on to become one of the biggest names in the sport alongside Hamed.

'I loved everything about Ricky. Ricky was a people's person. I never, ever saw support for a fighter in this country the way they loved Ricky. The amount of people that used to come out to Vegas to watch him fight, there was too many people! He just took over everything.

'When he'd fight in Manchester, there'd be over, I don't know, 50,000. We never saw crowds come out like that for any fighter in the history of boxing in the UK. Ricky had something special in regards to the love in people's hearts, how he made people feel and how he was just one of the boys, and just how genuine he was. He'd say what he felt, similar to myself.

'But he was an exceptionally good fighter. He was an amazing body puncher, and he did unbelievable in his career. He's one of the fighters that we can all say will go down in history as one of the best fighters this country has ever produced.

'It was just so sad to find out when we did about him. God bless him and his family. His family, I can't even imagine what they've been through and what they're going through. He's sadly missed. He'll never be forgotten, and he lit up Manchester in a way that nobody did.'

Itauma (right) is 14-0 with 12 knockouts and has boxed just 31 rounds in his career (pictured in action against Ilja Mezencev in May 2024)

Itauma will hope to prove Hamed right when he takes on Hrgovic in the much anticipated bout

For all the memories, the conversation brings Hamed back to the present and to his frustration that two of Britain's biggest current stars have chosen to take their long-awaited showdown away from the fans who helped make them.

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury look set to meet at Madison Square Garden on November 20, but Hamed thinks the fight belongs somewhere else.

'I think that's a UK fight. I think that's a big UK fight, and I think it should sell out Wembley. Madison Square Garden is an amazing place, and it's history, isn't it? And it will always be history in the making for any big fight.

'But I would prefer to watch that fight on our own soil, in London, and I think the British public deserve that to be in this country. You've got great British fighters that had a huge name in boxing a little bit before now, but in my eyes, that fight's better to be in London than in the States and in New York.'

As for who wins, even Hamed refuses to make a definitive call.

'That's a good question. I think any of them can win. For me, if Tyson Fury fights like he did against Wilder the first or the second time, it's going to be hard for AJ to beat that kind of guy.

'But we don't know who we have today in regards to Tyson Fury and where he's really at, and we don't know which AJ we have, especially after his last fight and everything he's been through.

'Look, it's going to be a big fight. Is it around about three, four, maybe five years too late. But regardless, I think the British public still want to see it.'

And that, ultimately, is why Hamed's excitement about Itauma feels so significant. He remembers what it was like when British boxing had fighters who could command the attention of an entire country. He believes Itauma could be the next one.

There is only one thing left for Itauma to do: prove him right.

Sports.title: How to fix Liverpool's leaky midfield: Snap up a new No 6, the unpalatable Florian Wirtz option, change the roles of Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong or bring in the academy kid who lit up pre-season
Sports.content:
How to fix Liverpool's leaky midfield: Snap up a new No 6, the unpalatable Florian Wirtz option, change the roles of Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong or bring in the academy kid who lit up pre-season

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Liverpool may be on the verge of splashing over £100m on their Mo Salah replacement with the French wonder winger Bradley Barcola on his way through the door, but he won't solve their midfield muddle.

The lack of a No 6, a screen, a player to snuff out danger and do the dirty work was glaringly obvious at Newcastle last week. It is a problem for new boss Andoni Iraola as he tries to get his feet under the table at Anfield.

During game one of the new regime, that Liverpool weakness, that openness in the centre of the park, was laid bare - a continuation of the problem that plagued Arne Slot and ultimately led to him losing his job.

For Newcastle’s first goal, Ryan Gravenberch tried a pass at the edge of the penalty area he was attacking. The Dutchman lost possession and, seconds later, the home team were on the charge. With one pass, they bypassed the midfield and were clean through on Liverpool’s two central defenders, with the full backs busting a gut to recover. Gravenberch and midfield partner Dominik Szoboszlai? Nowhere to be seen.

Later in the game, Gravenberch again lost possession at the edge of the box. This time, there were bodies for Yoane Wissa to get through – which he did too easily – but again, within seconds, Liverpool went from a promising attack to being vulnerable and exposed. Gravenberch, Szoboszlai and fellow midfielder Florian Wirtz? Jogging back.

The response to the game has been loud cries of ‘sign a defensive midfielder’ from fans and pundits including Daniel Sturridge and Jamie Carragher on Sky Sports. It formed the basis of Daily Mail Sport’s match analysis and was the talking point in Iraola’s post-match press briefing.

But is it as simple as that? And what are the other options to fix this midfield mess?

Yoane Wissa makes his way through the wide open spaces in the Liverpool midfield at St James' Park as Ryan Gravenberch gives chase

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola shows his displeasure during the 2-2 draw

SIGN A NEW No 6

This is not an overreaction based on one game of football. They have needed a No 6 since Fabinho left in 2023.

That summer, they had tried to sign Romeo Lavia, then of Southampton, and Moises Caicedo, then of Brighton. Both moved to Chelsea.

They ended up signing a stop-gap option in Wataru Endo, who arrived from Stuttgart on Deadline Day. The Japan international is the only specialist No 6 at the club but very rarely plays there and is often used as back-up in defence. He is also 33 and not a long-term solution.

Jurgen Klopp cobbled something together with Alexis Mac Allister, Curtis Jones and Trent Alexander-Arnold also playing in the holding role in a season where they made a fair title charge until it fizzled out in mid-March. The next summer, a deal for Real Sociedad and Spain No 6 Martin Zubimendi was advanced and Slot had spoken to the player. He decided to stay put and ultimately ended up at Arsenal a year later.

Slot found a revelation in pre-season as he converted the lesser-seen Gravenberch into a holding midfielder. He and Mac Allister formed a formidable duo on and off the ball as Liverpool romped to the Premier League title.

But it all fell apart from there as neither could sustain that level going into last season. Mac Allister, privately, was taken aback by some of the criticism he received but he seemed to struggle physically for the entire campaign. Jones’s exit this summer further compounds the lack of numbers in the position.

So, will they sign a defensive midfielder this summer? The messaging all window has been clear: wide attack is the priority – not a new No 6.

Lamine Camara at Monaco is a name that has circled in the last 24 hours – with Chelsea also said to be linked – but the word from Liverpool sources remains the same: The Reds are not in the market for midfielders. And that will only change if another midfielder leaves.

Liverpool have been trying to solve their No6 problem for ages and thought they had when they lined up Martin Zubimendi. He opted to stay at Real Sociedad, however, before joining Arsenal

Chelsea's Romeo Lavia is another midfielder Liverpool tried, and failed, to sign

DROP MEGA-MONEY WIRTZ

Given the £116m fee paid for Wirtz last year, this one will not go down well. It cannot be a long-term solution either.

But pushing Szoboszlai higher and having a more solid base achieves two things: it allows the Hungary star to have more of an attacking input and should, in theory, mean a double-pivot to shield the defence.

Iraola wants Wirtz and Alexander Isak to work in tandem up top and he will certainly not write them off after one sub-par game in the hostile environment of Newcastle. There are huge hopes for Wirtz this coming year.

One unpalatable option for Liverpool is to drop their big-money signing Florian Wirtz

TRUST THE IRAOLA PROCESS

It’s not like football fans to overreact, is it?

After five games last season, Liverpool looked likely to storm the league but their form fell off a cliff. Iraola was brought to the club because of his proven track record to improve players. Look at the likes of Antoine Semenyo, Milos Kerkez, Dean Huijsen, Ilya Zabarnyi as examples of those he took from unproven to big-money sales.

Tyler Adams, Eli Junior Kroupi and Rayan may also bag big sums for Bournemouth in the not-too-distant future, though the Cherries are keen to back Marco Rose as much as possible this season and are unlikely to sanction a sale for one of their big attackers.

Iraola insists it is not a personnel problem that plagued his midfield last weekend – and there is no guarantee a new signing would aid that. With time, the Basque will hope to solidify the issue.

Iraola wants his players to be front-footed and believes, over the course of a season, the positives outweigh the negatives.

CHANGE FORMATION COMPLETELY

Here’s a rogue one that has been suggested this week: Iraola should change to a different system altogether.

Jeremie Frimpong and Kerkez have struggled as full backs but what if they were wing backs with less defensive responsibilities? Wirtz’s best form came in a 3-4-2-1 formation under Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen.

This one is more of a fan hope than a realistic possibility, though. Otherwise their summer-long pursuit of wide forwards would be redundant – and the club also identified Iraola because he played a system similar to that which the squad is accustomed.

Another option is to convert full backs Milos Kerkez (above) and Jeremie Frimpong into wing backs - and bolster the middle of midfield with a 3-4-2-1 formation

GIVE THE KIDS A GO

Trusting youth players is in Iraola's identity. At his boyhood team Athletic Club, there is a long-standing policy to only have Basque players in the squad. They cannot go out and spend mega-money on a transfer target, but instead have to work with what they already have at their disposal.

Keeping this in mind, 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni will be given chances to impress. The young Englishman played just 21 minutes in the Premier League last term but was a star of pre-season and deserves more chances in the coming weeks.

The 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni impressed during pre-season for Liverpool

He is small in stature but plays with a maturity beyond his years. Daily Mail Sport has been present for many of his youth-team appearances where he showed he is an elegant midfielder who always demands possession and can dictate play from deep.

Nyoni can certainly push for minutes this term.

Another back-up option is academy graduate James McConnell. He spent the first half of last season at Ajax and the second half on the treatment table. But he is fit now and has been asked to stick around. He had agreed a loan move to Preston North End but that has been put on the back-burner for now at least.

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan and ex-EastEnders star wife Laila Rouass make announcement with X-rated message
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan and ex-EastEnders star wife Laila Rouass make announcement with X-rated message

Snooker icon Ronnie O'Sullivan and his wife promised to reveal all in a new announcement

View 3 Images Laila Rouass and Ronnie O'Sullivan have set up a joint Instagram page (Image: Getty Images)

Ronnie O’Sullivan and his actress wife Laila Rouass announced they have created a joint Instagram account in an X-rated post. The snooker legend married the former EastEenders star in June 2025 after a long on-and-off relationship dating back to 2012.

‌



The couple began dating over a decade ago and got engaged in 2013. However, their most recent split came in September 2024, before reconciling in the following January.

‌



The Rocket officially tied the knot last year in a low-key ceremony at St George’s Town Hall in Shadwell, East London, where Rouass grew up. And it appears the seven-time world snooker champion, 50, is ready to take his relationship to another level.

‌



Rouss, 55, and her husband recently launched a joint Instagram account, under the username ‘TheOSullivans’, which they hope will give fans a glimpse into his life away from snooker. The pair uploaded a snap of the two of them together for the first post.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gloomy Ronnie O'Sullivan sets retirement deadline after another sloppy performance READ MORE :

They captioned it: “Hi. Welcome. This is us. Unfiltered, uncouth, unhinged and unplanned. No inspirational quotes from us. No feigned positivity. No more f***s to give. Follow along if it sounds like your kind of thing. Laila & Ronnie.”

‌



World No.14 O’Sullivan also called for his fans to follow the new account by taking to Instagram Stories. He teased what can be expected on the new social media account, writing: “It’s all unplanned and unedited. All we do is eat tbh. See you there.”

The account has already racked up close to 6,000 followers. Their stories so far have included a look into their stay in China, where O’Sullivan has been for five weeks playing in various snooker tournaments.

3 View 3 Images O'Sullivan and Rouass made an X-rated announcement (Image: Instagram: @ronnie) 3 View 3 Images The couple married last year
