Sports.title: Featured Comment: Reintroducing refuelling would bring more negatives than positives | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses are right to argue Mohammed Ben Sulayem’s plan to reintroduce refuelling would create more negatives than positives, says reader @Stefmeister:

I wasn’t a fan of refuelling in F1 the last time and I wouldn’t be in favour of it returning.

I just always felt that it was more detrimental to the racing and never really liked the impact it had on how the races played out or how it impacted strategies.

Refuelling was always more planned and easier to read and predict with less room to adapt and change what you were doing based on how your race was playing out or what those around you were doing. You came up with a strategy the day before, went into the first stint with say 20 laps of fuel and with little room to alter that stint length the rest of your race had to be based off that.

Before and after when it was just about tyres things are a lot more reactive, harder to plan, harder to predict and you have a lot more room to change things on the fly based off how your race and what those around you are doing.

Today you can start a race looking to stop on lap 20 but if your tyres are wearing less than expected then you have scope to go a lot longer which you don’t have with refueling because if you put 20 laps of fuel in then you can’t go much longer without doing massive fuel saving.

And drivers in general have less input with refueling because yes they can do things to save fuel but they are still limited by how much was put in the tank. With tyres they can do more to extend, They can have input on changing strategy and can ask to go long if they feel tyres are holding on et cetera…

Just overall for me refueling introduces far more negatives than positives and I’d hate to see it come back.

@Stefmeister

Sports.title: Alpine confirm Colapinto will remain alongside Gasly in 2027 line-up | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Alpine has confirmed Franco Colapinto will remain at the team next year for what will be his second full season in Formula 1.

The 23-year-old joined the team last season, replacing Jack Doohan from the seventh round of the season in Miami. He ended the season point-less as Alpine struggled throughout the year with an uncompetitive car.

He has enjoyed more success this year, his first full season as an F1 driver, taking his best result so far with sixth place in the Canadian Gerand Prix. Colapinto has scored 19 points so far, putting him 12 in the championship, two places behind team mate Pierre Gasly.

The pair will remain team mates next year. “For me, having consistency is very important,” said Alpine’s executive consultant Flavio Briatore. “We are now settled from a driver point of view and I have said many times that, while this is an important piece of the puzzle, the most significant we have to get right is designing and building a fast race car which absolutely remains our number one priority.

“We have seen Franco truly grow and mature into a great driver this year. His results in Miami and Montreal especially confirmed what I already knew: Franco belongs in Formula 1 and he belongs at this team.”

Colapinto said he is “very pleased” to renew his contract with Alpine. “I feel very happy and very settled here and it’s been even better that we have made significant progress this year compared to last.”

He made his F1 debut in 2024 at Williams, replacing Logan Sargeant after the Dutch Grand Prix. The Alpine driver is the only Argentinian to race in F1 over the last 20 years and the team arranged a show run for him in Buenos Aires in April.

Sports.title: Mercedes told Antonelli he would get F1 chance before Hamilton’s exit was announced | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli has revealed how quickly Mercedes reacted to Lewis Hamilton’s decision to leave the team at the beginning of 2024.

The world championship leader said he first learned Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff intended to promote him to the team before Hamilton’s decision to join Ferrari was announced.

Ferrari announced Hamilton would join them in February 2024. Antonelli said Mercedes told him of their decision shortly beforehand.

“It’s 2024, the year I’m turning 18, it’s February, I was in Silverstone,” he said in a recent interview for one of the team’s sponsors. “I was testing Formula 3 to learn the track, because I was going to race there with Formula 2.

“I remember at the end of the day, Toto called me over to his office. And already there, I was a bit confused, because I’m like, [this] doesn’t really happen.

“So I got into his office. Obviously, it’s Toto, there’s Rosa [Herrero Venegas, PR manager] and she’s the one helping me during race weekends.

“Toto, first of all, didn’t waste any time, went straight to the point and it was like this was even before Lewis was announced. To Ferrari. So he said, look, Lewis is going to Ferrari and we were thinking to put you in the car for next year. And I’m like, ‘whoa’.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli had won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before. “My eyes were wide open and I was like, ‘are you kidding me?’ Because I hadn’t even started F2.

“So I had still so much to prove that I could earn that spot. And Toto was already talking about it.”

Wolff asked Antonelli if he would be ready for the opportunity. “I said, yeah, I’ve got to be ready,” Antonelli recalled.

Mercedes began a programme of F1 tests for Antonelli that year, culminating in his first appearance in an official practice session at Monza. Although Antonelli crashed five laps into the session, the following day Mercedes announced he would take Hamilton’s place in 2025.

However Antonelli had already learned of Mercedes’ decision long before that weekend.

“The official announcement came just at the start of summer break. It was, I think, just the start of August, probably, first day of August. I was at home with my family, and Toto organised this call, and where there were also all the big names from Mercedes.

“There was James Allison [technical director], Gwen Lagrue, who was the one who took me in the junior programme. There was Bradley [Lord], Rosa again, there was all of the big ones. Toto in the call went straight to the point and said he’s going to be our driver for next year. And it was an incredible moment.”

Sports.title: Why F1 team bosses believe refuelling “doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has suggested reintroducing refuelling to Formula 1 as a means of making the cars run at a lower weight.

However three bosses asked about the proposal are not convinced it would improve the racing.

Racing Bulls team principal Peter Bayer, who previously worked as the FIA’s secretary general, said the idea has been studied recently and found wanting.

“When I was still working with the FIA, we had a working group with Formula 1, with Ross Brawn [former F1 sporting director] back in the days, and his team, about how to improve the entertainment, the spectacle.

“One of the big ideas of some people was refuelling. We were digging very deep into historic footage, data that we had, and it showed that other than a couple of very spectacular and dangerous images, refuelling has not done really anything for the sport because most of the overtaking suddenly took place in the pit lane. So I wouldn’t be a big fan of that because it’s proven that it actually doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle.”

Refuelling also adds complexity for fans who are trying to follow the races, said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

“I’m personally not a big fan of refuelling, really,” he said. “When I was watching from outside, refuelling, it’s just that the race was so difficult to understand as a spectator sitting on the stand.

“Also in terms of qualifying, et cetera. I’m fond of a qualifying car being the lightest, the driver going for everything. So in short, I’m not fond of refuelling – and also the weight and cost and everything – I’m not a big fan.”

Williams team principal James Vowles, who previously headed Mercedes’ strategy division, pointed out that refuelling would take a lot of the intrigue away from pit stops.

“We could fundamentally predict exactly where the car is going to stop. You’re always going to take the car right to the end of its fuel load because that’s when it’s its fastest, which now means you can predict what’s going to happen, whether someone’s on a two or three or one, it doesn’t matter.

“Nowadays, with the exposure to the outside world, everyone will start getting that information. It actually takes quite a bit of the intrigue out of it for me.”

However he said he is in favour of trying to reduce the weight of the cars. “I’m completely in support of that,” he said. “I think going back to refuelling is not the right solution for it, however.

Vowles also admitted to having a personal reason to oppose refuelling. “It’s quite warm wearing a race suit when you’re on the pit wall, so I’d prefer not to do that again!”

Sports.title: John L. Sullivan Wins Disputed Title From Dominick McCaffrey
Sports.content:
That distinction allowed the show to proceed. It did nothing to produce an orderly championship.

Sullivan Had 40 Pounds on McCaffrey

Sullivan was 26 and weighed approximately 208 pounds. The 21 year old McCaffrey came in near 168, leaving the smaller Pittsburgh boxer to handle a massive physical disadvantage.

McCaffrey could not trade directly with Sullivan’s heavier rushes. He used footwork, slips and clinches to interrupt the larger man before another full attack developed. After injuring his right hand, McCaffrey relied heavily on his left and defensive positioning, turning survival into a technical exercise rather than a test of strength.

Sullivan was the recognized American bare knuckle champion, but his preparation left him tiring as the fight progressed. McCaffrey’s camp also believed Sullivan needed a knockout within the scheduled six rounds to win. Surviving accounts differ over what the signed agreement actually required.

Sullivan supplied the heavier blows. One shot to the side of McCaffrey’s head dropped him during the middle rounds. McCaffrey later claimed he broke his right hand against Sullivan’s head in the third and completed the fight using primarily his left.

The larger man began fading late. McCaffrey pressed him and remained ready to continue. A timekeeping mistake ended the sixth after approximately one minute, prompting referee William Tate to order another round to replace the missing fight time. That explains the peculiar result listed by BoxRec: Sullivan won on points in round seven of a six round fight.

A Championship Born Under Protest

Tate awarded Sullivan the decision based on the greater number of clean blows. McCaffrey’s camp protested, maintaining that lasting six rounds entitled him to a draw. The absence of an athletic commission left no independent authority to settle the disagreement. The promoter controlled the money, the referee’s interpretation determined the result, and McCaffrey’s only remaining option was a lawsuit.

The crowd treated McCaffrey’s survival as a moral triumph. Sullivan still collected nearly $6,000, representing approximately 60 percent of the gate, while McCaffrey received far less.

Sullivan became recognized as boxing’s first gloved heavyweight champion, yet the sport had not suddenly become modern merely because the fighters wore gloves. The disputed terms, confused timekeeping and uncertain ruling showed that Queensberry rules had arrived before boxing possessed a reliable system for enforcing them.

Sullivan later retained his bare knuckle claim by defeating Jake Kilrain over 75 rounds in 1889. James J. Corbett finally took the gloved championship from him in 1892. McCaffrey continued boxing larger opponents, later becoming an instructor and police officer while insisting for the rest of his life that Sullivan had never properly beaten him.

Sports.title: Healthy Hrgovic Ready To Test Itauma’s Experience
Sports.content:
Sanchez is not designing the strategy around landing one perfect heavyweight punch. He wants Hrgovic to force Itauma into situations the 21-year-old has avoided during a carefully controlled climb through the division. Itauma’s lack of professional rounds gives Hrgovic an area to attack. The young southpaw has usually removed opponents before a fight develops, while Hrgovic completed 12 physical rounds with Zhang.

If Hrgovic absorbs the initial assault, Itauma must handle his pace and maintain his speed against a heavyweight who will continue forcing exchanges. The Croatian’s right hand also provides a direct weapon against Itauma’s southpaw stance. Itauma has shown a tendency to retreat in straight lines when opponents reach him, leaving room for Hrgovic’s straight right or the heavier shot over the lead shoulder. Itauma’s hand speed may let him control the early exchanges, but pulling back with his head upright becomes more dangerous against a puncher of Hrgovic’s size.

Before turning professional, Itauma had limited amateur experience. Sanchez described his previous opposition as “selected opponents” and called Hrgovic his first top 5 or top 10 heavyweight.

Sanchez believes the hype machine crowned Itauma before he deserved it, giving Hrgovic every reason to ruin the party. The plan does not involve giving away early rounds while waiting for the youngster to fade. He wants Hrgovic taking the fight to Itauma from the first bell.

Itauma has never shared the ring with someone carrying Hrgovic’s physical size, battle-tested chin, or professional pedigree. If the quick stoppage eludes him, the young prospect will have to demonstrate real staying power against a foe who stands his ground.

Moses Itauma Shoves Hrgovic Off Weigh-In Stage

Moses Itauma initiated an ugly weigh-in clash today by shoving Filip Hrgovic backward and off the stage before their vacant IBF heavyweight title fight at London’s O2 Arena.

After regaining his balance, Hrgovic stepped forward and slapped Itauma across the face with his right hand. Itauma tried to reach the Croatian heavyweight, but security and members of both teams held the fighters apart.

Itauma started it by pushing Hrgovic off the edge of an elevated stage, where a bad landing carried more danger than anything likely to happen during a standard staredown. He was upset about Hrgovic stepping in front of him, partially for a double-biceps pose. It was pretty harmless stuff, but Itauma got heated enough to shove Hrgovic while his back was turned.

Hrgovic Exposes Itauma’s Temper

Hrgovic repeatedly labeled Itauma a protected “golden child” steered carefully toward this title opportunity. The way that Itauma lost his temper today was a signal that Hrgovic’s comments have gotten to him.

The reaction exposes genuine vulnerability. Confident fighters shrug off verbal insults, flash a grin, and settle business inside the ropes. Instead, the 21-year-old met a standard pose with physical aggression, proving his patience snaps the moment he feels slighted.

Hrgovic now holds a clear psychological target. If he roughs up Itauma on the inside, leans hard during clinches, and turns early rounds into a grueling dogfight, the young puncher must avoid unraveling into reckless mistakes.

Itauma hit the scale at 241.7 pounds, while Hrgovic came in trim at 236.2. The scale numbers do not dictate tactics outright, but the Croatian’s lean conditioning favors an active plan built on movement, straight right hands through the southpaw guard, and non-stop pressure.

Itauma has not faced incoming fire from anyone carrying Hrgovic’s rare blend of size, physical power, and battle-tested experience. The opposition fed to the young prospect so far sits firmly in the journeyman category, save for a 38-year-old, faded Dillian Whyte.

Hrgovic has already faced monstrous punchers, absorbing full-force bombs from Zhilei Zhang and trading heavy artillery with Daniel Dubois. Shoving someone off an elevated stage is simple. Keeping composure once Hrgovic connects with clean right hands will prove whether Itauma is truly ready for the elite level.

Sports.title: Benn’s Lack Of Real Power Spells Trouble Against Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Benn has not stopped an opponent since his second-round win over Chris van Heerden in April 2022. His five subsequent fights have covered 56 rounds, producing four decision wins and one decision loss. He dropped Chris Eubank Jr twice in the final round of their rematch, showing that he can hurt an opponent, but the fight still reached the scorecards.

That record supports Malignaggi’s boxing argument without proving anything about the testing case. Benn carries enough power to get an opponent’s attention, but Malignaggi does not consider it heavy enough to compensate for the difference in skill or prevent Garcia from waiting on the counter.

Benn Must Survive Garcia’s First Counter

Benn’s usual pressure may bring him directly into Garcia’s most dangerous punch. He tends to attack in straight lines and does not always disguise his entry with feints, head movement, or a jab. Garcia needs only a small opening to release the left hook while Benn is stepping toward him.

Such a punch is harder to see than a hook thrown during a stationary exchange. Benn will be moving into its force, increasing the damage while reducing his time to react. Malignaggi does not expect Garcia to overwhelm him with a long combination. He sees one fast counter changing the fight.

Returning to 147 pounds adds another concern. Benn has not made the welterweight limit since 2022. He boxed Chris Eubank Jr twice near the middleweight limit and weighed 149½ pounds against Regis Prograis in April. Those extra 2½ pounds do not sound substantial, but removing them after several years at higher weights may affect his stamina, reactions and ability to absorb Garcia’s counters.

A change in approach can make the entry less predictable. Feints and lateral steps would make it harder for Garcia to time the left hook. Repeating the same straight attack gives the faster puncher a clear target.

Ryan also creates opportunities once the distance closes. He often retreats in straight lines with his chin raised when placed under pressure. If Benn can reach his chest without absorbing the first counter, he can drive Ryan toward the ropes and force him to fight at close range.

Close quarters favor Benn’s physical style. He can attack the body, use his shoulders, and keep Garcia from setting his feet. Garcia’s defense becomes less reliable when an opponent prevents him from controlling the punching distance.

The difficulty is getting inside repeatedly. Garcia had roughly 200 amateur fights, while Benn’s amateur career consisted of only about 20. That difference gave Garcia far more time to learn distance, rhythm and shot selection before turning professional. Benn has gained experience during his professional career, but adjustments under pressure may still favor the fighter with the deeper foundation.

Targeting the body may help take some speed from Ryan. Benn will need patience rather than immediately reaching for the head once exchanges begin. Reckless pressure gives Garcia exactly the rhythm Malignaggi believes will produce the knockout.

Motivation and concentration remain the qualification in Malignaggi’s pick. Garcia has delivered different versions of himself based on his preparation and mental state. The focused version possesses enough speed, timing and power to expose Benn’s defensive openings.

Surviving the initial counters would make the contest more favorable to Benn. Ryan can lose discipline over 12 rounds, tire from repeatedly loading up and grow frustrated when an opponent refuses to break. Benn’s work rate and physical pressure then become more valuable during the later rounds.

Toughness alone will not protect Benn during the first exchanges. Garcia does not have to be the busier fighter or hold his ground for the full distance. One repeated aggressive entry may be enough to bring the counter Malignaggi expects.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Picks Mbilli To Overwhelm Canelo
Sports.content:
“I get the competitiveness of Canelo, and I respect it because lately I haven’t really respected a lot of his opponent choices. I respect the move that he’s making, but it’s a tough fight, and at 36, that kind of pace, I don’t think it’s something he can handle.” “I don’t think Canelo beats him. Pace is the worst thing for Canelo. I think Canelo is more skilled than Mbilli, but when you couldn’t handle a fast pace in your prime, a fast pace like that at 36 years old is tough. Mbilli makes up for his lack of skills with his pace. He’s not here because of his skills. I don’t know if Canelo can offset that pace. I really don’t,” said Malignaggi to Fight Hub TV.

The age difference alone does not decide the fight. What favors Mbilli is his willingness to keep working after the first combination. Alvarez has become increasingly selective with his punches, conserving energy and waiting for clean counters instead of matching an opponent’s activity.

Canelo’s Guard Will Absorb More Than Punches

A high guard allows Alvarez to catch punches on his gloves, shoulders and forearms. That defense limits clean contact, but it does not remove the physical cost of blocking repeated combinations. Dmitry Bivol kept hitting the guard and forced Alvarez to carry the weight of his attacks.

Not every punch must reach Canelo’s head or body. Blows landing on the arms can gradually reduce the speed and authority of Alvarez’s counters. If his shoulders and biceps begin to tire by the middle rounds, the technical advantage Malignaggi identified becomes harder to use.

Portions of recent fights have also found Canelo along the ropes, reducing his movement and looking for single counters. Resting there is far more dangerous against Mbilli. The challenger works at close range without waiting to see the effect of every shot. Even blocked combinations can leave an impression with judges if Alvarez remains covered while Mbilli controls the action.

The difference in activity was visible on the same September 2025 card. Mbilli threw 787 punches across 10 rounds against Lester Martinez, nearly 79 per round. Canelo attempted only 338 during his 12-round loss to Terence Crawford, an average of just over 28. Mbilli threw 449 more punches despite boxing six fewer minutes. The figures come from unofficial CompuBox totals published by The Ring and Sports Illustrated.

That output came despite Martinez repeatedly shoving Mbilli backward to create separation before punching. Those interruptions kept Mbilli from remaining at the distance where he did his best work. Canelo is unlikely to match that activity or spend the fight continually pushing Mbilli outside.

Alvarez landed 83 of 260 power punches against Crawford but attempted only 78 jabs. Those figures show how dependent he has become on selective power shots rather than sustained combinations. Mbilli will give him far less recovery time between those attempts.

Early body work offers Canelo his best chance to reduce that output. He cannot afford to wait several rounds before targeting the ribs and liver. Mbilli must be given a reason to slow down before his pressure begins draining Alvarez’s arms and legs.

The opportunity will be there because Mbilli can be hit. He leans over his front foot while unloading, leaving a lane for Canelo’s right uppercut and short hooks. Sergiy Derevyanchenko found Mbilli’s chin with counters despite fighting with an injured arm. Alvarez is more accurate and carries considerably more power.

The fight therefore turns on one question. Can Canelo hurt Mbilli badly enough early to control the pace, or can Mbilli absorb those counters and continue throwing?

Scorecard interpretation adds another difficulty. Judges often favor Canelo’s clean, visible counters over punches caught on his guard. Mbilli cannot depend on activity alone. He must keep Alvarez defending long enough to make control of each round unmistakable.

Respect for Canelo’s decision to accept the fight does not erase the physical concern. Alvarez may be the more complete boxer, but Mbilli owns the weapon Malignaggi believes Canelo is least equipped to handle at this stage of his career.

Sports.title: IBF Tries To End Jai Opetaia Lawsuit Early
Sports.content:
It argues that its rules required Opetaia to bring the case in New Jersey, where the IBF is based. The organization also claims he went to court without completing its mandatory internal appeal process. Opetaia has until September 8 to respond.

Those objections give the IBF a chance to attack the lawsuit without immediately defending the decision to remove Opetaia as cruiserweight champion. A ruling based on venue or internal appeal grounds would not establish that his accusations lack merit.

He may be allowed to refile in New Jersey or complete the IBF appeal procedure before returning to court. A dismissal with prejudice would cause far greater damage by preventing him from bringing the same claims again.

The $73,000 Sanctioning Fee

The complaint alleges that the IBF accepted Opetaia’s $73,000 sanctioning fee shortly before his March 8 fight with Brandon Glanton, then withdrew approval for the contest. The organization says the payment arrived March 6 and was returned the next day.

The timing is central to Opetaia’s claim under the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act. His complaint accuses the IBF of accepting the money without making required disclosures to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

The IBF says it withdrew sanction after learning that the Zuffa Boxing cruiserweight title would be awarded. Its rules recognize unifications involving only the IBF, WBA, WBC, and WBO.

His lawsuit argues that the refusal to recognize Zuffa’s title was part of coordinated action intended to punish him for joining a competing boxing operation. The accusation has not been proven, but it places the control exercised by boxing’s four established sanctioning bodies at the center of the case.

Mikaelian Risks His WBC Championship

Noel Mikaelian is now testing that control from another direction. The WBC ordered him to defend against David Benavidez, but Mikaelian accepted a September 12 fight with Opetaia instead.

Desai said Mikaelian is expected to be stripped, although the WBC has not issued a final ruling. The reason would be his failure to make the ordered Benavidez defense, not his participation in a Zuffa Boxing event.

His choice also shows the limits of sanctioning body authority. Opetaia remains The Ring champion and the leading cruiserweight despite losing the IBF belt. Mikaelian evidently considers facing him on the Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn card valuable enough to risk his own championship.

The IBF and WBC can remove their belts. They cannot make Opetaia less formidable or prevent the division’s leading fighters from treating him as its central figure.

Sports.title: Who’s who in the Tszyu Zoo
Sports.content:
In 2020, Tszyu had the first key fight of his career, facing fellow Australian and former world champion, Jeff Horn. Tszyu battered the former champion using his jab, uppercuts and big right hands to the body and head, hurting him and breaking him down to force a retirement TKO in the eighth round.

Tszyu’s next key fight was against the durable and courageous Japanese fighter, Takeshi Inoue, in November 2021.

This was Tszyu’s 20th fight of his career, and this fight proved to be a turning point for him as a fighter on the international stage. Although he was outgunned, Inoue fought with passion and pride to give Tszyu a hard fight and take Tszyu the twelve-round distance for the first time.

In March, 2024, Tszyu, on late notice, traveled to Las Vegas to face the towering junior middleweight champion, Sebastian Fundora, in what was an iconic fight for both boxers. Both fighters, splattered in blood and both hurt by accident and intention, gave the fans a fight to remember, with Fundora winning by a split decision. Inexperience and a stubborn refusal to accept defeat cost him the fight.

Another key fight was his fight against the Chechen come-forward fighter, Bakhram Murtazaliev in October 2024, just six months after recovering and healing from a bad cut to the top of his head in the Fundora fight.

Tszyu was battered into a state of shock and disbelief, then knocked down numerous times until the fight was stopped in the third round in Orlando, Florida.

Tszyu returned to Sydney and back to the drawing board . Six months later, he took a confidence-building fight against the unrated and limited fighter Joey Spencer, to then go back three months later to face Sebastian Fundora for the WBC light middleweight championship of the world.

In the return match, Fundora fought smart, outboxing Tszyu by using his skill , timing, and natural ability, beating the Australian to force a corner retirement at the end of the 7th round.

Tszyu came back in December, beating unknown Anthony Velasquez in Sydney.

After beating Denis Nurja in April 2026, Tszyu focused on the Spence Jnr fight, and the win was deemed by many as a tremendous victory. My view on this is yes, it was good to have the name of Errol Spence Jnr on his record, but the key factor in the decision win was that it has kept his career alive.

So where does he go from here? With a new management and coaching team around him, as well as fighting at his new weight of 160 pounds, what’s next?

Erislandy Lara is the WBA middleweight champion. With a good record of 32 wins ( 19 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the Cuban southpaw is 43 years old, and since 2022, he has battered Gary ‘Spike’ O’Sullivan, destroyed Michael Zerafa, proved to be too much for Danny Garcia, and in December 2025, he beat Johan Gonzales on points. Lara has not fought in 2026. On any given night, a motivated Lara is and can be an awkward and dangerous opponent for anyone.

Carlos Adames is the WBC middleweight champion. The Dominican Republic puncher has a great record with 25 ( 18 KOs) and 1 defeat. He is 32 years old, and he consistently fights only once a year.

Aaron McKenna is the IBF middleweight champion. The newly crowned Irishman is 27 years old, and he is an unbeaten, well-schooled boxer . His record stands at 21-0. ( 10 KOs) McKenna is 6’3, and he has a 75-inch reach. He won the World title, beating the Italian Etinosa Oliha in early August, and prior to that he outboxed the experienced Liam Smith. He has a tremendous work rate, and he has speed.

Denzel Bentley. WBO middleweight champion. With a record of 22 wins ( 18 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the 31-year-old Englishman was the interim champion, to then be elevated to the WBO champion due to Janibek Alimkhanuly relinquishing his title to move up to super middleweight.

My view is, all roads lead to Jermell Charlo. He could be the path of least resistance for a big money fight. He is still a name, and he was the junior middleweight champion of the world. He has been inactive since being outboxed and outmuscled by Saul Canelo Alvarez in September 2023. He has a record of 35-2-1 with 19 KOs. He would be moving up in weight to meet Tszyu, and that would suit the 36-year-old at this stage of his career. If staged in Australia, the fight will sell as there has been some history of trash talking by both fighters, and for Tszyu, this could be his swan song, so it makes great business sense for him and also lucrative for Charlo.

The question is, will Tszyu wait and fight for a mandatory shot at one of the world champions, or will he make a move on Charlo?

Gary Todd is an international best-selling author, and he has been involved in all aspects of the sport of boxing for decades . Check out his latest book, “ Greatest Ever Boxing Champions. Their mindset. Their Workouts, Their Journeys.”

Sports.title: Boxing’s Strangest Records Need More Than Numbers
Sports.content:
Willie Pep recorded 229 victories, Archie Moore won 186 times and Sugar Ray Robinson collected 174 wins. Fritzie Zivic, Henry Armstrong, Nicolino Locche, Kid Gavilan, Julio Cesar Chavez and Roberto Duran also passed 100.

Their totals came from a boxing economy built around regular ticket sales at local halls and arenas. Boxers needed another booking to collect another purse. Staying active also kept them in fighting condition, reducing the need for the long rebuilding camps associated with current appearances.

Modern headliners receive broadcast guarantees and purses that allow them to earn more from one event than an earlier fighter might have made across dozens of appearances. The financial pressure to box every few weeks has disappeared at the highest level.

A Loss Once Meant Something Different

Promoters today market a perfect record as proof of superiority. One defeat can reduce a fighter’s television value, weaken his negotiating position and send his handlers searching for several favorable opponents to rebuild him.

Earlier generations had less reason to protect every number. A defeat could be treated as experience because another fight might be available within weeks. Weekly club shows also gave developing professionals room to accumulate 40 or 50 contests before reaching the national level.

That regional structure has largely disappeared. Many prospects now move from long amateur careers into televised professional fights without passing through the same volume of club competition.

The Fighters Paid to Test Prospects

Kristian Laight finished with 12 wins, 279 losses and nine draws, but calling him one of boxing’s greatest losers misses his value. He completed 300 fights and was stopped only five times. That required defensive awareness, composure and a clear understanding of how to survive difficult rounds.

Promoters trusted Laight to test developing fighters without turning every bout into a reckless war. He provided rounds, exposed mistakes and helped matchmakers judge if a prospect was ready to advance.

Reggie Strickland served a similar role during a 360-fight career, compiling 66 wins, 276 losses and 18 draws. Peter Buckley recorded 32 wins, 256 losses and 12 draws while facing future champions including Naseem Hamed, Kell Brook, Acelino Freitas and Gavin Rees.

Both men regularly traveled into the territory of promoted fighters. Winning a close points decision under those conditions was difficult, especially when the local boxer represented the financial investment behind the event. Their records cannot be separated from the purpose they served.

Too many upsets would cost a journeyman future calls. Getting knocked out too easily offered little developmental value. The job required operating between those extremes.

Boxing records tell us who won and lost, but not what each fighter was being paid to accomplish. Wickwar’s 340 victories preserve the remains of an industry built on constant competition. Laight’s 279 defeats expose the workforce that allowed another generation to learn its trade.

Both records belong in boxing history, though not for the same reason.

Sports.title: Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson Faces Shawn McCalman For WBA Intercontinental Title
Sports.content:
Coming out of the renowned Upton Boxing Center, Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson started his pro career with thirteen consecutive victories. Back in August 2023, Simpson took a costly trip to Atlanta, as he suffered his first defeat by way of majority decision to Vladimir Hernandez.

Ten months later, Simpson made a return trip to Atlanta for another Overtime Boxing event, and he lost via controversial split-decision to Raiko Santana. Truck Simpson bounced back with a first-round stoppage victory over Trevon Smith.

In his next outing, Simpson suffered another setback, as he was outpointed by Jahi Tucker. Once again, Simpson took a moment to regroup, and then he bounced back with a second-round TKO victory over George Sosa.

Now Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson is ready to step into the ring in front of his hometown fans to face a dangerous opponent. His adversary for this event is the Colorado native Shawn McCalman.

Similar to Truck Simpson, Shawn McCalman started his pro career with fifteen consecutive victories. He came up short in two of his last four fights, as he lost to highly ranked Diego Pacheco and the undefeated Moreno Fendero.

Now Shawn McCalman has vowed to travel to Baltimore and bring the WBA Intercontinental strap back to Colorado. This match will be a challenging bout for both fighters.

The southpaw Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson is a boxer who has all the tools. His confidence is at an all-time high, and he believes all he has to do is stay focused, and his time to shine will be right here, right now.

Simpson knows the night of September 19th will be a true test. According to a recent post, challenging nights are now a personal requirement for Truck.

Ghana News.title: Anta Education Fund beneficiaries rise to 1,519 as Amin Adam supports 200 more students
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Karaga and former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has provided financial support to 200 students from various tertiary institutions to enable them to pay their school fees.

The latest intervention, which was made in Karaga, forms part of the MP’s ongoing efforts under the Anta Education Fund to ease the financial burden on students and families in the constituency.

According to Dr Amin Adam, the latest beneficiaries bring to 1,519 the total number of students who have benefited from the fund since its establishment in 2020.

In a Facebook post, Dr Amin Adam said the initiative was established to provide educational support to students in the Pishigu area of the Karaga Constituency and has since expanded its impact across the constituency.

He stressed that education remained central to his development agenda, saying, “Education remains our priority; and we will continue to give greater attention to the education of our people.”

The Karaga MP said the continued investment in education was necessary to give young people the opportunity to pursue tertiary education despite financial difficulties.

“Yesterday in Karaga, we provided support to 200 students from various tertiary educational institutions to pay their fees,” he stated, adding that the intervention had contributed to the growing number of beneficiaries under the Anta Education Fund.

The latest initiative further reinforces Dr Amin Adam’s stated commitment to using education as a tool for improving opportunities for young people in the constituency.

Ghana News.title: OSP dismisses claims of strained relationship with Attorney-General
Ghana News.content:
OSP's Director of Strategy, Research and Communications, Samuel Appiah Darko

The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has rejected perceptions of a strained relationship with the Office of the Attorney-General, insisting that the two institutions maintain a strong working relationship.

The Director of Strategy, Research and Communications at the OSP, Samuel Appiah Darko, made the clarification when he called into JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 29.

According to him, the OSP continues to collaborate effectively with relevant state institutions, particularly the Office of the Attorney-General, in carrying out its anti-corruption mandate.

Mr Appiah Darko said that although some members of the public may perceive recent developments as evidence of a clash between the OSP and the Attorney-General, that impression does not reflect the actual relationship between the two offices.

"The reason why I have called on the show is to talk about these things. First of all, the issue that the OSP is not collaborating with the AG, I think that it is a wrong perception," he said.

"Is that not obvious from your press conferences?" the host of the show, Samson Lardy Anyenini, asked him.

He replied, "I know that people think that there is tension between the AG and the OSP. There could be tension, but you cannot also deny the OSP from also telling Ghanaians about some of the things that it is doing, and it wants to do. For instance, if the OSP needs to respond to some information that has already been put in the public domain that may not be accurate and the OSP clarifies that, that does not mean that the OSP is breeding a fight or tension."

He maintained that the OSP enjoys cordial relations with its stakeholders and remains committed to the institutional cooperation required to investigate and prosecute corruption-related offences effectively.

His intervention followed concerns raised during the programme about what appeared to be inadequate collaboration between the OSP and the Attorney-General.

Mr Appiah Darko’s remarks sought to assure the public that the two institutions are working together despite differences that may arise in the performance of their respective statutory responsibilities.

In recent times, the two institutions have appeared to disagree over their respective roles in Ghana’s fight against corruption, particularly regarding the AKSA bribery allegations and the Abu Trica case. Their public statements have also created the impression of a dispute over which institution deserves credit for the progress made in the two cases.

Ghana News.title: We’ve asked AG to collaborate on cases but were turned down – OSP
Ghana News.content:
The Director of Strategy, Research and Communications at the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), Samuel Appiah Darko, has claimed that the Attorney-General (AG) has declined several requests from the office to collaborate on cases.

Mr Appiah Darko said the OSP had, on several occasions, approached the Office of the AG for cooperation but did not receive the requested support.

"There are so many issues the OSP has kept quiet and not talked about. Look, there are instances where the OSP has approached the Attorney General's office and said, let us collaborate in this matter and we have been turned down," he claimed on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 29.

His comments followed concerns about an apparent lack of collaboration between the two institutions, which play critical roles in Ghana’s criminal justice system and the fight against corruption.

Mr Appiah Darko maintained that although the OSP generally has a good working relationship with the Attorney-General and other stakeholders, there have been instances where its requests for case-specific collaboration were turned down.

According to him, several developments occur behind the scenes, but the OSP does not consider it necessary or appropriate to place every institutional interaction in the public domain.

"When you are managing a state institution, a very sensitive one, it is not all the information you will come out to the public to talk about," he noted.

Mr Appiah Darko argued that public assessments of the OSP’s performance and institutional relationships should take account of the work and engagements that may not be publicly disclosed.

Ghana News.title: OSP must be judged by its mandate, not who occupies the office – Baffour Awuah
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah

The Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, has called on Ghanaians to avoid defining the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) by the personality of the individual occupying the position.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 29, the MP argued that public discussions about the OSP should focus on the institution, its legal mandate and its performance rather than the officeholder.

"We should avoid personalising the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP). I listened to the press conference, and I was sad that you came and said that all that is happening is because of hatred for the occupant of the office. Very respectfully was below the belt," he said.

"Why would you want to believe or make it seem that it is a personal matter against the occupant of the office?, While you take that position, it becomes very difficult for cooperation," he added.

His comments followed the OSP’s recent press conference, during which the anti-corruption body declared its “rebirth” and reaffirmed its commitment to fighting corruption.

The discussion also examined emerging concerns, including what appears to be inadequate collaboration between the OSP and the Office of the Attorney-General.

Mr Awuah maintained that personalising the OSP could weaken public confidence in the institution and distract attention from broader questions about its effectiveness and relationship with other state agencies.

He called for the OSP to be treated as an enduring state institution whose credibility and operations should not depend solely on the person serving as Special Prosecutor.

Ghana News.title: OSP says intervention has reduced corruption in GRA Customs vehicle auctions
Ghana News.content:
The Director of Strategy, Research, and Communication at the OSP, Samuel Appiah Darko

The Director of Strategy, Research and Communications at the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), Samuel Appiah Darko, says the office’s intervention has helped reduce corruption within the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA).

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 29, Mr Appiah Darko said the OSP was undertaking significant anti-corruption work that was not always publicised.

He cited the sanitisation of vehicle auction processes within the Customs Division as one of the OSP’s notable interventions.

According to him, the OSP received a report alleging that some customs officers were manipulating vehicle auctions for personal financial gain. The office subsequently investigated the matter and intervened to address the reported irregularities.

Mr Appiah Darko said the intervention had helped sanitise the auction system and minimise opportunities for corruption within the division.

"If you go to the Customs Division, in the past you would hear a lot of wrong about auction vehicles, now it is reduced. It is the work of the OSP. We had to change the benchmark value that was given to Customs Officials, the opportunity to be able to engage in corruption and all that; the OSP is the one that brought all these things to an end through the work we did in the Labianca case and all that," he said.

He argued that the impact of the OSP should not be assessed solely by the cases or investigations it announces publicly, as some of its work involves behind-the-scenes interventions aimed at preventing corruption.

He, therefore, rejected claims that the OSP was doing little to combat corruption, insisting that the office continued to deliver results across various public institutions.

Ghana News.title: Trust, judgment and value: The 3 questions every organisation must answer about AI
Ghana News.content:
Charlotte Forson-Abbey

Over the past year, I have participated in numerous conversations with boards, executives, and business leaders about artificial intelligence. While these discussions often begin with excitement about the technology's potential, they almost always converge on a few underlying concerns.

The questions are not usually about whether AI is powerful. Most leaders already recognise that it is.

Instead, the conversation usually comes down to three fundamental questions:

Can we trust it?

Is it creating value?

Who remains accountable?

These questions may appear straightforward, but they will often determine whether AI becomes a source of lasting business value or simply another technology experiment. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in business processes and decision-making, the challenge for leaders is no longer just adopting the technology. It is ensuring that it is used responsibly, effectively, and with appropriate oversight.

Can We Trust It?

Trust has always been a cornerstone of business success.

Investors rely on accurate information to make decisions. Customers trust organisations with their data. Employees trust leadership to act responsibly. Without trust, confidence erodes and performance suffers.

AI introduces new questions into that equation.

Unlike traditional systems that operate according to predefined rules, AI models often generate outputs based on patterns in data. While this can produce remarkable results, it can also make outcomes more difficult to explain and understand.

As organisations adopt AI, leaders must ask important questions:

How reliable is the data being used?

How are AI outputs being validated?

What controls exist to identify errors or bias?

Who oversees ongoing performance?

These are not purely technology concerns. They are governance concerns.

Regulators across the world are increasingly paying attention to how AI is governed, and Africa is unlikely to be an exception. In Ghana, organisations are already subject to requirements around data privacy, cybersecurity, and responsible handling of information. While AI-specific regulation is still evolving, the direction of travel is clear. Boards and management teams will increasingly be expected to understand how AI systems operate, what data they rely on, and how associated risks are managed. The organisations building these governance foundations today will be better prepared for tomorrow's regulatory expectations.

The reality is that trust cannot be assumed simply because a system is sophisticated. It must be earned through transparency, oversight and accountability. Organisations that establish clear governance around AI will be better positioned to build confidence among customers, employees, investors, and regulators.

In many ways, trust will become a key differentiator in the AI era. Technology may be widely accessible, but confidence in how it is deployed will not be.

Is It Creating Value?

The second question is equally important.

Today, many organisations are investing heavily in AI initiatives. New tools are being deployed, pilot projects are being launched, and employees are being encouraged to integrate AI into their daily work.

Yet one question continues to surface in boardrooms:

Where is the measurable value?

The assumption that AI adoption automatically leads to productivity gains can be misleading. Technology alone rarely transforms an organisation. Sustainable value typically requires changes to processes, skills, ways of working, and performance measurement.

Simply providing employees with AI tools does not guarantee better outcomes.

In fact, some organisations are experiencing what might be described as an AI productivity paradox. Work is being completed faster. More content is being produced. Information is easier to access.

Yet improvements in business performance are often harder to demonstrate.

This should not be surprising. Every major technological shift has required organisations to rethink how work is done before meaningful benefits can be realised.

The most successful organisations are focusing less on adoption metrics and more on business outcomes. Rather than asking how many employees are using AI, they are asking:

Has decision-making improved?

Have risks been reduced?

Has customer experience improved?

Have costs been lowered?

Is productivity genuinely increasing?

Ultimately, the objective is not to deploy AI for its own sake. The objective is to create value.

Leaders who remain focused on outcomes rather than hype will be far more likely to realise meaningful returns from their investments.

Who Remains Accountable?

The third question may be the most important.

As AI becomes more capable, there is a growing temptation to view technology as a substitute for human judgment. That would be a mistake.

AI can analyse information at extraordinary speed. It can identify patterns, generate insights, and support complex decision-making. However, it cannot assume responsibility for the consequences of those decisions.

Accountability remains a human responsibility.

Business decisions are rarely based on data alone. They require context, experience, professional scepticism, ethical considerations, and an understanding of stakeholder expectations.

A board evaluating a strategic investment must consider factors that extend beyond projections and forecasts. A management team responding to a crisis must weigh commercial, reputational, and social implications. An auditor assessing risk must apply judgment in situations where there may be no clear answer.

These responsibilities cannot be delegated to algorithms.

In fact, as AI becomes more prevalent, human judgment may become more valuable. The ability to challenge assumptions, interpret complex situations, and make balanced decisions will remain essential.

The future of work is unlikely to be defined by humans competing against AI. Rather, it will be shaped by organisations that successfully combine technological capability with human insight.

The best outcomes will come not from AI alone, but from people who know how to use it wisely.

Looking Ahead

AI represents one of the most significant technological developments of our time. Its potential to improve efficiency, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation is undeniable.

However, organisations should resist the temptation to view AI solely through a technology lens.

The more important questions are ultimately about leadership, governance, and accountability.

Can we trust it?

Is it creating value?

Who remains accountable?

The organisations that answer these questions effectively will be best positioned to realise the benefits of AI while managing its risks.

Technology will continue to evolve. The principles of trust, value, and sound judgment will not.

In the age of AI, those principles may matter more than ever.

Ghana News.title: GWL restores water supply after damaged pipeline disrupts Western Accra communities
Ghana News.content:
Ghana Water Ltd (GWL) has completed repair works on a damaged 500mm-diameter main pipeline and restored water supply to several communities in Western Accra.

According to a press statement issued on Saturday, August 29, the pipeline was damaged during excavation works undertaken by AVERCO Construction Ltd, resulting in a temporary interruption in supply to communities including Mallam, Darkuman, Nshorna, Machetato, Korle Bu, Mamprobi, Dansoman Township and Chorkor.

GWL said its engineers and technical teams worked continuously to repair the affected section, allowing supply to resume in the affected areas.

However, the company cautioned that some customers may continue to experience low water pressure or intermittent flow as pressure across the network gradually stabilises.

GWL has urged residents to remain patient during the restoration period and allow time for normal service to resume fully.

Management also thanked affected customers for their patience and cooperation, while acknowledging the contribution of other stakeholders to the speedy completion of the repairs.

Customers who continue to experience supply problems have been advised to report them through GWL’s official communication channels.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s democracy remains strong despite its challenges – Interior Minister assures Russian envoy
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has assured the Russian Ambassador to Ghana, Sergei Berdnikov, that Ghana’s democracy remains strong despite the challenges associated with democratic governance.

According to a Facebook post by the Ministry of the Interior on Saturday, Mr Mohammed-Mubarak said Ghana had witnessed peaceful transfers of power between successive governments since embracing democratic rule.

He attributed the country’s democratic stability to Ghanaians’ commitment to peace, noting that political transitions had occurred smoothly and without major difficulties.

The Interior Minister also stressed the need for international cooperation in promoting peace and security, arguing that no country could operate effectively in isolation.

He said collaboration and the exchange of ideas and intelligence with other countries would strengthen Ghana’s efforts to maintain national security.

Mr Mohammed-Mubarak acknowledged the longstanding relationship between Ghana and Russia, which dates back to the administration of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah.

He consequently called for stronger cooperation between the two countries, particularly in training, security and other areas of mutual interest.

For his part, Ambassador Berdnikov commended the Interior Minister for his leadership and focus on Ghana’s security.

He also expressed appreciation for the warm reception and called for enhanced bilateral security cooperation that would benefit both Ghana and Russia.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
