Poland has formally requested that the European Commission fine Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, €250 million (1.1 billion zloty) for failing to tackle fraudulent advertising on its platforms. Its decision follows a high-profile campaign by Rafał Brzoska, the billionaire owner of Polish delivery giant InPost, over scam adverts on Facebook that exploit fake images of him and other prominent Polish public figures, including President Karol Nawrocki. Platformy cyfrowe muszą ponosić pełną odpowiedzialność za swoje działania i dlatego zawnioskowałem o nałożenie na Metę kary w wysokości miliarda złotych. Po analizie materiałów, w tym tych otrzymanych od Meta, a także kolejnych doniesień medialnych o braku kontroli nad… pic.twitter.com/1zSZg8MGf4 — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 27, 2026 On Thursday morning, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski announced that he had sent a request to the European Commission to take action against Meta, including fining it €250 million. “Inaction and ineffectiveness in combating harmful s and fraudulent content targeting Poles will not be tolerated,” wrote Gawkowski. “I expect the European Commission to conduct the proceedings swiftly and impose the fine. There is more than enough evidence.” The minister also called on Meta itself to “immediately introduce effective tools to eliminate scams, fake s, and the promotion of illegal applications. This Wild West on the platform must come to an end”. Gawkowski shared an image of the first page of a letter he had sent to Henna Virkkunen, the European commissioner for technological sovereignty, security and democracy, in which he argued that Meta’s failure to combat fraud may violate the EU’s Digital Services Act. He pointed to a study by CERT Polska, a Polish state IT security body, which found that, of 122 adverts reported to Meta as being fraudulent, in 106 cases the company rejected requests to remove them. Gawkowski noted that the European Consumer Organisation has reported similar concerns to the EU. On Wednesday, Gawkowski also shared copies of correspondence he had exchanged with Meta earlier this month. In response to the minister’s concerns, the tech firm had argued that it “does not seek to profit from” fraudulent advertising and outlined steps it was taking to address the problem. Meta disclosed that, between July 2025 and June 2026, it had, in Poland alone, removed 380,000 examples of content and 137,000 adverts for violating its policies on fraudulent practices. It noted that the vast majority were removed before users even reported them. Meta przesłała odpowiedź o działaniach związanych ze zwalczaniem scamów i wskazuje, że niektóre dane przekazuje z zachowaniem ścisłej poufności. W państwie szanującym obywatela takie dane muszą być jawne i dlatego podjąłem decyzję o ujawnieniu treści pisma. W piśmie Meta… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 26, 2026 Gawkowski’s intervention follows a high-profile campaign by Brzoska, one of Poland’s richest people and who, along with his wife, former TV presenter and businesswoman Omenaa Mensah, is a prominent public figure. Brzoska and Mensah have long complained about the unauthorised use of their likenesses in fraudulent social-media advertising, especially on Facebook. In 2024, Poland’s data protection authority ordered Meta to stop displaying adverts that featured false reports of Mensah’s death to promote scams. Earlier this month, Brzoska renewed his campaign, highlighting an example of a scam on Facebook that used a fake image of him being handcuffed by police in his home. Tak działa koncern @Meta w Polsce-nieustająco tolerując fake newsy na mój i wiele innych publicznych osób temat… Może innym to nie przeszkadza, ale jeśli moje małoletnie dzieciaki wysyłają mi te screeny pytając "o co chodzi Tato?", to jak się polskiemu zarządowi tej gównianej… pic.twitter.com/rp4CUscah1 — Rafał Brzoska (@RBrzoska) August 14, 2026 Brzoska – who also pointed to examples of Facebook running fake adverts featuring other prominent Polish figures, including President Nawrocki – launched a petition calling for platforms that run scam adverts to be fined 150% of the revenue they received from them. The petition – which, at the time of writing, has been signed by almost 91,000 people – cited leaked data, reported by Reuters last year, indicating that Meta estimated 10% of its sales in 2024, around €16 billion, came from advertising scams or illegal products and services. In comments to Reuters, Meta said at the time that the estimate was “rough and overly inclusive” and that the actual figure was lower. But it declined to provide an updated figure. World.title: Foreign Pupils on the Rise in Czech Schools — Nearly One in Five in Prague
World.content:
Of the nearly one million pupils attending Czech primary schools last academic year, almost 8% were foreign nationals, most commonly from Ukraine.

According to the Czech Statistical Office (CSO), Prague recorded the highest proportion, with foreign pupils making up 18% of all children in its primary schools.

Compulsory education is mandatory for Czech citizens as well as citizens of other European Union member states who reside in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days. The requirement also applies to foreign nationals with long-term residence permits.

Their children therefore have the same rights as Czech children, including access to free education, school meals and extracurricular activities.



The number of foreign pupils increased significantly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, nearly doubling that year. Their numbers have continued to rise ever since. Today, children from Ukraine account for 5% of all pupils in the Czech Republic.

The trend is similar in secondary schools, where the proportion of foreign pupils reached its highest level in the past 10 years, at almost 5% of the total.

Although the number of children in primary schools has remained relatively stable at just over one million in recent years, a sharp decline is expected in the coming years due to the falling birth rate, according to Vendula Kašparová of the CSO’s Social Development Statistics Department. The office said the birth rate has been falling continuously for the fifth consecutive year.

The decline is already visible at the kindergarten level. The number of children enrolled in kindergartens fell below 350,000 in the 2025/2026 academic year, the first time this has happened since 2013. Over the past three years, enrolment has dropped by more than 21,000 children, or around 5.8%.

Fewer Children Receiving Deferrals From Starting School

Kašparová identifies another clear trend: fewer children are being granted deferrals from starting compulsory school. Since the 2021/2022 academic year, the proportion of six-year-olds whose school entry was deferred has fallen from 24.1% in September 2021 to 17.7% in September 2025, representing just under 21,000 pupils.

Furthermore, an amendment to the Education Act is expected to reduce the number of deferrals even further. Under the new rules, deferrals will only be granted when justified by a medical condition that prevents a child from attending school.

This could include a serious medical condition following surgery, cancer treatment or a moderate intellectual disability.

World.title: Czechia, the Land of Burgers. More Fast Food Chains Enter the Market
World.content:
The Czech fast food market is expanding beyond its established players, with new international brands entering the country and existing chains opening restaurants in smaller cities.

McDonald’s and KFC continue to build their networks, while brands from Germany, the United States and Poland are looking for opportunities in the Czech Republic.

The expansion is increasingly moving beyond Prague and other major cities, with retail parks becoming an important location for new restaurants.



Burgermeister prepares Czech debut

One of the newest international brands preparing to enter the Czech market is Germany’s Burgermeister. The Berlin-based burger chain plans to open its first restaurant on Wenceslas Square at the beginning of next year.

The company already sees its Prague location as more than a single restaurant. It is also considering further locations across the country.

Popeyes and Burger King continue expanding

Burger King entered the Czech market 18 years ago and now operates around 70 restaurants. Popeyes arrived much later but has expanded quickly, opening 19 locations during its first three years in the country.

The companies are building a network that stretches from smaller regional towns to central Prague. In Králův Dvůr, a town of around 11,000 people, both Burger King and Popeyes operate at the Litavka Retail Park.

Popeyes is preparing additional restaurants at the Eden shopping centre and in the Budějovická area of Prague. The chain is also expanding into regional cities, with planned locations in Klatovy and Písek.

Five Guys adds another international brand

The Czech burger market gained another major international name last December when U.S. chain Five Guys opened its first Prague restaurant.

The restaurant is located in the former Máj department store on Národní Street. Five Guys is known for burgers prepared to order and a wide range of toppings, allowing customers to customise their meals.

Its prices, however, are generally higher than those of traditional fast food chains.

Another U.S. brand, Dave’s Hot Chicken, is also expected to enter the Czech market this year, according to consulting firm Cushman & Wakefield.

The chain specialises in spicy fried chicken and will therefore compete directly with established players such as KFC and Popeyes.

Czech chains are looking beyond their home cities

The expansion is not limited to international companies.

Czech burger chain Mama’s Burger is also developing its network. Originally based in Ostrava, the company has expanded into several larger Czech cities and operates a restaurant at Prague’s Arkády Pankrác shopping centre.

The company is also seeking franchise partners as it looks to increase the number of locations.

World.title: Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
World.content:
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.

Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.

At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.



The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.

The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.

The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.

How the Champions League league phase works

The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.

Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.

The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.

The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

World.title: MINT Market Returns to Prague’s Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
World.content:
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.

From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.



The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.

MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.

Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.

For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.

“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.

“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”

The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

World.title: Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
World.content:
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.

The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.

The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.



One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.

Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public

Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.

An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.

Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.

A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.

The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.

A Baroque complex with a long military history

Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.

The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.

Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

Prague’s beer lovers can look forward to one of the city’s biggest beer events of the year as Manifesto Market brings back its annual beer festival for a third edition.

The two-day event will bring together some of the Czech Republic’s best-known craft breweries, alongside a guest brewery from Berlin, with more than 40 beers available to taste throughout the weekend.

Zichovec, Sibeeria, Chroust, MadCat, Fracek, Pivovar VIK and Berlin-based BRLO will each have their own pop-up tent, giving visitors the chance to explore a wide range of beer styles directly from the breweries.



More breweries are expected to be announced ahead of the event.

One of the highlights will be the festival’s limited-edition glass. It serves as the ticket for accessing the festival specials and can also be taken home as a souvenir.

The beer will be accompanied by food from more than 10 international kitchens at Manifesto. Visitors can expect everything from juicy burgers and tacos to spicy ramen and authentic Chinese roast duck, making it possible to turn the beer tasting into a full weekend meal.

World.title: More Czechs Are Living Paycheck to Paycheck, New Survey Finds
World.content:
The number of Czechs who have nothing left from their paycheck at the end of the month is rising.

This year, 13 percent say they have no money left after covering their expenses, up from 9 percent last year. Meanwhile, 84 percent have at least a small amount left over, five percentage points less than in 2025.

The findings come from a May survey conducted by loan provider Provident Financial among 1,000 respondents.



According to the survey, Czechs’ ability to save is declining. Only 43 percent of respondents have at least 20 percent of their monthly income left after covering their expenses, down nine percentage points from last year. Almost half of Czechs nevertheless regularly set aside part of their paycheck each month.

At the same time, their overall financial resilience appears to be improving. More than a quarter of respondents have enough savings to cover their expenses for more than a year, compared with just 15 percent last year. The share of people with no financial reserve at all has also fallen, from 18 percent in 2025 to 13 percent this year.

The gap between men and women in the amount of money left at the end of the month has also narrowed. This year, 45 percent of men have at least 20 percent of their paycheck left after expenses, compared with 59 percent last year. Among women, the figure has fallen from 45 percent to 39 percent.

The share of Czechs with enough savings to cover 12 months without their main source of income has increased sharply this year, rising by 11 percentage points compared with 2025. At the same time, the proportion of respondents whose savings would last less than three months fell to 12 percent, down from 17 percent a year earlier.

Men are considerably more likely than women to report having enough savings to cover at least six months of expenses. The figure is 63 percent among men, compared with 39 percent among women.

Education also appears to play an important role in financial preparedness. Seven in ten respondents with a university degree say they have enough savings to cover at least six months, compared with 43 percent among people with lower levels of education.

World.title: Hungarian Gripens alerted as man steals aircraft and flies toward Paks nuclear plant
World.content:
Hungarian Gripen fighter jets were scrambled after a light aircraft reportedly stolen from an airfield in Kalocsa headed towards Paks, home to Hungary’s nuclear power plant.

Gripens sent after stolen aircraft landing detected by military radar

According to Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, the Hungarian Defence Forces detected the aircraft on radar shortly after it took off and immediately launched a pair of Gripen fighter jets.

The Paks Nuclear Power Plant is a specially protected facility. Civilian aircraft are prohibited from entering a three-kilometre radius around the site below an altitude of 6,000 metres, making the approaching aircraft a matter requiring an immediate military response.

Aircraft crashes near Gerjen while Gripens stayed overhead

The incident ended only minutes later when the light aircraft made an emergency landing in the Gerjen area, according to the minister. The Gripens located the damaged aircraft and remained above the scene until a rescue helicopter and ground emergency crews arrived.

Police and other relevant authorities also attended, with an on-site inspection and investigation subsequently launched. The minister said that, according to the information available at the time, nobody was injured.

Pilot reportedly stole the Cessna from Kalocsa airfield

Hungarian news outlet HVG reported that the aircraft was a Cessna 172 allegedly taken from Kalocsa Airport by a pilot who was in a disturbed state. According to the report, the man, born in 2002, landed the aircraft in a field near the village of Gerjen. Initial reports differed over whether the aircraft came down in a sunflower or corn field.

The aircraft was reportedly damaged in the landing, with its landing gear broken and the plane coming to rest on its wing, partially tilted to one side. Firefighters and a rescue helicopter were dispatched to the scene. No further details about the person who allegedly took the aircraft have been released.

Military response shows air-defence readiness

The Defence Minister described the incident as an unusual alert but said it demonstrated the importance of maintaining a constant state of readiness. He highlighted the sequence of detecting, responding to, identifying and assisting in an incident, saying the Hungarian Defence Forces were prepared to respond at any time, both in the air and on the ground.

The circumstances surrounding the aircraft theft and its attempted flight towards Paks remain under investigation.

World.title: Drought in Hungary brought another power plant to its knees
World.content:
Hungary’s Tiszalök Hydroelectric Power Plant has halted electricity generation because of exceptionally low water levels on the Tisza River, amid a severe drought affecting the region.

The shutdown was reported by Péter Lajos Szakács, a Tisza party MP for the area, who stressed that the facility’s primary role is water-flow regulation, with electricity generation serving as a secondary function.

Despite the shutdown, the electricity supply of Tiszalök and the surrounding area remains secure, while the Paks Nuclear Power Plant is operating at full capacity, he said.

Water levels too low for hydropower

Under normal conditions, the Tiszalök power plant has a generation capacity of 12.9 megawatts, equivalent to around 0.65 per cent of the full capacity of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant.

However, the Tisza’s low water level had already prevented the plant from reaching its normal output in recent weeks. According to the North Hungarian Water Management Directorate (ÉMVIZIG), neither the current water level nor the flow rate is sufficient for the hydroelectric plant to operate.

Water regulation at the Tiszalök barrage is continuing through a single gate that remains in operation.

Tisza catchment receives just a quarter of usual water

The severity of the shortage is reflected in the amount of water reaching the Tisza from its catchment area. The catchment has received only around a quarter of its usual water volume this year.

Further downstream, the Tisza Lake – an artificial reservoir created following the construction of the Kisköre Water Barrage – has consequently lost virtually all of its usable water reserves. Its water level has fallen to 610 centimetres.

Stay up-to-date: Russia threatens to cut oil and gas supplies to Hungary after Budapest labels Moscow a security threat

Authorities redirect water to drought-hit areas

Because of the extraordinary drought, ÉMVIZIG began lowering the upstream water level at the Tiszalök Water Barrage on 27 August. The level had previously been raised as high as possible to retain water.

Over the coming week, the level held at Tiszalök is expected to fall by 20 centimetres from its current 420-centimetre level. The released water will provide additional supplies for the Tisza Lake, the Eastern Main Canal and the Körös Valley, where water shortages are also severe.

One aim is to help maintain a water level above 610 centimetres at Kisköre-Felső for as long as possible, supporting the Tisza Lake’s water reserves. Another is to direct previously stored water towards the Eastern Main Canal.

World.title: Hungary marks 500th anniversary of Battle of Mohács with new commemorative coins
World.content:
Hungary has marked the 500th anniversary of the Battle of Mohács with the release of commemorative coins and a special stamp block, unveiled at an anniversary ceremony in the southern Hungarian town of Mohács on Friday.

National Bank and Hungarian Post Office unveil special issues honouring the victims and heroes

The Hungarian National Bank (Magyar Nemzeti Bank, MNB) has issued two commemorative coins — a HUF 30,000 silver coin and a HUF 6,000 non-ferrous metal version.

Meanwhile Magyar Posta has released a special stamp block commemorating one of the defining events in Hungarian history.

The Battle of Mohács took place on 29 August 1526, when the Hungarian army suffered a decisive defeat against the forces of the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

The Battle of Mohács resulted in heavy Hungarian losses and had profound consequences for the country’s subsequent history.

Two commemorative coins issued in limited numbers

Levente Sipos-Tompa, Vice President of the MNB responsible for the supervision of financial institutions and consumer protection spoke at the anniversary event.

He said the central bank’s commemorative coins pay tribute to the heroes and victims of the battle and to the courage of the soldiers who sacrificed themselves in defence of their homeland.

The MNB is issuing 5,000 examples of each version, meaning that only 10,000 coins in total will be produced.

The central bank emphasised that the primary purpose of commemorative coins is to convey historical and cultural value and attract attention to significant events.

They are not intended for everyday transactions. Their limited production and artistic design give them a special collector’s value, while the denomination helps preserve their value as collectible coins.

A design inspired by the Mohács National Memorial Site

The obverse of the coins features a composition inspired by the split gate of the Mohács National Memorial Site, alongside a stylised depiction of a burial mound decorated with sword-divided, cross-shaped motifs.

The design also carries an inscription quoting the closing lines of Károly Kisfaludy’s poem Mohács, written in 1821. The inscription reflects on the historical significance of Mohács while looking towards the future and peace.

The reverse depicts mounted warriors heading into battle, facing a line of lances symbolising the Ottoman army. The coins were designed by Zoltán Endrődy.

The HUF 30,000 coin is made of 925-fineness silver and weighs 31.46 grams. It has a proof finish and measures 26.40 by 39.60 millimetres.

The HUF 6,000 version is made from an alloy containing 75 per cent copper and 25 per cent nickel, weighs 27 grams and has a satin finish. Both coins have a rectangular shape with a smooth edge.

The 2026 minting year and the BP mint mark also appear on the obverse, while the reverse features the official ‘Mohács 500’ logo and the denominations.

The special coin commemorating the 500th anniversary of the Battle of Mohács. Photo: MTI/Kacsúr Tamás

Special stamp block recalls the Battle of Mohács through art

Magyar Posta has also issued a commemorative stamp block for the 500th anniversary. The postal issue is intended not only as a philatelic collector’s item but also as a tribute to those who lost their lives defending their homeland on 29 August 1526.

The stamp block uses prominent works of art connected with the Battle of Mohács and the period to evoke the historical events.

The frame features a woodcut entitled The Battle of Mohács, produced in 1526. The stamp on the left depicts István Dorffmaister’s portrait Louis II, while the stamp on the right features a detail from József Borsos’s The Battle of Mohács in 1526, a copy of Dorffmaister’s painting.

The commemorative envelope is decorated with a detail from Bertalan Székely’s painting The Discovery of the Body of Louis II. The first-day cover also bears the official logo of the Mohács 500 commemorative year.

The stamp block was produced at the Pénzjegynyomda printing house using photographs by István Füzi and Gerald Raab, based on a design by graphic artist Balázs Hajnal. The commemorative envelopes were produced by Pátria Nyomda.

More on Hungarian history: 30 years of UNESCO recognition — fascinating facts about Hungary’s Pannonhalma Archabbey — Photo gallery

Remembering a turning point in Hungarian history

The anniversary issues form part of Hungary’s wider commemorations of the half-millennium since the Battle of Mohács. The 1526 defeat became a defining turning point in Hungarian history.

King Louis II was killed following the battle, while the defeat contributed to the subsequent division of the Kingdom of Hungary and the expansion of Ottoman influence in the region.

Five centuries later, the new coins and stamps provide tangible reminders of the people who fought and died at Mohács, while preserving the memory of the battle through Hungary’s traditions of coin collecting and philately.

The commemorative issues were unveiled in Mohács during the city’s official 500th-anniversary celebrations, attended by representatives of the MNB, Magyar Posta and the local government.

World.title: Update on injured Gripen pilot after dramatic ejection in Hungary
World.content:
Good news has emerged about the Hungarian fighter pilot who was forced to eject from his Gripen after the aircraft suffered a technical failure during a military exercise near Szolnok. The 51-year-old major has been discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery at home.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi announced the news on Facebook on Friday, wishing the experienced pilot a full and speedy recovery.

The officer had to undergo surgery after suffering a spinal injury during the ejection from the JAS 39 Gripen. According to the Defence Ministry, his recovery has progressed quickly enough for doctors to allow him to leave the hospital.

Pilot underwent successful spinal surgery

The fighter pilot was taken by helicopter to the Honvéd Hospital in Budapest shortly after the incident, where doctors diagnosed a spinal injury.

He underwent surgery on Tuesday. According to Telex, neurosurgeon György Székely of the North-Pest Central Hospital – Honvéd Hospital previously said that the relatively minor spinal operation offered the pilot the best chance of making a full recovery.

Ejecting from a fighter aircraft is medically dangerous because the procedure involves extremely high acceleration, placing considerable stress on the body, particularly the spine. The pilot’s discharge comes just four days after the accident. Earlier in the week, officials had said he could leave hospital “within days”.

The Gripen after the crash. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

Experienced pilot stayed with aircraft until the last moment

The major is described as a highly experienced and physically fit pilot, with almost 2,000 hours of flight experience and participation in international operations.

The Gripen was taking part in a high-speed interception exercise when the technical failure occurred. The aircraft had taken off from Kecskemét as part of a pair exercise and had already completed an interception before the problems emerged during the second attempt.

A series of warning messages appeared before the aircraft’s instruments went dark. The pilot then decided to eject. Before doing so, however, he reportedly attempted to direct the malfunctioning aircraft towards the grounds of the Szolnok helicopter brigade, helping to keep it away from populated areas.

The aircraft ultimately crashed within the military base rather than in a residential area.

Pilot reportedly eager to return to flying

After the operation, Ruszin-Szendi visited the injured major in hospital. According to earlier reports, the pilot told the minister that he was already looking forward to getting back into a fighter aircraft. The incident is still being investigated, including the precise cause of the technical failure.

The pilot’s decision-making and experience have been credited with helping prevent a potentially much more serious accident. Despite having to abandon the aircraft, he remained in control of the situation until the final stages and ensured the malfunctioning Gripen was directed towards a safe area.

Before his discharge, Hungarian President András Baka, who also serves as commander-in-chief of the Hungarian Defence Forces, visited the pilot in hospital. The 51-year-old major will now continue his rehabilitation at home. Defence Minister Ruszin-Szendi has wished him a full recovery.

World.title: Was the weather completely different 500 years ago? This is what was recorded in the days before the Battle of Mohács
World.content:
Have you ever wondered what the weather was like before or during major historical events? We now have an idea of the conditions in which the participants of the Battle of Mohács had to fight. Historical records suggest that the weather was particularly wet in the days leading up to the battle 500 years ago.

No official measurements, but historical records remain

HungaroMet told the Hungarian news agency MTI that meteorological measurements in Hungary only date back to 1870. As a result, the weather conditions surrounding the Battle of Mohács can only be reconstructed from historical records. One important source is Antal Réthly’s four-volume work Weather Events and Natural Disasters in Hungary.

Réthly, who was also involved in founding the Hungarian Meteorological Society, spent more than seven decades collecting and critically analysing historical information about weather events and natural disasters. He also sought to document their social and economic consequences.

The volumes present the records in chronological order, while also allowing readers to search for particular weather events – such as lightning, floods and heatwaves – or for specific locations and regions.

The weather records relating to the Battle of Mohács can be found in the first volume, which covers the period from the earliest records up to 1700. At HungaroMet’s request, the four-volume work was digitised by the Library and Information Centre of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (MTA KIK). The volumes are available in the MTA KIK’s digital collection.

The Battle of Mohács Memorial in 2025. Photo: Helló Magyar

Muddy, impassable roads and heavy rain

In his work, Réthly wrote that “mud and roads that were without proper routes were truly a natural disaster for Hungary”, as roads were “completely impassable” in some years, probably on many occasions.

As an example, he noted that Ottoman chroniclers accompanying Sultan Suleiman I had also recorded the significant role played by the deep mud created during periods of particularly heavy rainfall.

“For example, between 14 and 17 August 1526 – 12 days before the disaster at Mohács – the Ottoman army crossed the Drava, but because the roads had been damaged by continuous rainfall, they did not reach Baranyavár until 26 August. It took them ten days to cover the 25–30-kilometre journey,” Réthly wrote.

According to historical records, heavy rainfall was recorded in Mohács in August and September 1526. Rain was reported along the Drava on 22 August, while on the following day it “rained continuously from morning until evening”. On 24 August, records state that “very heavy rain fell both day and night”.

“The Battle of Mohács” painted by Bertalan Székely. Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Have you read this? Hungary’s most bizarre 20 August monument? Devecser unveils a winged penis, UPDATE: Hungary’s ‘winged phallus’ memorial taken down as officials offer strange explanations

An icy shower

Based on Miklós Istvánffy’s History of Hungary, Réthly also recorded a dramatic weather event from 29 August 1526.

According to the account, when King Louis II reached the Csele stream between Mohács and the village of Csele, the stream had swollen due to flooding of the Danube and an “icy shower” that poured down after the battle.

Drawing on the shorter historical works of Mihály Horváth, Réthly also recorded that on the night of 29 August, a heavy downpour gave many Hungarians an opportunity to escape. However, when King Louis II attempted to cross the rain-swollen, marshy Csele stream on horseback, his exhausted horse was unable to climb the steep bank on the opposite side. The horse fell backwards, burying the king beneath it.

On 29 August 1526, the Ottoman army inflicted a decisive defeat on the Hungarian forces at the Battle of Mohács. King Louis II also died while fleeing after the battle.

The defeat had catastrophic consequences for the Kingdom of Hungary. The country was subsequently divided into three parts, ushering in around 150 years of Ottoman rule over much of Hungary.

World.title: PM Magyar hits back at critics of Hungary’s new asset recovery office, his own supporters among others: ‘They are harming the country’
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar has strongly defended the newly established National Office for Asset Recovery and Asset Protection (NVVH), accusing those who seek to undermine or discredit its work of opposing efforts to recover allegedly stolen public assets.

In a video posted on Facebook on Friday, Magyar said the new authority should certainly be criticised and scrutinised, and that its performance should be held to account. However, he argued that anyone who weakens, discredits or obstructs its work for political reasons is deliberately causing harm.

His comments came after the Hungarian Parliament elected Anna Unger as the NVVH’s president and Katalin Tasnádi as deputy president responsible for investigations.

Magyar: The new office must be judged by its results

Addressing supporters of the governing Tisza Party, Magyar said it was “extremely unfair and unjust” to question the commitment of MPs or government members to political change simply because of the parliamentary decision concerning the leadership of the new office.

According to the prime minister, those who genuinely support political change and want an effective asset recovery authority should judge its leadership based on its future actions and results. Magyar also insisted that the selection process had been professional and transparent.

He said he had recently spoken by telephone with Miklós Ligeti, legal director of Transparency International Hungary and one of the candidates considered for the position.

“He confirmed to me that he also considered the procedure constitutional, lawful and fair,” Magyar said.

The prime minister also urged public figures, including former MPs and former government officials, to reconsider their criticism of the authority and its newly appointed leadership.

“Those who try to trip up those responsible for recovering public assets right at the starting line will later find it difficult to explain whose interests they were actually serving,” Magyar said.

If you missed it: PM Magyar announces headquarters of new asset recovery office

‘The biggest Hungarian economic crimes ever seen’

Magyar described Tasnádi as one of Hungary’s best-prepared prosecutors and said her task would be to investigate what he called “the biggest Hungarian economic crimes ever seen” and identify those responsible. The prime minister also said the government wanted to speed up criminal proceedings.

He argued that it was unacceptable for criminal cases to take five to ten years to conclude and said the government would submit every necessary legislative amendment to Parliament to shorten the time required for investigations, prosecutions and court proceedings.

The NVVH is intended to play a central role in one of the Tisza Party’s key political pledges: recovering public assets that the government alleges were improperly taken and ensuring that those responsible face consequences.

NVVH leaders to receive 24-hour police protection

Magyar also highlighted the risks associated with investigating organised economic crime. He said that fighting and investigating the “mafia” was among the most dangerous tasks and confirmed that the leaders of the new authority would receive 24-hour personal protection from the police.

Magyar condemns Fidesz comparison with the ÁVH

The prime minister also sharply criticised the opposition Fidesz party for comparing the NVVH with the ÁVH, Hungary’s communist-era State Protection Authority. Magyar called the comparison “despicable” and said it was a shameful insult to the memory of the ÁVH’s victims and the legacy of the 1956 revolution.

He said he was not surprised that Fidesz was attacking the new authority and its leadership with what he described as low-level political tactics, claiming that the party had “plundered this wonderful country” over the past 16 years.

As a result, he argued, its representatives had something to fear and something to lose from effective asset recovery.

Magyar called on members of the public not to fall for what he described as personal and hurtful provocations. Instead, he urged Hungarians to support those taking on the task of recovering public assets and to defend them against what he called attacks without any factual basis.

‘Now something will happen’

Concluding his video, Magyar wished the new authority’s current and future employees success. “Work bravely, work freely,” he said, adding that he hoped that in a few years no Hungarian would again have to say, as people had so often said in previous decades, that “nothing ever happens in this country”.

“Because now something will happen,” the prime minister concluded.

World.title: Russia tells Hungary’s Péter Magyar to stop ‘hesitating’ over Paks II nuclear project
World.content:
A senior Russian senator has urged Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar to stop wavering over the controversial Paks II nuclear power plant project, warning that energy security and affordable electricity should not become the subject of “political games”.

Elena Perminova, first deputy chair of the International Affairs Committee of Russia’s Federation Council, issued the warning on Friday as tensions continue to grow between the Hungarian government and Russian state nuclear giant Rosatom over the future of Paks II.

“Prime Minister of Hungary Péter Magyar should stop hesitating and take the position of constructive, responsible work,” Perminova told Russian state news agency RIA Novosti. She argued that “security, energy sovereignty and affordable electricity for Hungarian citizens are not a field for political games”.

Have you heard? Russia threatens to cut oil and gas supplies to Hungary after Budapest labels Moscow a security threat

Russia defends Rosatom’s role in Paks II

Perminova also praised Russia’s nuclear industry, echoing President Vladimir Putin’s claim that Russia is the “absolute and undisputed world leader” in the nuclear power plant construction market. She said Russia possessed expertise covering the entire nuclear energy chain, from uranium mining and enrichment to fuel production, reactor design and construction, staff training and waste disposal.

According to the senator, the reliability of Russian nuclear technology has already been demonstrated, while Rosatom continues to build nuclear power plants around the world. Perminova also contrasted Russia’s position with what she described as the West’s energy crisis and dependence on external energy sources.

She claimed Hungary was already benefiting from cheap and reliable energy thanks to former prime minister Viktor Orbán’s pragmatic policies, and accused Magyar’s statements of posing “a direct threat” to Hungary’s own economy.

According to Perminova, continued cooperation with Rosatom on Paks II would serve Hungary’s “vital interests” and contribute to energy stability across Europe.

Budapest and Rosatom clash over the project

The latest Russian criticism follows increasingly sharp disagreements between the Hungarian government and Rosatom over the progress and cost of Paks II. On 13 August, Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev told Russian journalists that construction of the two new reactors had accelerated and that the company was following the timetable agreed with the Hungarian client.

Work on the foundation of the fifth reactor building is reportedly around 80 per cent complete, with more than 18,000 cubic metres of concrete already poured. Rosatom says preparations for the first concrete pour for the sixth unit are also progressing, while equipment for both reactors is being manufactured.

However, Magyar struck a very different tone the following day. Speaking at a press conference about the water-management measures around the existing Paks nuclear plant, the Hungarian prime minister questioned whether Rosatom had actually complied with its contractual commitments.

“If they had complied with the contract, Paks II would already have been operating in 2024,” Magyar said, while claiming that the project could now cost twice as much as originally planned.

He also famously argued that, after spending around HUF 1,000 billion (approx. EUR 2.75 billion), “there are only two large holes” at the site. Magyar has stressed that not all delays can be blamed on Rosatom, but said the Russian company nevertheless bears some responsibility.

Could Rosatom be pushed out of Paks II?

The dispute has raised the possibility that Hungary could seek major changes to the Paks II project — potentially even reducing or ending Rosatom’s role. At the same time, completely abandoning the existing project and starting again from scratch could prove extremely expensive, particularly given the work and equipment already in place.

Rosatom says the fifth reactor’s foundation is progressing, while excavation work for the sixth unit is also underway. Major equipment has already been produced or is being manufactured, including reactor components and a 730-tonne core catcher delivered to the construction site in 2024.

The project also involves companies from several countries beyond Hungary and Russia. French engineering group Alstom is supplying the turbines, while American, Czech, French, Dutch, German, Austrian, Swiss, Slovak and Turkish companies are also involved.

Rosatom currently says around 500 people are working on the project.

World.title: What’s the public’s problem with Unger? PM Magyar hits back at critics of Hungary’s new asset recovery chief
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar has hit back at criticism surrounding Anna Róza Unger, who was elected president of Hungary’s newly established National Asset Protection and Asset Recovery Office (NVVH) by Parliament on Friday.

Magyar responded to the criticism in several Facebook posts following Unger’s election, arguing that the performance of a public official should ultimately be judged by their actions rather than by the opinions of their critics.

“In a functioning and humane country, a leader’s work is judged by their actions, not by the opinions of pundits,” Magyar wrote. He added that choosing the head of a major public institution should not be treated as a popularity contest.

“The selection of the head of a serious institution is not an elimination show and not a vote on popularity,” the prime minister said.

Magyar takes aim at Ákos Hadházy

Magyar also appeared to respond directly to criticism from former MP Ákos Hadházy, who has questioned aspects of the selection process for the new office’s leadership. Hadházy announced that he would submit a public-interest data request to the minister responsible for the Prime Minister’s Office in an effort to obtain information about the evaluation system used in the recruitment process.

In response, Magyar wrote that the “so-called expert” was asking the Prime Minister’s Office for information even though Parliament had conducted the selection process. The prime minister also referred to Hadházy, writing:

“Many people wanted a veterinarian to be appointed to head the NVVH and the Prosecutor General’s Office, and now they object that we did not choose a lawyer.”

Magyar did not name Hadházy directly in the post. However, Hadházy then reacted to this post, writing:

“Dear Prime Minister, anyone who believes the government should not be criticised wants New Fidesz and NER 2.0. And they are working toward that end. I hope that is not what you want. Allow me—as a veterinarian—to oppose this by expressing my opinion. Of course, I will also request the scoring system from Parliament, and I very much hope you will support its release. I am turning to the Prime Minister’s Office because, to my knowledge, that is where these matters were decided.”

If you missed it: BREAKING: Hungary’s new asset recovery chief elected in secret vote

Unger’s lack of legal background questioned

One of the main criticisms of Unger’s appointment is that she is not a lawyer. Magyar addressed the issue at a press conference after Parliament’s vote, arguing that Hungarian law does not require the president of the NVVH to be a lawyer.

He pointed to the FBI as an example, saying that its director is not necessarily a lawyer either.

“What is important, and what it will be, is that the investigative deputy president, the deputy president responsible for prosecutions and the deputy president responsible for appeals should be lawyers and prosecutors,” Magyar said.

The new office is being established with a broader leadership structure, with specialist legal responsibilities assigned to its deputy heads.

Magyar also responds to criticism from within Tisza

The appointment has not been universally welcomed even among supporters of Magyar’s Tisza Party. In a comment beneath one of his posts, the prime minister addressed Tisza supporters who had expressed dissatisfaction with Unger’s election.

“It is perfectly fine to criticise and disagree, but I ask that we do not go below a certain level,” Magyar wrote.

Unger was elected by Parliament on Friday with 137 votes in favour, seven against and one abstention. Katalin Tasnádi was elected as investigative deputy president with 139 votes in favour, six against and one abstention.

The two officials subsequently took their oaths in Parliament. The new asset recovery office is expected to play a central role in the government’s efforts to recover allegedly misused public funds and protect state assets.

World.title: Bucharest Stock Exchange-listed tech company AROBS posts 121% higher net profit in H1
World.content:
AROBS Transilvania Software (BVB: AROBS), one of the largest entrepreneurial technology companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange, recorded consolidated turnover of RON 292 million in the first half of 2026, up 36% compared to H1 2025, EBITDA of RON 40 million, a 29% increase, and net profit of approximately RON 23 million, up 121% compared to the same period of last year.

The first six months of 2026 represented the AROBS group’s best first half of the past three years in terms of turnover, EBITDA, operating profit, and net profit. The positive momentum accelerated in the second quarter, when the group generated turnover of approximately RON 148 million, EBITDA of RON 22 million, and net profit of over RON 15 million, twice the level recorded in Q1 2026 and almost four times higher than in Q2 2025.

“In 2024 and 2025, we increased the scale of the group and added capabilities through the acquisitions we completed. In 2026, our focus is on integrating these capabilities through One AROBS and transforming this structure into an organization that operates as one, both commercially and operationally,” stated Voicu Oprean, founder and CEO of AROBS.

Of the consolidated turnover recorded in H1 2026, RON 242 million, representing almost 83% of the total, was generated by activities classified as organic, while RON 50 million came from companies included in the M&A scope.

At business segment level, Software Services generated turnover of approximately RON 186 million, up 31% compared to H1 2025. Software Products recorded turnover of RON 54 million, 17% above the level reported in the comparable period, while the segment’s gross margin increased from 52% to 54%.

The fastest growth was recorded by Integrated Systems, where turnover advanced by 88% to RON 52 million, mainly as a result of the implementation of projects for the National House of Public Pensions and the Ministry of Health. Furthermore, after the end of the first semester, AROBS Systems signed a contract with the Agency for Payments and Intervention for Agriculture (APIA) with a total value of approximately RON 70 million, excluding VAT, of which approximately 61% is attributable to the company.

In the first half of the year, AROBS achieved 53% of the turnover, 49% of the EBITDA and 65% of the net profit envisaged in the 2026 Consolidated Revenue and Expense Budget, which provides for turnover of RON 552 million, EBITDA of RON 82 million and net profit of RON 35 million. The budget approved in April was prepared based on prudent estimates regarding the contributions of GESS and QUEST, companies acquired by AROBS in November 2025 and January 2026, respectively, and does not include contracts signed after its approval, including the contract concluded by AROBS Systems with APIA in August.

“The results for the first half of the year provide the first financial confirmation of this model. For the second half of the year, our objective is for the increase in turnover to translate to a greater extent into EBITDA. Looking ahead to 2027-2030, the group’s development will be supported by expansion in international markets, the organization of our activities around the verticals in which we have expertise, the development of proprietary products and the integration of AI into the solutions and services we provide,” he added.

World.title: Romanian digital education infrastructure provider Ascendia posts 50% higher net profit in H1
World.content:
Ascendia (BVB: ASC), a Romanian benchmark and provider of critical learning infrastructure, announced its financial results for the first half of 2026. According to the press release, the company recorded the best first half in its history, marking accelerated growth supported by the completion of previous projects, its own product portfolio, and efficient capital management.

The financial performance in H1 2026 was directly supported by the increase in operating revenue. This advance was driven by robust turnover of more than RON 20.6 million, generated mainly by services and sales associated with its own educational software products (CoffeeLMS, LIVRESQ and eJourneys), as well as contracts financed through the PNRR.

At the same time, the company achieved a net profit of RON 8.11 million, up 49.52% compared with the same period in 2025, achieving a solid operating margin of 44.09%. The evolution confirms the efficiency of the integrated business model and the scalable use of in-house products.

“The first half of 2026 was the best first half in the company’s history. After the very good results recorded in H1 2025, we managed to achieve significant growth both in terms of revenue and net profit. We have a solid financial position, with cash of around RON 25.8 million. This flexibility allows us to consider the possibility of early repayment of the ASC27 bonds to reduce financing costs,” said Cosmin Mălureanu, CEO and co-founder of Ascendia.

As of June 30, 2026, equity doubled to RON 37.95 million, representing 71% of total assets of RON 53.45 million. The current liquidity ratio strengthened to 4.56, giving the company the capacity to finance future expansion stages without the pressure of an immediate need for external financing.

World.title: CTP delivers 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehousing in Bucharest
World.content:
Developer and operator of logistics and industrial real estate CTP has delivered nearly 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehouse space to Frigonet Logistics at CTPark Bucharest South, according to a press release published on Friday, August 28.

Frigonet Logistics provides integrated cold chain logistics services, including refrigerated warehousing and handling, national dual-temperature distribution for chilled and frozen goods, picking, and cross-docking. The company selected CTPark Bucharest South for its strategic location and excellent connectivity to Bucharest and key regional hubs, enabling more efficient distribution routes and supporting the continued expansion of its operations.

Frigonet Logistics has signed a long-term lease for its new facility, which it will use to expand its temperature-controlled storage operations for refrigerated and frozen food products, supporting its growing logistics network across Romania.

CTPark Bucharest South is strategically located with direct access to Bucharest’s ring road and major national transport corridors, providing excellent connectivity to the capital, the A0, A1 and A2 motorways, and key destinations across Romania and Southeastern Europe. The park comprises nearly 140,000 sqm of built space across a nearly 37-hectare site.

“Beyond the operational advantages, the location at CTPark Bucharest South provides excellent connectivity to Bucharest and our key regional hubs, helping us optimise distribution routes and improve logistics efficiency. This investment gives us the capacity and flexibility required to support our continued growth and to provide our customers with temperature-controlled transport and logistics services that meet the highest standards,” explained David Stoian, Executive Director of Frigonet Logistics.

The facility incorporates dedicated frozen storage operating at -20°C, a 0-4°C buffer area, a refrigeration plant, and the infrastructure required to safely handle and store temperature- sensitive products while maintaining an uninterrupted cold chain.

“We are pleased to welcome Frigonet Logistics to CTPark Bucharest South and to support the company’s next stage of expansion,” said Cristina Manea, Business Developer at CTP in Romania.

World.title: Mastering the Music Business brings over 100 speakers to Bucharest
World.content:
The 11th edition of the Mastering the Music Business (MMB) conference will take place at Hotel Caro in Bucharest from September 1 to 3. More than 100 speakers from 16 countries will participate in 27 panels, workshops, and discussions on building careers in the music industry.

The lineup includes Romanian artists and industry figures such as Grasu XXL, Nicole Cherry, Marius Moga, AFO, Bean of Subcarpați, and television host Cătălin Măruță, who also manages singer Andra.

They will be joined by professionals representing European festivals, booking agencies, record labels, and music organizations. Speakers include European Music Exporters Exchange president Corinne Sadki, ESNS junior booker Janneke de Boer, SoAlive Music Conference founder Ruth Koleva, Music Glue business development head Marion Sosnowicz, and Future Echoes festival director Peter Åstedt.

For the first time, the conference will host representatives of music export offices from 11 European countries: Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, Switzerland, Belgium, France, Italy, Ukraine, Austria, Greece, and Germany. Discussions will focus on festivals, touring, and the professional networks that could help Romanian artists reach European markets.

The program will cover topics including artificial intelligence in the creative process, independent music economics, ticket fraud, songwriting, artist selection by European bookers, mental health, fan communities, copyright, and crisis management.

AFO and Bean will discuss Subcarpați’s development on the opening day, while Marius Moga will participate in a panel about how brands choose music projects. The final day will feature a conversation with Măruță about managing Andra and a keynote address by Grasu XXL.

The conference will also include three small-group accelerators focusing on music marketing, booking, and music business fundamentals. They are open to ticket holders through separate registration, subject to availability.

Each conference day will be followed by concerts at Club Expirat as part of the MMB Showcase Festival. Twelve acts from Romania and elsewhere in Europe will perform during the three evenings, with admission free, subject to venue capacity.

World.title: Romania’s population drop slowed by migration but still ongoing
World.content:
Romania’s resident population reached 19.041 million people on January 1, 2026, 1,829 fewer than a year earlier, according to provisional data published Friday, August 28, by the National Institute of Statistics.

The decline was largely limited by migration. The number of immigrants exceeded that of emigrants by 102,200, but the difference did not fully offset the natural decrease of 104,100 people.

Overall, the positive international migration balance increased compared with previous years and covered almost the entire difference between the number of deaths and the number of births.

Among people who left Romania, men accounted for 57.9% of the total. They were also the majority among those who came to the country, with a share of 58.6%.

The urban population reached 9.792 million people at the beginning of 2026, up 0.2% from the same period in 2025. The female population stood at 9.744 million people, down 0.1%.

Beyond the decrease in the number of inhabitants, INS data indicate an intensification of demographic aging. People aged at least 65 accounted for 20.5% of the population on January 1, 2026, compared with 20.3% a year earlier. At the same time, the share of children aged 0 to 14 fell from 15.4% to 15.1%.

The demographic aging index therefore rose from 131.3 to 135.9 elderly people for every 100 young people. In other words, at the beginning of 2026, Romania had almost 136 people aged at least 65 for every 100 children under 15. The demographic dependency ratio fell slightly, from 55.6 to 55.2 young and elderly people for every 100 working-age adults.

INS included foreign citizens in the resident population, as well as stateless people, who usually live in Romania for a period of at least 12 months. During the war in Ukraine, the statistics also include Ukrainian citizens benefiting from temporary protection in Romania.

World.title: Tour of Romania brings together 23 cycling teams from 16 countries
World.content:
The 2026 Tour of Romania will bring together approximately 150 cyclists from 23 teams representing 16 countries between September 9 and 13. Italian Olympic champion Elia Viviani will also attend the race as manager of Italy’s national team.

The five-stage competition will cover more than 800 kilometers, beginning in Chișinău, Moldova, and ending with a final circuit in Bucharest. This will be the first edition of the race to start outside Romania.

“The presence of 23 teams from 16 countries confirms the growing interest in the Tour of Romania,” Romanian Cycling Federation president Cătălin Sprinceană said. “We are pleased that the public will be able to see athletes from so many countries at the start.”

The lineup includes ten UCI continental teams, eight club teams, and five national teams. The participating countries are Albania, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Moldova, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Turkey, and the United States.

The national teams of Romania, Italy, Moldova, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina will compete in the race.

Elia Viviani won the Olympic omnium title at Rio 2016 and is a three-time Olympic medalist and three-time track world champion. He has also won stages in all three Grand Tours and claimed the European road race title in 2019. After a 16-year professional career, the Italian cyclist is beginning a new role as manager of his country’s national team.

The participating teams will be officially presented in Chișinău on September 8. The first stage, from Chișinău to Ungheni, will take place the following day.

The race will then continue in Romania with stages from Iași to Piatra Neamț on September 10, Piatra Neamț to Băile Balvanyos on September 11, and Brașov to Ploiești on September 12. The final stage will be held on a circuit in Bucharest on September 13.

The race will be broadcast live by Prima Sport and on the official Tour of Romania and Auchan Romania Facebook pages, while TVR Sport will air daily highlights. Further details can be found here.

World.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge opens registration for Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca events
World.content:
NASA Space Apps Challenge, the world’s largest hackathon, will return to Romania on November 14-15, with simultaneous events in Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca. Registration for the 48-hour international event is open until November 13.

Under the theme The Next Frontier!, participants will form teams of up to six members and use NASA’s open data to develop solutions to challenges related to Earth and space exploration. The challenges will be announced on September 17.

The competition is open to programmers, scientists, engineers, designers, students, storytelling specialists, and other people interested in technology and innovation, regardless of their age, experience, or professional background.

“Romania has people with ideas and skills who can compete at the highest international level, and this competition is an extraordinary opportunity to bring them together and connect them to one of the most innovative global communities,” said Diana Iosu, founder of DiFine PR and organizer of the Bucharest edition.

The Bucharest event will be held at the Romanian-American University, while the Cluj-Napoca competition will take place at ClujHUB. Registration for Bucharest is available here, and for Cluj here.

Two winning teams will be selected from each city to advance to the global competition and compete against thousands of teams worldwide. Global winners will be invited to visit a NASA center or facility, attend an event celebrating their projects, and meet representatives of the US space agency.

Participants will also receive free access to the Google AI Professional Certificate course offered through Coursera.

People under 18 may participate only with the consent of a parent or legal guardian, who must accompany them throughout the event.

The 2025 edition attracted 200 registrations in Romania. Winning projects included an algorithm assessing the environmental effects of business decisions, a visual platform for learning about physics and astrophysics, and an AI solution that converted air-quality data into real-time information.

Launched globally in 2012, the NASA Space Apps Challenge has brought together more than 487,000 participants from 190 countries and territories. The Romanian editions are organized by ROTSA and DiFine PR.

World.title: IKEA opens first Plan and Order Point in Iași
World.content:
IKEA will open its first Plan and Order Point in Iași on Monday, August 31. Located in Egros Shopping Center, the studio will be the retailer’s sixth such facility in Romania.

The location will offer personalized planning services for kitchens, wardrobes, and storage solutions. Customers will be able to work individually with IKEA specialists to select configurations, products, and finishes suited to their homes and budgets, the company said.

The studio will feature three kitchen layouts, three wardrobe solutions, two planning desks, and more than 1,400 IKEA products. Around 50 everyday products will also be available to purchase directly.

Customers can collect their orders free of charge from the location, arrange home delivery, or use another IKEA pick-up point. Furniture assembly services will also be available.

The new facility replaces IKEA’s existing pick-up point at Egros Shopping Center, with collection services integrated into the expanded format.
